works.title: The Critique of Pure Reason
works.author: Immanuel Kant
works.edition: J. M. D. Meiklejohn translation · Gutenberg eText #4280
works.description: What can we know—and what gives a claim the right to call itself knowledge?

items.text: Problem: determine how cognition can contain necessity and strict universality if cognition begins temporally with experience.

passages.note: Experience is the temporal beginning; necessity marks non-empirical cognition.
Experience is the temporal beginning; necessity marks non-empirical cognition.

grounding.note: Experience is the temporal beginning; necessity marks non-empirical cognition.

items.text: Reframing: distinguish the temporal occasion of knowledge from the source of its validity.

passages.note: Temporal beginning is distinguished from absolute independence of experience.
Temporal beginning is distinguished from absolute independence of experience.

grounding.note: Temporal beginning is distinguished from absolute independence of experience.

items.text: Key operation: isolate pure a priori cognition by tests unavailable to experience.

passages.note: Necessity and strict universality are stated as tests.
Necessity and strict universality are stated as tests.

grounding.note: Necessity and strict universality are stated as tests.

items.text: Central difficulty: explain synthetic a priori judgments, where predicates extend concepts necessarily without empirical support.

passages.note: Synthetic a priori synthesis lacks experiential aid and requires a ground.

grounding.note: Synthetic a priori synthesis lacks experiential aid and requires a ground.

items.text: Strategic pivot: metaphysics depends entirely on the possibility, scope, and limits of synthetic a priori cognition.

passages.note: Metaphysics depends on resolving synthetic a priori possibility.
Metaphysics depends on resolving synthetic a priori possibility.

grounding.note: Metaphysics depends on resolving synthetic a priori possibility.

items.text: Argument type: transcendental-diagnostic and architectonic; it diagnoses dogmatic failure and constructs the preconditions for legitimate metaphysics.

passages.note: Dogmatic procedure is diagnosed; critique is framed as propedeutic.
Dogmatic procedure is diagnosed; critique is framed as propedeutic.

grounding.note: Dogmatic procedure is diagnosed; critique is framed as propedeutic.

items.text: Movement: experience → a priori distinction → necessity/universality tests → analytic/synthetic distinction → universal problem → critique as prior tribunal of reason.

passages.note: The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.
The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.
The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.
The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.
The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.

grounding.note: The cited passages supply the stated sequential movement.

items.text: All human knowledge begins in time with experience.

passages.note: Knowledge begins with experience in time.

grounding.note: Knowledge begins with experience in time.

items.text: Not all human knowledge must arise from experience.

passages.note: Beginning with experience does not entail arising from it.

grounding.note: Beginning with experience does not entail arising from it.

items.text: Empirical cognition is a compound of received sensible impressions and contributions supplied by the faculty of cognition.

passages.note: Empirical knowledge is described as a compound of impressions and contribution.

grounding.note: Empirical knowledge is described as a compound of impressions and contribution.

items.text: A priori knowledge is knowledge absolutely independent of all experience.

passages.note: A priori knowledge is absolutely independent of all experience.

grounding.note: A priori knowledge is absolutely independent of all experience.

items.text: Pure a priori knowledge contains no empirical element.

passages.note: Pure a priori knowledge has no mixed empirical element.

grounding.note: Pure a priori knowledge has no mixed empirical element.

items.text: Necessity is an infallible mark of a priori cognition.

passages.note: Necessity is given as a criterion of a priori cognition.

grounding.note: Necessity is given as a criterion of a priori cognition.

items.text: Strict universality is an infallible mark of a priori cognition.

passages.note: Strict universality is given as a criterion of a priori cognition.

grounding.note: Strict universality is given as a criterion of a priori cognition.

items.text: Experience yields only comparative universality, never strict universality or necessity.

passages.note: Experience yields comparative, not strict, universality.

grounding.note: Experience yields comparative, not strict, universality.

items.text: Human cognition contains judgments and concepts that exhibit necessity and strict universality.

passages.note: Necessary and strictly universal a priori judgments are affirmed.

grounding.note: Necessary and strictly universal a priori judgments are affirmed.

items.text: Certain a priori cognitions are conditions of the possibility of experience itself.

passages.note: A priori principles are called indispensable bases of experience.

grounding.note: A priori principles are called indispensable bases of experience.

items.text: Reason naturally generates questions that exceed all possible experience.

passages.note: Reason is said unceasingly to progress toward non-empirical questions.

grounding.note: Reason is said unceasingly to progress toward non-empirical questions.

items.text: Dogmatic metaphysics attempts supersensible cognition without first examining reason’s capacity.

passages.note: Metaphysics begins dogmatically without prior capacity examination.

grounding.note: Metaphysics begins dogmatically without prior capacity examination.

items.text: Judgments are either analytic, where the predicate is contained in the subject-concept, or synthetic, where the predicate adds something not contained in it.

passages.note: Analytic containment and synthetic addition are explicitly defined.

grounding.note: Analytic containment and synthetic addition are explicitly defined.

items.text: Analytic judgments clarify concepts but do not extend cognition.

passages.note: Analytic judgments are explicative rather than augmentative.

grounding.note: Analytic judgments are explicative rather than augmentative.

items.text: Synthetic judgments extend cognition by connecting a predicate not contained in the subject-concept.

passages.note: Synthetic judgments add a predicate not contained in the concept.

grounding.note: Synthetic judgments add a predicate not contained in the concept.

items.text: Synthetic a priori judgments require a non-empirical ground for necessary conceptual synthesis.

passages.note: Synthetic a priori judgment requires a ground beyond experience.

grounding.note: Synthetic a priori judgment requires a ground beyond experience.

items.text: Mathematics, pure natural science, and metaphysics each depend on synthetic a priori judgments.

passages.note: Mathematics, physics, and metaphysics are each assigned synthetic a priori principles.
Mathematics, physics, and metaphysics are each assigned synthetic a priori principles.

grounding.note: Mathematics, physics, and metaphysics are each assigned synthetic a priori principles.

items.text: The universal problem of pure reason is how synthetic a priori judgments are possible.

passages.note: The universal problem is explicitly formulated.

grounding.note: The universal problem is explicitly formulated.

items.text: The existence or downfall of metaphysics as science depends on solving the problem of synthetic a priori cognition.

passages.note: Metaphysics' existence or downfall depends on the problem's solution.

grounding.note: Metaphysics' existence or downfall depends on the problem's solution.

items.text: Critique of pure reason must determine the sources, validity, extent, and limits of a priori cognition.

passages.note: Critique concerns the sources and limits of pure reason.

grounding.note: Critique concerns the sources and limits of pure reason.

items.text: Critique is not an enlargement of speculative reason but its purification, correction, and limitation.

passages.note: Critique is negative, purifying reason rather than enlarging it.

grounding.note: Critique is negative, purifying reason rather than enlarging it.

items.text: Transcendental inquiry concerns cognition of objects insofar as that cognition is possible a priori, not objects simply as objects.

passages.note: Transcendental inquiry concerns cognition's a priori mode, not objects alone.

grounding.note: Transcendental inquiry concerns cognition's a priori mode, not objects alone.

items.text: Human knowledge has two basic sources: sensibility gives objects; understanding thinks objects.

passages.note: Sense gives objects; understanding thinks them.

grounding.note: Sense gives objects; understanding thinks them.

items.text: Conditions under which objects are given precede conditions under which objects are thought.

passages.note: Conditions of givenness precede conditions of thought.

grounding.note: Conditions of givenness precede conditions of thought.

items.text: A priori does not mean independent merely of this or that experience.

passages.note: A priori is denied to mean independence from only particular experiences.

grounding.note: A priori is denied to mean independence from only particular experiences.

items.text: Pure a priori cognition is not cognition mixed with empirical concepts.

passages.note: Pure a priori knowledge excludes every empirical element.

grounding.note: Pure a priori knowledge excludes every empirical element.

items.text: Experience is not a source of necessity.

passages.note: Experience cannot establish necessity.

grounding.note: Experience cannot establish necessity.

items.text: Experience is not a source of strict universality.

passages.note: Experience cannot establish strict universality.

grounding.note: Experience cannot establish strict universality.

items.text: Induction is not strict universality but arbitrary extension from observed cases.

passages.note: Empirical universality is called arbitrary extension from observed cases.

grounding.note: Empirical universality is called arbitrary extension from observed cases.

items.text: Causality is not reducible to repeated succession, association, or subjective habit.

passages.note: Humean association and habit would remove causal necessity.

grounding.note: Humean association and habit would remove causal necessity.

items.text: The certainty of experience cannot rest on rules that are themselves merely empirical and contingent.

passages.note: Experience cannot gain certainty from merely empirical rules.

grounding.note: Experience cannot gain certainty from merely empirical rules.

items.text: Mathematics is not analytic merely because its demonstrations use the principle of contradiction.

passages.note: Mathematics is denied to be analytic despite contradiction-based demonstrations.
Mathematics is denied to be analytic despite contradiction-based demonstrations.

grounding.note: Mathematics is denied to be analytic despite contradiction-based demonstrations.

items.text: Analytic clarification is not metaphysical extension.

passages.note: Analysis is preparation, not metaphysics' synthetic extension.

grounding.note: Analysis is preparation, not metaphysics' synthetic extension.

items.text: Dogmatic metaphysics is not a legitimate science.

passages.note: Dogmatic attempts to establish metaphysical science are treated as non-existent.

grounding.note: Dogmatic attempts to establish metaphysical science are treated as non-existent.

items.text: Supersensible speculation is not justified by freedom from empirical contradiction.

passages.note: Freedom from experiential opposition is not treated as progress or warrant.

grounding.note: Freedom from experiential opposition is not treated as progress or warrant.

items.text: The absence of experiential resistance is not evidence of cognitive validity.

passages.note: Lack of resistance beyond experience enables fictions rather than validity.

grounding.note: Lack of resistance beyond experience enables fictions rather than validity.

items.text: The critique is not a critique of books or historical systems.

passages.note: The object is explicitly not a critique of books and systems.

grounding.note: The object is explicitly not a critique of books and systems.

items.text: The critique is not a doctrine or completed organon of pure reason.

passages.note: Critique is distinguished from doctrine and a completed organon.

grounding.note: Critique is distinguished from doctrine and a completed organon.

items.text: Transcendental philosophy is not empirical psychology.

passages.note: Transcendental philosophy is delimited to pure speculative cognition.

grounding.note: Transcendental philosophy is delimited to pure speculative cognition.

items.text: Transcendental philosophy is not practical philosophy or morality insofar as motives involve feeling.

passages.note: Practical motives belong to feeling and empirical sources.

grounding.note: Practical motives belong to feeling and empirical sources.

items.text: The present critique is not the full system of transcendental philosophy.

passages.note: Critique is the idea and plan, not the complete system.
Critique is the idea and plan, not the complete system.

grounding.note: Critique is the idea and plan, not the complete system.

items.text: Knowledge beyond experience cannot be licensed by mere conceptual analysis.

passages.note: Conceptual analysis cannot account for synthetic a priori extension.
Conceptual analysis cannot account for synthetic a priori extension.

grounding.note: Conceptual analysis cannot account for synthetic a priori extension.

items.text: A temporal dependence on experience is compatible with a non-empirical source of validity.

passages.note: Temporal beginning is paired with absolute independence of validity-source.
Temporal beginning is paired with absolute independence of validity-source.

grounding.note: Temporal beginning is paired with absolute independence of validity-source.

items.text: The a priori must be isolated by validity-criteria rather than by psychological origin alone.

passages.note: Initial psychological indistinguishability gives way to validity criteria.
Initial psychological indistinguishability gives way to validity criteria.

grounding.note: Initial psychological indistinguishability gives way to validity criteria.

items.text: Necessity and strict universality expose a cognitive source distinct from experience.

passages.note: Necessity and strict universality indicate a peculiar a priori source.

grounding.note: Necessity and strict universality indicate a peculiar a priori source.

items.text: Pure a priori cognition is established not merely by examples but by its role as condition of experience.

passages.note: A priori principles are supported as conditions of possible experience.

grounding.note: A priori principles are supported as conditions of possible experience.

items.text: If causal connection were empirical habit, its necessity would disappear.

passages.note: Deriving causality from habit would make its necessity merely subjective.

grounding.note: Deriving causality from habit would make its necessity merely subjective.

items.text: Metaphysics is unavoidable as a natural disposition but invalid as dogmatic science.

passages.note: Metaphysics persists naturally while dogmatic systems are rejected.
Metaphysics persists naturally while dogmatic systems are rejected.

grounding.note: Metaphysics persists naturally while dogmatic systems are rejected.

items.text: The analytic/synthetic distinction is required because not all a priori cognition is merely explicative.

passages.note: The distinction separates explicative analysis from augmentative synthesis.
The distinction separates explicative analysis from augmentative synthesis.

grounding.note: The distinction separates explicative analysis from augmentative synthesis.

items.text: Synthetic a priori cognition is the decisive site where extension, necessity, and non-empirical validity intersect.

passages.note: The passage joins extension, necessity, and non-empirical synthesis.

grounding.note: The passage joins extension, necessity, and non-empirical synthesis.

items.text: Mathematics cannot serve as proof of unlimited speculative reason because its a priori synthesis depends on intuition.

passages.note: Mathematical synthesis requires intuition and cannot license unlimited extension.
Mathematical synthesis requires intuition and cannot license unlimited extension.

grounding.note: Mathematical synthesis requires intuition and cannot license unlimited extension.

items.text: Pure natural science is possible only if nature is subject to a priori principles not derived from empirical observation.

passages.note: Pure physics contains necessary synthetic a priori principles.

grounding.note: Pure physics contains necessary synthetic a priori principles.

items.text: Metaphysics as science requires prior critique because its aim is synthetic extension beyond experience.

passages.note: Metaphysical synthetic extension beyond experience requires prior decision on reason's capacity.
Metaphysical synthetic extension beyond experience requires prior decision on reason's capacity.

grounding.note: Metaphysical synthetic extension beyond experience requires prior decision on reason's capacity.

items.text: The critique must precede any organon of pure reason because the possibility of extension remains undetermined.

passages.note: An organon is premature while extension remains doubtful.

grounding.note: An organon is premature while extension remains doubtful.

items.text: Transcendental critique is negative in speculative use because it secures validity by limiting illegitimate extension.

passages.note: Speculative critique is negative by purifying and limiting reason.

grounding.note: Speculative critique is negative by purifying and limiting reason.

items.text: The doctrine of sensibility must precede the doctrine of understanding because givenness precedes thought.

passages.note: Conditions of sense precede conditions under which objects are thought.

grounding.note: Conditions of sense precede conditions under which objects are thought.

items.text: The system relocates the origin of necessity from objects-as-given to the subject’s a priori cognitive conditions.

passages.note: Necessity is traced to a peculiar a priori cognitive faculty.
Necessity is traced to a peculiar a priori cognitive faculty.

grounding.note: Necessity is traced to a peculiar a priori cognitive faculty.

items.text: Experience becomes neither the producer of all cognition nor its passive content, but the field made possible by prior forms and rules.

passages.note: Experience is occasioned by sense and conditioned by a priori principles.
Experience is occasioned by sense and conditioned by a priori principles.
Experience is occasioned by sense and conditioned by a priori principles.

grounding.note: Experience is occasioned by sense and conditioned by a priori principles.

items.text: Metaphysics is preserved only by being suspended: its claims must be halted until the faculty that produces them is judged.

passages.note: Natural metaphysics persists while dogmatic claims are suspended for critique.
Natural metaphysics persists while dogmatic claims are suspended for critique.
Natural metaphysics persists while dogmatic claims are suspended for critique.

grounding.note: Natural metaphysics persists while dogmatic claims are suspended for critique.

items.text: Critique converts reason from a speculative builder into a self-limiting tribunal.

passages.note: Critique makes reason judge its sources, limits, and worth.
Critique makes reason judge its sources, limits, and worth.

grounding.note: Critique makes reason judge its sources, limits, and worth.

items.text: The analytic/synthetic distinction transforms the problem of metaphysics from “what concepts contain” into “how necessary augmentation is possible.”

passages.note: The distinction redirects inquiry toward possible necessary synthesis.
The distinction redirects inquiry toward possible necessary synthesis.
The distinction redirects inquiry toward possible necessary synthesis.

grounding.note: The distinction redirects inquiry toward possible necessary synthesis.

items.text: The legitimacy of science depends less on objects than on the lawful mode by which objects can be given and thought.

passages.note: Validity is investigated through a priori cognition and conditions of givenness/thought.
Validity is investigated through a priori cognition and conditions of givenness/thought.

grounding.note: Validity is investigated through a priori cognition and conditions of givenness/thought.

items.text: Hume’s skeptical restriction is overcome only if the problem of causality is generalized into the universal structure of synthetic a priori cognition.

passages.note: Hume's causal problem is explicitly subsumed under the universal problem.

grounding.note: Hume's causal problem is explicitly subsumed under the universal problem.

items.text: Dogmatism and skepticism are paired failures: dogmatism extends without critique; skepticism denies without grasping the universal conditions of extension.

passages.note: Dogmatic extension leads to groundless assertion and skepticism.
Dogmatic extension leads to groundless assertion and skepticism.

grounding.note: Dogmatic extension leads to groundless assertion and skepticism.

items.text: The critique’s negative function generates a positive architectonic possibility: a future system of pure reason can be planned only after limitation.

passages.note: Negative critique prepares a future organon, canon, and system.
Negative critique prepares a future organon, canon, and system.

grounding.note: Negative critique prepares a future organon, canon, and system.

items.text: It must not be true that all cognitive validity is empirical in origin.

passages.note: Not all cognition arises from experience; a priori validity is marked separately.
Not all cognition arises from experience; a priori validity is marked separately.

grounding.note: Not all cognition arises from experience; a priori validity is marked separately.

items.text: It must not be true that necessity is only subjective compulsion produced by habit.

passages.note: Habit-based causality would eliminate objective necessity.

grounding.note: Habit-based causality would eliminate objective necessity.

items.text: It must not be true that concepts alone can ground all a priori extension.

passages.note: Synthetic extension exceeds concepts and requires intuition or another ground.
Synthetic extension exceeds concepts and requires intuition or another ground.

grounding.note: Synthetic extension exceeds concepts and requires intuition or another ground.

items.text: It must not be true that reason’s natural tendency toward the supersensible guarantees its legitimacy.

passages.note: Natural supersensible questions require a critical decision on reason's ability.
Natural supersensible questions require a critical decision on reason's ability.

grounding.note: Natural supersensible questions require a critical decision on reason's ability.

items.text: It must not be true that the absence of experiential refutation is sufficient warrant for speculative cognition.

passages.note: Absence of experiential opposition permits fictions rather than warrant.

grounding.note: Absence of experiential opposition permits fictions rather than warrant.

items.text: It must not be true that metaphysics can be evaluated by its historical systems rather than by the faculty that generates them.

passages.note: The required touchstone concerns reason's faculty, not systems or books.

grounding.note: The required touchstone concerns reason's faculty, not systems or books.

items.text: It must not be true that critique requires exhaustive knowledge of external objects; otherwise the proposed science would be impossible.

passages.note: The inquiry concerns the mind within rather than inexhaustible external objects.

grounding.note: The inquiry concerns the mind within rather than inexhaustible external objects.

items.text: It must not be true that the mind’s a priori powers are indefinitely complex or unsurveyable.

passages.note: The a priori faculty is presented as surveyable through radical conceptions.
The a priori faculty is presented as surveyable through radical conceptions.

grounding.note: The a priori faculty is presented as surveyable through radical conceptions.

items.text: It must not be true that practical motives can be included in transcendental philosophy without contaminating its purity.

passages.note: Practical motives introduce feeling and empirical content.

grounding.note: Practical motives introduce feeling and empirical content.

items.text: The forbidden possibility is that reason’s highest objects are intrinsically inaccessible yet structurally unavoidable.

passages.note: Supersensible problems are unavoidable while their knowability remains undecided.
Supersensible problems are unavoidable while their knowability remains undecided.
Supersensible problems are unavoidable while their knowability remains undecided.

grounding.note: Supersensible problems are unavoidable while their knowability remains undecided.

items.text: The discourse is organized around the absence of a given object corresponding to metaphysical ideas.

passages.note: Supersensible conceptions lack corresponding objects in experience.

grounding.note: Supersensible conceptions lack corresponding objects in experience.

items.text: The argument depends on excluding a standpoint outside reason from which reason could be judged.

passages.note: The critical object is sought wholly within the mind's a priori cognition.

grounding.note: The critical object is sought wholly within the mind's a priori cognition.

items.text: The critique circles the impossibility of using experience to validate what makes experience possible.

passages.note: Experience depends on a priori principles that experience cannot supply.
Experience depends on a priori principles that experience cannot supply.

grounding.note: Experience depends on a priori principles that experience cannot supply.

items.text: The system silently forecloses any metaphysics that does not pass through the self-limitation of cognition.

passages.note: Speculative extension requires critique and determination of limits.
Speculative extension requires critique and determination of limits.

grounding.note: Speculative extension requires critique and determination of limits.

items.text: The deepest negation is that thought may not legitimately coincide with being beyond the conditions of possible experience.

passages.note: Supersensible claims lack experiential objects and cognition is delimited by possible a priori modes.
Supersensible claims lack experiential objects and cognition is delimited by possible a priori modes.

grounding.note: Supersensible claims lack experiential objects and cognition is delimited by possible a priori modes.

items.text: Temporal Awakening: objects affect sensibility → cognition begins empirically.

passages.note: Objects affect sense and awaken cognition.

grounding.note: Objects affect sense and awaken cognition.

items.text: Source Separation: empirical occasion ≠ total source of cognition → a priori contribution becomes thinkable.

passages.note: Sensuous impressions are occasion, not the total source.

grounding.note: Sensuous impressions are occasion, not the total source.

items.text: Criterion Extraction: necessity + strict universality → non-empirical validity-source.

passages.note: Necessity and strict universality indicate an a priori source.

grounding.note: Necessity and strict universality indicate an a priori source.

items.text: Possession Claim: mathematics, causality, substance, space → evidence of operative a priori cognition.

passages.note: Mathematics, causality, space, and substance exemplify a priori cognition.
Mathematics, causality, space, and substance exemplify a priori cognition.

grounding.note: Mathematics, causality, space, and substance exemplify a priori cognition.

items.text: Danger Zone: reason exceeds possible experience → metaphysics arises as natural but dogmatic tendency.

passages.note: Reason exceeds experience and metaphysics arises naturally.
Reason exceeds experience and metaphysics arises naturally.

grounding.note: Reason exceeds experience and metaphysics arises naturally.

items.text: Failure Diagnosis: dogmatic extension without prior capacity-test → contradiction and skepticism.

passages.note: Dogmatic capacity-free extension culminates in contradiction and skepticism.
Dogmatic capacity-free extension culminates in contradiction and skepticism.

grounding.note: Dogmatic capacity-free extension culminates in contradiction and skepticism.

items.text: Judgment Bifurcation: analytic clarification vs synthetic augmentation → extension-problem isolated.

passages.note: Analytic explication is distinguished from synthetic augmentation.

grounding.note: Analytic explication is distinguished from synthetic augmentation.

items.text: Core Problem Formation: necessary augmentation without experience → “How are synthetic a priori judgments possible?”

passages.note: The core question is explicitly formulated.

grounding.note: The core question is explicitly formulated.

items.text: Science-Triage: mathematics and pure physics exist → ask how possible; metaphysics disputed → ask whether and how possible.

passages.note: Existing mathematics and physics are asked how; metaphysics whether and how.

grounding.note: Existing mathematics and physics are asked how; metaphysics whether and how.

items.text: Critical Turn: examine reason itself, not objects or systems → determine sources, scope, and limits.

passages.note: Critique investigates reason's faculty rather than objects or systems.
Critique investigates reason's faculty rather than objects or systems.

grounding.note: Critique investigates reason's faculty rather than objects or systems.

items.text: Architectonic Restriction: critique ≠ doctrine; critique = propedeutic/touchstone/canon for future system.

passages.note: Critique is propedeutic and a touchstone for possible organon or canon.
Critique is propedeutic and a touchstone for possible organon or canon.

grounding.note: Critique is propedeutic and a touchstone for possible organon or canon.

items.text: Elemental Ordering: sensibility gives before understanding thinks → transcendental aesthetics must precede transcendental logic.

passages.note: Sense gives before understanding thinks; doctrine of sense comes first.

grounding.note: Sense gives before understanding thinks; doctrine of sense comes first.

items.text: Experience begins cognition → cognition may contain non-empirical contribution → a priori isolated.

passages.note: Experience begins cognition, but a priori contribution is isolated.
Experience begins cognition, but a priori contribution is isolated.

grounding.note: Experience begins cognition, but a priori contribution is isolated.

items.text: A priori isolated → necessity and strict universality become tests → empirical derivation excluded.

passages.note: The a priori tests exclude empirical derivation.
The a priori tests exclude empirical derivation.

grounding.note: The a priori tests exclude empirical derivation.

items.text: A priori possession established → reason’s supersensible tendency diagnosed → dogmatic metaphysics problematized.

passages.note: A priori possession precedes diagnosis of supersensible reason.
A priori possession precedes diagnosis of supersensible reason.

grounding.note: A priori possession precedes diagnosis of supersensible reason.

items.text: Dogmatic failure diagnosed → analytic/synthetic distinction introduced → real extension located in synthesis.

passages.note: Analytic/synthetic distinction follows the diagnosis of speculative overreach.
Analytic/synthetic distinction follows the diagnosis of speculative overreach.

grounding.note: Analytic/synthetic distinction follows the diagnosis of speculative overreach.

items.text: Synthetic a priori judgments identified in mathematics, physics, metaphysics → universal problem of pure reason formulated.

passages.note: The sciences' synthetic a priori principles yield the universal problem.
The sciences' synthetic a priori principles yield the universal problem.
The sciences' synthetic a priori principles yield the universal problem.

grounding.note: The sciences' synthetic a priori principles yield the universal problem.

items.text: Universal problem formulated → metaphysics made dependent on critique → critique assigned negative-propaedeutic function.

passages.note: The universal problem makes critique a prerequisite and propedeutic.
The universal problem makes critique a prerequisite and propedeutic.

grounding.note: The universal problem makes critique a prerequisite and propedeutic.

items.text: Critique defined → transcendental philosophy delimited → science divided by sources of cognition.

passages.note: Critique and transcendental philosophy are delimited by pure sources.
Critique and transcendental philosophy are delimited by pure sources.

grounding.note: Critique and transcendental philosophy are delimited by pure sources.

items.text: Sensibility gives objects → understanding thinks objects → doctrine of sense must come first.

passages.note: Sense gives objects, understanding thinks, and sense comes first.

grounding.note: Sense gives objects, understanding thinks, and sense comes first.

items.text: Experience is remapped from origin of all knowledge to trigger and field of synthesis.

passages.note: Experience occasions cognition and functions as a synthesis of intuitions.
Experience occasions cognition and functions as a synthesis of intuitions.

grounding.note: Experience occasions cognition and functions as a synthesis of intuitions.

items.text: A priori cognition is reclassified by validity-markers rather than by chronological priority.

passages.note: A priori is defined by absolute independence and identified by markers.
A priori is defined by absolute independence and identified by markers.

grounding.note: A priori is defined by absolute independence and identified by markers.

items.text: Necessity and universality become diagnostic instruments for detecting non-empirical cognition.

passages.note: Necessity and universality are explicitly diagnostic tests.

grounding.note: Necessity and universality are explicitly diagnostic tests.

items.text: Metaphysics is reclassified from failed doctrine to unavoidable disposition requiring critique.

passages.note: Metaphysics is natural and indestructible but dogmatic systems are discredited.
Metaphysics is natural and indestructible but dogmatic systems are discredited.

grounding.note: Metaphysics is natural and indestructible but dogmatic systems are discredited.

items.text: Humean skepticism is displaced by a broader problem that includes mathematics and pure physics.

passages.note: Hume's causal restriction is broadened to mathematics and pure philosophy.

grounding.note: Hume's causal restriction is broadened to mathematics and pure philosophy.

items.text: Mathematics is reclassified from analytic demonstration to synthetic construction through intuition.

passages.note: Mathematics is synthetic and depends on intuition.
Mathematics is synthetic and depends on intuition.

grounding.note: Mathematics is synthetic and depends on intuition.

items.text: Conceptual analysis is demoted from knowledge-extension to preparatory clarification.

passages.note: Analysis clarifies; synthetic judgment supplies genuine extension.
Analysis clarifies; synthetic judgment supplies genuine extension.

grounding.note: Analysis clarifies; synthetic judgment supplies genuine extension.

items.text: The object of philosophy shifts from things beyond experience to the faculty that claims to know them.

passages.note: Inquiry shifts to the faculty and mode of cognition.
Inquiry shifts to the faculty and mode of cognition.

grounding.note: Inquiry shifts to the faculty and mode of cognition.

items.text: Limitation becomes productive: setting bounds becomes the condition for any future system.

passages.note: Limits and correction are presented as preparation for future system.
Limits and correction are presented as preparation for future system.

grounding.note: Limits and correction are presented as preparation for future system.

items.text: The science of reason is made finite because its object is not infinite nature but reason’s own a priori faculty.

passages.note: Reason's own a priori faculty is finite and surveyable unlike external nature.
Reason's own a priori faculty is finite and surveyable unlike external nature.

grounding.note: Reason's own a priori faculty is finite and surveyable unlike external nature.

items.text: Practical philosophy is excluded from transcendental philosophy by the empirical contamination of feeling and motive.

items.text: Failure: without intuition there is no subsumption, no object-determination, no synthetic principle.

passages.note: Without schema there is no subsumption, determination, or synthetic principle.

grounding.note: Without schema there is no subsumption, determination, or synthetic principle.

items.text: Residue: thought can still represent an indeterminate object in general by abstraction from sensibility.

passages.note: Categories still think an object in general after abstraction from intuition.

grounding.note: Categories still think an object in general after abstraction from intuition.

items.text: Reclassification: this residue is noumenon only negatively, as limit-concept.

passages.note: This problematic residue is noumenon only as a negative limit.

grounding.note: This problematic residue is noumenon only as a negative limit.

items.text: Prohibition: positive noumenon would require intellectual intuition, which human cognition lacks.

passages.note: Positive noumenon requires intellectual intuition absent from us.

grounding.note: Positive noumenon requires intellectual intuition absent from us.

items.text: Diagnostic extension: metaphysical systems arise when logical comparison is substituted for transcendental reflection.

passages.note: Neglected transcendental reflection produces false synthetic systems.
Neglected transcendental reflection produces false synthetic systems.

grounding.note: Neglected transcendental reflection produces false synthetic systems.

items.text: Amphiboly mechanism: representation’s faculty-source is ignored → phenomena treated as noumena → logical relations projected as ontological relations.

passages.note: Leibniz ignores sensibility and treats phenomena as intelligibilia.

grounding.note: Leibniz ignores sensibility and treats phenomena as intelligibilia.

items.text: Corrective mechanism: assign transcendental place → restrict concepts to proper faculty-use → dissolve false synthetic metaphysics.

passages.note: Transcendental topic assigns proper faculty-place and blocks false principles.
Transcendental topic assigns proper faculty-place and blocks false principles.

grounding.note: Transcendental topic assigns proper faculty-place and blocks false principles.

items.text: Terminal schema: A priori form → possible experience → legitimate objectivity / abstraction from sensibility → empty thought → limitative noumenon.

passages.note: Possible experience grounds objectivity; abstraction leaves limitative emptiness.
Possible experience grounds objectivity; abstraction leaves limitative emptiness.

grounding.note: Possible experience grounds objectivity; abstraction leaves limitative emptiness.

items.text: Survey of understanding’s territory → need to determine its boundaries → empirical use declared sole legitimate use.

passages.note: Territory is surveyed, bounds sought, and empirical use made sole admissible.
Territory is surveyed, bounds sought, and empirical use made sole admissible.

grounding.note: Territory is surveyed, bounds sought, and empirical use made sole admissible.

items.text: Concept requires object → object requires intuition → human intuition is sensuous → categories require sensibility.

passages.note: Concepts require intuitions; ours are sensuous; categories thus require sensibility.
Concepts require intuitions; ours are sensuous; categories thus require sensibility.

grounding.note: Concepts require intuitions; ours are sensuous; categories thus require sensibility.

items.text: Categories without schemata → logical forms only → no synthetic a priori principles beyond possible experience.

passages.note: Without schema, categories yield no transcendental synthetic principle.

grounding.note: Without schema, categories yield no transcendental synthetic principle.

items.text: Appearance implies contrast with thing-in-itself → contrast generates noumenon → noumenon splits into negative and positive senses.

passages.note: Appearance's contrast with thing in itself yields negative and positive noumenon.

grounding.note: Appearance's contrast with thing in itself yields negative and positive noumenon.

items.text: Positive noumenon requires intellectual intuition → intellectual intuition absent → positive noumenology void.

passages.note: The required intellectual intuition is absent, voiding positive category-use.

grounding.note: The required intellectual intuition is absent, voiding positive category-use.

items.text: Negative noumenon remains necessary → limits sensibility → does not enlarge understanding.

passages.note: Negative noumenon limits sensibility without extending cognition.
Negative noumenon limits sensibility without extending cognition.

grounding.note: Negative noumenon limits sensibility without extending cognition.

items.text: Confusion of faculty-use → transcendental amphiboly → Leibnizian intellectualization of phenomena.

passages.note: Leibniz's intellectualization of phenomena follows amphiboly.

grounding.note: Leibniz's intellectualization of phenomena follows amphiboly.

items.text: Transcendental reflection → assignment of concepts to sensibility or understanding → dissolution of false metaphysical principles.

passages.note: Reflection assigns faculty-source and prevents false synthetic propositions.
Reflection assigns faculty-source and prevents false synthetic propositions.

grounding.note: Reflection assigns faculty-source and prevents false synthetic propositions.

items.text: Classification of nothing → formal closure: not every thinkable representation is an object.

passages.note: The taxonomy closes by separating thinkable emptiness from objects.
The taxonomy closes by separating thinkable emptiness from objects.

grounding.note: The taxonomy closes by separating thinkable emptiness from objects.

items.text: The territory of truth is redrawn as possible experience, not as being in general.

passages.note: Truth's territory is the bounded field of possible experience.
Truth's territory is the bounded field of possible experience.

grounding.note: Truth's territory is the bounded field of possible experience.

items.text: Ontology is demoted from science of things as such to analytic of the pure understanding’s empirical employment.

passages.note: Ontology must give place to analytic of pure understanding.

grounding.note: Ontology must give place to analytic of pure understanding.

items.text: Noumenon is reclassified from supersensible object to boundary-function.

passages.note: Noumenon is assigned a merely negative limitative use.

grounding.note: Noumenon is assigned a merely negative limitative use.

items.text: The thing-in-itself becomes thinkable as limit but unknowable as determinate object.

passages.note: Things in themselves are thinkable only as unknown somethings.

grounding.note: Things in themselves are thinkable only as unknown somethings.

items.text: The apparent expansion of understanding beyond sensibility is reinterpreted as a void produced by abstraction.

passages.note: Transcendent seeming is a contentless logical form after abstraction.

grounding.note: Transcendent seeming is a contentless logical form after abstraction.

items.text: Sensibility becomes a positive source of objective cognition, not a defect or confusion of intellectual cognition.

passages.note: Sensibility is a distinct source, not intellectual confusion.

grounding.note: Sensibility is a distinct source, not intellectual confusion.

items.text: Space and time are repositioned as prior formal conditions of appearances rather than relations derived from things.

passages.note: Space and time precede phenomena as formal conditions.

grounding.note: Space and time precede phenomena as formal conditions.

items.text: Logical relations among concepts cease to be reliable guides to ontological relations among objects.

passages.note: Logical comparison alone cannot establish objective relations.

grounding.note: Logical comparison alone cannot establish objective relations.

items.text: Leibnizian principles are reclassified as valid only under illicit abstraction from sensuous conditions.

passages.note: Leibnizian principles fail when sensuous conditions are omitted.
Leibnizian principles fail when sensuous conditions are omitted.

grounding.note: Leibnizian principles fail when sensuous conditions are omitted.

items.text: Difference, opposition, internality, and form/matter are split according to their transcendental place.

passages.note: The four reflection titles are differentiated by transcendental place.
The four reflection titles are differentiated by transcendental place.

grounding.note: The four reflection titles are differentiated by transcendental place.

items.text: “Nothing” is mapped as multiple failures of objecthood rather than as a single negation.

passages.note: Nothing is divided into multiple forms of object-failure.
Nothing is divided into multiple forms of object-failure.

grounding.note: Nothing is divided into multiple forms of object-failure.

items.text: The unknowable is no longer an invitation to speculative extension but a structural marker of cognitive finitude.

passages.note: The unknowable marks limits of sensibility and cognitive use.
The unknowable marks limits of sensibility and cognitive use.

grounding.note: The unknowable marks limits of sensibility and cognitive use.

items.text: Surface: the chapter determines whether pure concepts of understanding can apply to phenomena, noumena, or both.

passages.note: The chapter contrasts empirical category-use with putative noumenal use.
The chapter contrasts empirical category-use with putative noumenal use.

grounding.note: The chapter contrasts empirical category-use with putative noumenal use.

items.text: Structural: cognition is generated only through the conjunction of sensibility as givenness and understanding as synthesis.

passages.note: Object-determination requires sensibility and understanding together.

grounding.note: Object-determination requires sensibility and understanding together.

items.text: Diagnostic: metaphysical error is produced by confusing empirical, transcendental, logical, and sensible uses of concepts.

passages.note: Amphiboly follows confusion of logical and transcendental faculty-use.
Amphiboly follows confusion of logical and transcendental faculty-use.

grounding.note: Amphiboly follows confusion of logical and transcendental faculty-use.

items.text: Methodological: transcendental reflection functions as a topic assigning every representation to its proper cognitive source.

passages.note: Transcendental topic assigns conceptions to sensibility or understanding.

grounding.note: Transcendental topic assigns conceptions to sensibility or understanding.

items.text: Metastrategic: reason secures its domain by limiting its claims rather than by extending them.

passages.note: Understanding secures itself by determining and respecting its boundaries.

grounding.note: Understanding secures itself by determining and respecting its boundaries.

items.text: Ontological: objects of human cognition are appearances; things in themselves are not denied but withdrawn from determination.

passages.note: Human objects are phenomena; things in themselves remain undetermined.

grounding.note: Human objects are phenomena; things in themselves remain undetermined.

items.text: Epistemic: objective validity is not produced by conceptual consistency but by relation to possible intuition.

passages.note: Objective validity requires possible intuitive presentation, not mere logic.

grounding.note: Objective validity requires possible intuitive presentation, not mere logic.

items.text: Temporal/Formal: time is required for categories such as causality, contingency, reality, and substance to acquire determinate sense.

passages.note: Quantity, reality, substance, causality, and contingency require time.

grounding.note: Quantity, reality, substance, causality, and contingency require time.

items.text: Polemical: Leibnizian intellectualism and Lockean sensualism are both rejected as reductions of the dual-source structure of cognition.

passages.note: Leibnizian intellectualization and Lockean sensualization reject dual sources.

grounding.note: Leibnizian intellectualization and Lockean sensualization reject dual sources.

items.text: Limitative: the supersensible is preserved only as empty room beyond the bounds of sensuous intuition, not as a field of knowledge.

passages.note: Noumenal space is empty and cannot be filled by experience or understanding.

grounding.note: Noumenal space is empty and cannot be filled by experience or understanding.

items.text: The axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the chapter’s main restriction: categories have objective validity only within possible experience.

passages.note: These passages explicitly establish empirical-only objective validity.
These passages explicitly establish empirical-only objective validity.
These passages explicitly establish empirical-only objective validity.

grounding.note: These passages explicitly establish empirical-only objective validity.

items.text: The distinction between negative and positive noumenon is sufficient to reconstruct the chapter’s handling of things in themselves.

passages.note: They define both noumenon senses and retain only the negative one.
They define both noumenon senses and retain only the negative one.
They define both noumenon senses and retain only the negative one.

grounding.note: They define both noumenon senses and retain only the negative one.

items.text: The appendix is reconstructible from the axioms of transcendental reflection, faculty-distinction, and amphiboly.

passages.note: The appendix states reflection, faculty distinction, and amphiboly directly.
The appendix states reflection, faculty distinction, and amphiboly directly.

grounding.note: The appendix states reflection, faculty distinction, and amphiboly directly.

items.text: What remains underdetermined is the positive status of the thing-in-itself as cause, ground, or merely limiting correlate of appearance.

passages.note: The object is called cause of appearance yet denied all category-determination.

grounding.note: The object is called cause of appearance yet denied all category-determination.

items.text: The structure is internally coherent so long as “thinking” the noumenon is kept distinct from “cognizing” it.

passages.note: Noumenon is thinkable problematically but unavailable to cognition.
Noumenon is thinkable problematically but unavailable to cognition.

grounding.note: Noumenon is thinkable problematically but unavailable to cognition.

items.text: The main tension lies in requiring reference to a non-sensible ground while denying all categories by which such reference could be determined.

passages.note: A ground is posited while quantity, reality, substance, and cause are barred.

grounding.note: A ground is posited while quantity, reality, substance, and cause are barred.

items.text: The argument is strongest where it shows that logical possibility cannot replace conditions of object-givenness.

passages.note: The passage expressly rejects logical possibility as objective possibility.

grounding.note: The passage expressly rejects logical possibility as objective possibility.

items.text: The argument depends on compression where it treats human sensibility as the only available intuition while leaving other possible intuitions merely problematic.

passages.note: Human sensuous intuition is fixed, while other intuition remains merely problematic.
Human sensuous intuition is fixed, while other intuition remains merely problematic.

grounding.note: Human sensuous intuition is fixed, while other intuition remains merely problematic.

items.text: Reconstruction from this system would preserve the real movement: boundary of understanding → voiding of transcendental use → negative noumenon → critique of amphiboly.

passages.note: These passages supply the stated sequence from boundary to amphiboly critique.
These passages supply the stated sequence from boundary to amphiboly critique.
These passages supply the stated sequence from boundary to amphiboly critique.
These passages supply the stated sequence from boundary to amphiboly critique.

grounding.note: These passages supply the stated sequence from boundary to amphiboly critique.

items.text: Problem: empirical perception gives only contingent succession, but experience requires objective temporal determination.

passages.note: Perception yields contingent conjunction; experience requires objective temporal relation.

grounding.note: Perception yields contingent conjunction; experience requires objective temporal relation.

items.text: Reframing: objectivity is not extracted from perception; it is generated by a priori rules governing the temporal synthesis of perceptions.

passages.note: A priori temporal concepts and apperceptive rules determine experience.
A priori temporal concepts and apperceptive rules determine experience.

grounding.note: A priori temporal concepts and apperceptive rules determine experience.

items.text: Core thesis: experience is possible only through necessary connections among perceptions under rules of time.

passages.note: The stated principle makes necessary connection of perceptions the condition of experience.

grounding.note: The stated principle makes necessary connection of perceptions the condition of experience.

items.text: Argument type: transcendental deduction of empirical objectivity through temporal schematization.

passages.note: The text derives empirical-objective principles through schemata and possible experience.
The text derives empirical-objective principles through schemata and possible experience.

grounding.note: The text derives empirical-objective principles through schemata and possible experience.

items.text: Movement: subjective apprehension → insufficiency of perception → necessity of temporal rule → analogical regulation → objective experience.

passages.note: The opening insufficiency, temporal rules, and unity of nature form this movement.
The opening insufficiency, temporal rules, and unity of nature form this movement.
The opening insufficiency, temporal rules, and unity of nature form this movement.

grounding.note: The opening insufficiency, temporal rules, and unity of nature form this movement.

items.text: The three modes of time generate three analogies: permanence, succession, coexistence.

passages.note: The three temporal modi and corresponding rules are explicitly named.

grounding.note: The three temporal modi and corresponding rules are explicitly named.

items.text: Final position: nature is the unity of all phenomena under necessary a priori rules of temporal connection.

passages.note: Nature is defined as phenomena connected by necessary laws.

grounding.note: Nature is defined as phenomena connected by necessary laws.

items.text: Experience is empirical cognition that determines an object by means of perceptions.

passages.note: Experience is explicitly defined as empirical cognition determining objects through perceptions.

grounding.note: Experience is explicitly defined as empirical cognition determining objects through perceptions.

items.text: Experience requires a synthesis of perceptions not itself contained in perception.

passages.note: Experience is a synthesis not contained in perception.

grounding.note: Experience is a synthesis not contained in perception.

items.text: The synthesis required for experience consists in the unity of the manifold of perception in one consciousness.

passages.note: The required synthesis contains the unity of the manifold in consciousness.

grounding.note: The required synthesis contains the unity of the manifold in consciousness.

items.text: Perceptions as apprehended are contingently conjoined and do not themselves disclose necessity.

passages.note: Perceptions come together contingently, without necessity discoverable in apprehension.

grounding.note: Perceptions come together contingently, without necessity discoverable in apprehension.

items.text: Objective experience requires relations of existence to be represented as objectively in time, not merely as subjectively apprehended in time.

passages.note: Experience must represent existence objectively in time rather than as apprehended.

grounding.note: Experience must represent existence objectively in time rather than as apprehended.

items.text: Time itself cannot be perceived.

passages.note: Time itself is explicitly said not to be perceived.

grounding.note: Time itself is explicitly said not to be perceived.

items.text: Determination of objects in time requires a priori concepts of temporal connection.

passages.note: Temporal existence-determination requires a priori connecting conceptions.

grounding.note: Temporal existence-determination requires a priori connecting conceptions.

items.text: A priori temporal concepts possess necessity.

passages.note: The relevant a priori conceptions are said always to possess necessity.

grounding.note: The relevant a priori conceptions are said always to possess necessity.

items.text: The unity of apperception imposes a priori rules on all possible empirical consciousness in time.

passages.note: Apperceptive unity subjects empirical consciousness to temporal rules.

grounding.note: Apperceptive unity subjects empirical consciousness to temporal rules.

items.text: The analogies concern the existence of phenomena and their temporal relations, not the construction of intuition or sensation.

passages.note: The principles concern phenomenal existence and its relations, not intuition's synthesis.

grounding.note: The principles concern phenomenal existence and its relations, not intuition's synthesis.

items.text: Existence cannot be constructed a priori.

passages.note: Existence is explicitly said not to admit construction.

grounding.note: Existence is explicitly said not to admit construction.

items.text: The analogies are regulative principles of empirical synthesis, not constitutive principles of object-generation.

passages.note: Analogies are explicitly rules of experience and merely regulative.

grounding.note: Analogies are explicitly rules of experience and merely regulative.

items.text: Categories apply to experience only through their schemata.

passages.note: Phenomena are subordinated to categories only through schemata.

grounding.note: Phenomena are subordinated to categories only through schemata.

items.text: The principles of experience apply only to phenomena, not to things in themselves.

passages.note: The principles have empirical, not transcendent, validity.

grounding.note: The principles have empirical, not transcendent, validity.

items.text: Temporal relations among phenomena require a permanent substratum.

passages.note: A perceptible substratum is required for temporal determination.

grounding.note: A perceptible substratum is required for temporal determination.

items.text: The permanent substratum of phenomena is substance.

passages.note: The phenomenal temporal substratum is identified as substance.

grounding.note: The phenomenal temporal substratum is identified as substance.

items.text: Substance in phenomena remains permanent while its determinations change.

passages.note: Substance remains while changing features are its determinations.

grounding.note: Substance remains while changing features are its determinations.

items.text: Objective succession requires an irreversible rule determining which state precedes and which follows.

passages.note: Objective sequence requires a necessary determination of before and after.

grounding.note: Objective sequence requires a necessary determination of before and after.

items.text: The rule of objective succession is the relation of cause and effect.

passages.note: The necessary temporal relation is identified as cause and effect.

grounding.note: The necessary temporal relation is identified as cause and effect.

items.text: An event is a change in the determinations of substance, not the absolute origin or extinction of substance.

passages.note: Change is defined as successive states of the same permanent object.

grounding.note: Change is defined as successive states of the same permanent object.

items.text: Objective coexistence requires reciprocal temporal determinability among coexistent substances.

passages.note: Objective coexistence requires reciprocal determination of temporal position.
Objective coexistence requires reciprocal determination of temporal position.

grounding.note: Objective coexistence requires reciprocal determination of temporal position.

items.text: Reciprocal temporal determinability among substances is dynamical community or mutual influence.

passages.note: Reciprocal influence is defined as community or reciprocity.

grounding.note: Reciprocal influence is defined as community or reciprocity.

items.text: Nature is the totality of phenomena connected in their existence according to necessary rules.

passages.note: Nature is the totality of necessarily connected phenomena.

grounding.note: Nature is the totality of necessarily connected phenomena.

items.text: Experience is not mere intuition or sensation.

passages.note: Experience is distinguished from mere intuition or sensation.

grounding.note: Experience is distinguished from mere intuition or sensation.

items.text: The unity of experience is not contained in perception itself.

passages.note: The synthesis and unity of experience are not contained in perception.

grounding.note: The synthesis and unity of experience are not contained in perception.

items.text: Necessity is not discoverable from apprehension alone.

passages.note: Necessity cannot be discovered in apprehension.

grounding.note: Necessity cannot be discovered in apprehension.

items.text: Objective temporal order is not identical with subjective succession of representations.

passages.note: Mere apprehensive order leaves objective sequence undetermined.

grounding.note: Mere apprehensive order leaves objective sequence undetermined.

items.text: Time is not an object of perception.

passages.note: Time itself is not an object of perception.

grounding.note: Time itself is not an object of perception.

items.text: The existence of phenomena is not constructible like mathematical magnitude.

passages.note: Existence cannot be constructed a priori.

grounding.note: Existence cannot be constructed a priori.

items.text: Analogies are not mathematical proportions.

passages.note: Philosophical analogies are contrasted with mathematical proportions.

grounding.note: Philosophical analogies are contrasted with mathematical proportions.

items.text: Analogies do not yield the fourth term of experience a priori; they yield only the rule for finding it.

passages.note: Analogies provide a rule for finding the fourth term, not that term itself.

grounding.note: Analogies provide a rule for finding the fourth term, not that term itself.

items.text: The analogies are not constitutive principles.

passages.note: Analogies are explicitly merely regulative.

grounding.note: Analogies are explicitly merely regulative.

items.text: The categories are not directly applied to phenomena apart from schemata.

passages.note: Categories are applied through schemata rather than directly.

grounding.note: Categories are applied through schemata rather than directly.

items.text: The principles do not synthesize things in themselves.

passages.note: The principles cannot synthetically cognize things in themselves.

grounding.note: The principles cannot synthetically cognize things in themselves.

items.text: Substance is not inferred dogmatically from the concept of persistence alone.

passages.note: A dogmatic proof of substance from concepts is rejected.

grounding.note: A dogmatic proof of substance from concepts is rejected.

items.text: Change is not absolute coming-to-be or passing-away of substance.

passages.note: Origin and extinction are distinguished from change.

grounding.note: Origin and extinction are distinguished from change.

items.text: Origin from nothing is not a possible object of experience.

passages.note: Creation cannot be admitted as an event among phenomena.

grounding.note: Creation cannot be admitted as an event among phenomena.

items.text: Extinction into nothing is not a possible object of experience.

passages.note: Absolute extinction is excluded from possible perception.

grounding.note: Absolute extinction is excluded from possible perception.

items.text: Causality is not derived from repeated empirical observation of similar sequences.

passages.note: The empirical derivation of causal necessity from similar sequences is rejected.

grounding.note: The empirical derivation of causal necessity from similar sequences is rejected.

items.text: Objective succession is not a subjective play of imagination.

passages.note: Sequence without a rule is called a merely subjective play of representations.

grounding.note: Sequence without a rule is called a merely subjective play of representations.

items.text: Simultaneous cause and effect do not abolish the temporal order of causal dependence.

passages.note: Simultaneity of cause and effect leaves their dynamical temporal order intact.

grounding.note: Simultaneity of cause and effect leaves their dynamical temporal order intact.

items.text: Coexistence is not cognized by mere placement in the same absolute time.

passages.note: Same-time placement alone cannot establish objective coexistence.

grounding.note: Same-time placement alone cannot establish objective coexistence.

items.text: Isolated substances cannot be objects of possible empirical coexistence.

passages.note: Completely isolated substances cannot yield empirical cognition of coexistence.

grounding.note: Completely isolated substances cannot yield empirical cognition of coexistence.

items.text: Empty space, if unperceived and without empirical connection, is not an object of possible experience.

passages.note: Empty space beyond empirical perception is not an object of possible experience.

grounding.note: Empty space beyond empirical perception is not an object of possible experience.

items.text: Synthetic a priori laws of experience cannot be proved dogmatically from mere concepts.

passages.note: Dogmatic proof from mere concepts is said to fail for these principles.

grounding.note: Dogmatic proof from mere concepts is said to fail for these principles.

items.text: Experience requires necessary connection among perceptions because perception supplies contingency while experience requires objective unity.

passages.note: Contingent perception is contrasted with objectively necessary experiential unity.

grounding.note: Contingent perception is contrasted with objectively necessary experiential unity.

items.text: Temporal objectivity must be rule-governed because time cannot itself serve as perceived standard of temporal placement.

passages.note: Unperceivable time requires rule-governed temporal connection.

grounding.note: Unperceivable time requires rule-governed temporal connection.

items.text: The analogies are necessary conditions of experience because all empirical consciousness must be synthesized under a priori unity in time.

passages.note: Apperceptive unity subjects all empirical consciousness to temporal rules.

grounding.note: Apperceptive unity subjects all empirical consciousness to temporal rules.

items.text: The analogies regulate relations of existence rather than construct objects because existence is not constructible a priori.

passages.note: Existence is not constructible; analogies therefore regulate its relations.
Existence is not constructible; analogies therefore regulate its relations.

grounding.note: Existence is not constructible; analogies therefore regulate its relations.

items.text: The analogies have empirical but not transcendent use because categories reach phenomena only through schemata and cannot determine things in themselves.

passages.note: Schemata confine the principles to empirical phenomenal use.

grounding.note: Schemata confine the principles to empirical phenomenal use.

items.text: Substance must be permanent because temporal relations require a stable phenomenal correlate of time.

passages.note: Substance supplies the stable phenomenal correlate required for time-relations.

grounding.note: Substance supplies the stable phenomenal correlate required for time-relations.

items.text: Change presupposes permanence because alteration is intelligible only as successive determinations of the same enduring substratum.

passages.note: Alteration is successive determination of one enduring subject.

grounding.note: Alteration is successive determination of one enduring subject.

items.text: Absolute creation or annihilation cannot enter possible experience because either would destroy the unity of empirical time.

passages.note: Origin or extinction of substances would abolish empirical unity of time.
Origin or extinction of substances would abolish empirical unity of time.

grounding.note: Origin or extinction of substances would abolish empirical unity of time.

items.text: Objective succession requires causality because only a necessary rule distinguishes an event-order from reversible subjective apprehension.

passages.note: Only causal necessity distinguishes objective from reversible apprehensive order.

grounding.note: Only causal necessity distinguishes objective from reversible apprehensive order.

items.text: Empirical truth about events depends on causality because an event becomes objective only when its place in time is determined by a rule.

passages.note: Causality grounds objective empirical judgment about event-sequence.

grounding.note: Causality grounds objective empirical judgment about event-sequence.

items.text: The empirical concept of action implies substance because action is causality grounded in a permanent subject of changing determinations.

passages.note: Action leads through causality to substance as permanent subject.

grounding.note: Action leads through causality to substance as permanent subject.

items.text: All change is continuous in form because time contains no smallest parts and causal production determines transition through degrees.

passages.note: Causal production proceeds through degrees because time lacks smallest parts.
Causal production proceeds through degrees because time lacks smallest parts.

grounding.note: Causal production proceeds through degrees because time lacks smallest parts.

items.text: Coexistence requires reciprocity because reversible apprehension can be objectively valid only if each substance determines the temporal position of the other.

passages.note: Objective coexistence requires reciprocal influence and temporal determination.
Objective coexistence requires reciprocal influence and temporal determination.

grounding.note: Objective coexistence requires reciprocal influence and temporal determination.

items.text: The unity of nature follows from the analogies because all phenomena must be temporally connected under rules of permanence, causality, and reciprocity.

passages.note: The three temporal rules express the lawful unity of nature.
The three temporal rules express the lawful unity of nature.

grounding.note: The three temporal rules express the lawful unity of nature.

items.text: Objectivity is produced by rule-bound temporal synthesis, not received as a property of sensations.

passages.note: Objective significance consists in necessary rule-bound connection of representations.

grounding.note: Objective significance consists in necessary rule-bound connection of representations.

items.text: The phenomenal object is the correlate of necessary order in representations.

passages.note: The phenomenal object is what contains the necessary rule of apprehension.

grounding.note: The phenomenal object is what contains the necessary rule of apprehension.

items.text: Nature is not an aggregate of given things but the lawful unity of possible experience.

passages.note: Nature is defined as lawful totality of phenomenal existence.

grounding.note: Nature is defined as lawful totality of phenomenal existence.

items.text: Substance, causality, and community are not optional metaphysical hypotheses; they are structural conditions for temporal object-determination.

passages.note: The three relations are each presented as conditions of temporal object-cognition.
The three relations are each presented as conditions of temporal object-cognition.
The three relations are each presented as conditions of temporal object-cognition.

grounding.note: The three relations are each presented as conditions of temporal object-cognition.

items.text: Empirical laws depend on primitive a priori laws because particular regularities presuppose the possibility of lawful experience as such.

passages.note: Empirical laws depend on primitive a priori laws making nature possible.

grounding.note: Empirical laws depend on primitive a priori laws making nature possible.

items.text: The analogies convert ontology into conditions of empirical temporality: being-in-experience means being determinable in time by rule.

passages.note: The analogies determine phenomenal existence through time-relations under rules.

grounding.note: The analogies determine phenomenal existence through time-relations under rules.

items.text: The distinction between subjective sequence and objective succession makes causality the condition of eventhood.

passages.note: Necessary causal order distinguishes eventhood from subjective sequence.

grounding.note: Necessary causal order distinguishes eventhood from subjective sequence.

items.text: The distinction between reversible apprehension and objective simultaneity makes reciprocity the condition of coexistence.

grounding.note: Multiple side-by-side times are rejected in favor of one time.

items.text: Substance is reclassified as condition of temporal determinability, not as dogmatic thing-in-itself.

grounding.note: Coexistence is cognized only under dynamical reciprocal community.

items.text: The entire system restricts metaphysics by making objectivity dependent on conditions of empirical givenness rather than on conceptual thinkability.

passages.note: Objectivity requires possible experience and intuition, not concepts alone.

grounding.note: Objectivity requires possible experience and intuition, not concepts alone.

items.text: The refutation of idealism reverses Cartesian priority: inner experience becomes dependent upon outer experience for its temporal determinacy.

passages.note: Internal experience is possible only through external experience.

grounding.note: Internal experience is possible only through external experience.

items.text: The categories are preserved as a priori while denied independent object-generating power.

passages.note: Categories remain a priori forms while lacking independent cognition.

grounding.note: Categories remain a priori forms while lacking independent cognition.

items.text: Natural necessity becomes lawful phenomenal dependence, not metaphysical compulsion of things in themselves.

passages.note: Necessity concerns causal relations of phenomena only.

grounding.note: Necessity concerns causal relations of phenomena only.

items.text: Experience is constructed as one continuous rule-governed field in which every valid perception must have an assignable place.

grounding.note: Experience requires continuous unity in which perceptions have their place.

items.text: The possible cannot be treated as an unlimited reservoir beyond actuality unless reason illegitimately exceeds the understanding.

passages.note: Understanding cannot survey possibility beyond experience; absolute possibility belongs to reason.
Understanding cannot survey possibility beyond experience; absolute possibility belongs to reason.

grounding.note: Understanding cannot survey possibility beyond experience; absolute possibility belongs to reason.

items.text: The proof of objective reality for pure concepts depends on exhibition in intuition, making intuition the limiting interface between thought and objectivity.

passages.note: Objective reality of pure concepts requires intuition.

grounding.note: Objective reality of pure concepts requires intuition.

items.text: The system simultaneously grounds empirical realism and transcendental idealism by making external objects empirically necessary while denying access to things in themselves.

grounding.note: External objects are empirically necessary while space is denied as thing-in-itself property.

items.text: It must not be true that concepts alone can generate objective reference.

grounding.note: Concepts alone do not yield cognitions or synthetic propositions.

items.text: It must not be true that existence is a predicate contained in the complete concept of a thing.

passages.note: Existence is not inferred from complete conceptual determination.

grounding.note: Existence is not inferred from complete conceptual determination.

items.text: It must not be true that inner consciousness contains its own temporal criterion.

passages.note: Inner time-determination needs a permanent outside inner sense.

grounding.note: Inner time-determination needs a permanent outside inner sense.

items.text: It must not be true that the subject can be empirically determined without external intuition.

passages.note: Self-cognition without external empirical intuition is excluded.

grounding.note: Self-cognition without external empirical intuition is excluded.

items.text: It must not be true that a priori categories apply to things independently of possible experience.

passages.note: Categories are restricted to possible experience.

grounding.note: Categories are restricted to possible experience.

passages.note: Chance, leaps, hiatuses, and blind fate are excluded.

grounding.note: Chance, leaps, hiatuses, and blind fate are excluded.

items.text: It must not be true that absolute possibility is available to the understanding.
