grounding.note: Absolute possibility is not an empirically employable understanding concept.

items.text: It must not be true that the field of possible objects can be mapped independently of our forms of intuition and understanding.

passages.note: Other possible experiential spheres cannot be decided by understanding.

grounding.note: Other possible experiential spheres cannot be decided by understanding.

items.text: It must not be true that the permanent required for time-determination can be supplied by the thinking “I.”

grounding.note: The thinking “I” has no intuition-predicate of permanence.

items.text: It must not be true that empirical realism requires things in space to be things in themselves.

grounding.note: Treating space as thing-in-itself property produces dogmatic idealism.

items.text: The system is organized around the foreclosure of a conceptually accessible absolute object.

grounding.note: Objective cognition is limited to intuitively given possible experience.

items.text: The argument depends on the inadmissibility of a self-sufficient interiority capable of grounding experience from within itself.

grounding.note: Inner experience depends on external permanence and experience.

Modal predicates are restricted to cognitive relations within experience.

grounding.note: Modal predicates are restricted to cognitive relations within experience.

items.text: The unity of experience silently forbids plural, disconnected experiential worlds as objects of understanding.

grounding.note: Understanding cannot establish more than one all-embracing experience.

items.text: The discourse circles an unavailable outside: what lies beyond possible experience may be thinkable by reason as a problem but cannot be cognized by understanding.

grounding.note: Beyond-experience questions are assigned to reason and deferred.

items.text: The system requires that objectivity be neither merely subjective representation nor thing-in-itself access, but this mediating position remains structurally tense.

grounding.note: External objects are necessary for experience while space is not thing-in-itself property.

items.text: Pure understanding principles → conditions of possible experience → no transcendental employment beyond experience.

grounding.note: Pure principles are principles only of possible experience.

grounding.note: The modal thesis leads to formal experiential possibility.

items.text: Reality problem → perception as criterion → lawful mediate existence → boundary against unsupported existence-claims.

grounding.note: Reality and mediate existence depend on perception and empirical law.

items.text: Idealist challenge → inner experience analyzed → time-determination requires permanence → permanence requires external objects → external experience proved.

grounding.note: The theorem and proof derive outer experience from time-determination.

items.text: Necessity problem → causality of phenomenal states → hypothetical necessity → nature as lawful continuity.

grounding.note: Necessity is causal, hypothetical, and continuous within nature.

grounding.note: Scope questions are withheld from understanding and assigned to reason.

items.text: General closure → categories require intuition → relation-categories require external intuition → all pure principles apply only to possible experience.

grounding.note: Modality indicates cognitive procedure rather than object-content.

grounding.note: Possibility requires construction under experiential form, not consistency.

grounding.note: Reality depends on perception or lawful perceptual connection.

items.text: Inner experience loses foundational priority and becomes dependent on external experience.

passages.note: Internal experience is dependent on external experience.

grounding.note: Internal experience is dependent on external experience.

items.text: Idealism is displaced from a skepticism about outer objects to a failure to explain inner temporal determination.

items.text: The possible is no longer an independently surveyable domain larger than the real.

grounding.note: Understanding cannot establish a possibility-field exceeding reality.

Categories are valid only with intuition in possible experiential synthesis.

grounding.note: External intuition grounds relation categories, quantity, and internal change.

items.text: Nature becomes visible as the continuous lawful unity required for experience, not as a thing-in-itself totality.

grounding.note: Nature is the continuous lawful unity of phenomena.

items.text: Epistemic: cognition requires the conjunction of concept, intuition, sensation, and lawful synthesis.

grounding.note: External experience conditions determinate inner experience.

passages.note: Understanding makes unified continuous experience possible.

grounding.note: Understanding makes unified continuous experience possible.

grounding.note: Absolute possibility and other experiential spheres belong to reason.

items.text: Reconstruction from this system would preserve the real movement: modal restriction → experiential criterion → anti-idealist inversion → phenomenal necessity → critique of pure conceptual metaphysics.

grounding.note: The I think is described as accompanying all thought.

items.text: The “I think” is not an intuition of the self as object.

passages.note: Self-consciousness in thought is a logical function and does not present the self as object.

grounding.note: Self-consciousness in thought is a logical function and does not present the self as object.

items.text: The unity of apperception is a logical condition of thought, not a metaphysical determination of a thinking substance.

passages.note: Subjecthood in judgment does not establish self-subsistent substantial existence.
Subjecthood in judgment does not establish self-subsistent substantial existence.

grounding.note: Subjecthood in judgment does not establish self-subsistent substantial existence.

items.text: Rational psychology must derive all claims from the single representation “I think” if it is to remain pure.

passages.note: The I think is explicitly called rational psychology's only text.

grounding.note: The I think is explicitly called rational psychology's only text.

items.text: Any empirical predicate introduced into rational psychology converts it into empirical psychology.

passages.note: Any particular empirical perception converts rational psychology into empirical psychology.

grounding.note: Any particular empirical perception converts rational psychology into empirical psychology.

items.text: The logical subject of judgment cannot thereby be cognized as a substantial subject of existence.

passages.note: Logical subjecthood is insufficient for cognition of substantial existence.
Logical subjecthood is insufficient for cognition of substantial existence.

grounding.note: Logical subjecthood is insufficient for cognition of substantial existence.

items.text: Simplicity, identity, and subjecthood in thought are analytic features of apperception, not synthetic cognitions of the soul.

passages.note: Simplicity and identity in thought are analytic, not synthetic knowledge of a substance.
Simplicity and identity in thought are analytic, not synthetic knowledge of a substance.

grounding.note: Simplicity and identity in thought are analytic, not synthetic knowledge of a substance.

items.text: Internal intuition supplies only temporal phenomenal data, not knowledge of the self as thing in itself.

passages.note: Internal empirical intuition is sensuous and presents only phenomenal data.

grounding.note: Internal empirical intuition is sensuous and presents only phenomenal data.

items.text: No permanent intuition is given in inner sense sufficient to ground the category of substance for the self.

passages.note: Inner intuition supplies nothing permanent for the category of substance.

grounding.note: Inner intuition supplies nothing permanent for the category of substance.

items.text: Speculative reason cannot dogmatically affirm either spiritualist or materialist determinations of the soul beyond experience.

passages.note: Neither materialism nor spiritualism determines the soul, and dogmatic affirmations are barred.
Neither materialism nor spiritualism determines the soul, and dogmatic affirmations are barred.

grounding.note: Neither materialism nor spiritualism determines the soul, and dogmatic affirmations are barred.

items.text: Practical reason may legitimately orient the subject beyond empirical life without yielding speculative cognition of the soul.

passages.note: Practical orientation beyond life remains after speculative renunciation.
Practical orientation beyond life remains after speculative renunciation.

grounding.note: Practical orientation beyond life remains after speculative renunciation.

items.text: Cosmological reason applies the demand for unconditioned totality to the objective synthesis of phenomena and thereby generates antinomy.

passages.note: Objective synthesis of phenomena and unconditioned unity generate cosmological contradiction.

grounding.note: Objective synthesis of phenomena and unconditioned unity generate cosmological contradiction.

items.text: A transcendental idea is not a concept adequate to an object given in experience.

passages.note: No object adequate to a transcendental idea can be given in possible experience.

grounding.note: No object adequate to a transcendental idea can be given in possible experience.

items.text: Dialectical sophisms are not accidental fabrications of individual thinkers.

passages.note: Dialectical arguments are not fictions or accidental products of reason.

grounding.note: Dialectical arguments are not fictions or accidental products of reason.

items.text: The illusion of pure reason is not removable by superior intelligence.

passages.note: Even the wisest cannot become thoroughly rid of dialectical illusion.

grounding.note: Even the wisest cannot become thoroughly rid of dialectical illusion.

items.text: The “I think” is not a determinate concept of a soul-object.

passages.note: The I represents only a contentless transcendental subject = x.

grounding.note: The I represents only a contentless transcendental subject = x.

items.text: Self-consciousness is not inner cognition of the self as substance.

passages.note: Self-consciousness in thought does not cognize the self as an object.

grounding.note: Self-consciousness in thought does not cognize the self as an object.

items.text: Logical subjecthood is not ontological substantiality.

passages.note: The conclusion from subject in thought to existing substance is exposed as equivocation.

grounding.note: The conclusion from subject in thought to existing substance is exposed as equivocation.

items.text: Logical simplicity is not metaphysical simplicity of substance.

passages.note: Logical simplicity of Ego is not simple substantiality.

grounding.note: Logical simplicity of Ego is not simple substantiality.

items.text: Analytic identity of apperception is not personal identity as persistence of substance through time.

passages.note: Analytic identity in representations does not establish personal substance-identity.

grounding.note: Analytic identity in representations does not establish personal substance-identity.

items.text: Distinguishing oneself from outer things does not prove separability from outer things.

passages.note: Distinction from external things does not show independent existence from them.

grounding.note: Distinction from external things does not show independent existence from them.

items.text: Rational psychology is not a science that enlarges self-knowledge.

passages.note: Rational psychology supplies no addition to self-knowledge.

grounding.note: Rational psychology supplies no addition to self-knowledge.

items.text: Inner sense does not disclose the self as noumenon.

passages.note: Inner empirical intuition cannot cognize the self as noumenon.

grounding.note: Inner empirical intuition cannot cognize the self as noumenon.

items.text: The Cartesian “I think” does not yield an inference to substantial existence.

passages.note: I think does not infer existence; the Cartesian propositions are identical.

grounding.note: I think does not infer existence; the Cartesian propositions are identical.

items.text: The soul’s simplicity, even if granted, does not prove its permanence or immortality.

passages.note: Simplicity excludes decomposition but not gradual intensive diminution.

grounding.note: Simplicity excludes decomposition but not gradual intensive diminution.

items.text: The failure of speculative proof of immortality does not refute practical admission of future life.

passages.note: Practical admission of future life loses nothing from speculative renunciation.

grounding.note: Practical admission of future life loses nothing from speculative renunciation.

items.text: Materialism cannot explain the thinking subject as merely spatial matter.

passages.note: Materialism cannot determine the constitution of the thinking Ego.

grounding.note: Materialism cannot determine the constitution of the thinking Ego.

items.text: Spiritualism cannot establish the independent constitution of the soul by pure concepts.

passages.note: Spiritualism is equally insufficient to determine the self's existence.

grounding.note: Spiritualism is equally insufficient to determine the self's existence.

items.text: Cosmical ideas are not doctrines of a valid rational cosmology.

passages.note: Rational cosmology is presented as pretended, not valid doctrine.

grounding.note: Rational cosmology is presented as pretended, not valid doctrine.

items.text: Antinomy is not a contingent dispute but reason’s necessary self-conflict when totality is sought in phenomena.

passages.note: Cosmological antithetic is natural and unavoidable when reason seeks unconditioned unity.
Cosmological antithetic is natural and unavoidable when reason seeks unconditioned unity.

grounding.note: Cosmological antithetic is natural and unavoidable when reason seeks unconditioned unity.

items.text: Rational psychology collapses if it adds any determinate empirical content to the “I think.”

passages.note: The smallest empirical predicate destroys the purity of rational psychology.
The smallest empirical predicate destroys the purity of rational psychology.

grounding.note: The smallest empirical predicate destroys the purity of rational psychology.

items.text: Rational psychology cannot establish the soul as substance because the category of substance requires intuition and no permanent inner intuition is available.

passages.note: Substance requires permanent intuition, which inner intuition does not provide.

grounding.note: Substance requires permanent intuition, which inner intuition does not provide.

items.text: The paralogism consists in shifting from the logical necessity of using “I” as subject to the metaphysical assertion that the self exists only as subject.

passages.note: The argument shifts between subject as thought-function and object given in intuition.

grounding.note: The argument shifts between subject as thought-function and object given in intuition.

items.text: The predicates substance, simplicity, personality, spirituality, and immortality arise by illicitly objectifying formal features of apperception.

passages.note: Traditional soul predicates arise from applying categories to mere unity of consciousness.
Traditional soul predicates arise from applying categories to mere unity of consciousness.

grounding.note: Traditional soul predicates arise from applying categories to mere unity of consciousness.

items.text: The “I think” gives an indeterminate consciousness of existence, not a determinate cognition of the mode of that existence.

passages.note: I think gives undetermined perception of existence rather than its determinate mode.

grounding.note: I think gives undetermined perception of existence rather than its determinate mode.

items.text: The subject cannot cognize itself through the categories because it must presuppose itself as the condition for applying them.

passages.note: The subject cannot make itself an object of categories it must presuppose.

grounding.note: The subject cannot make itself an object of categories it must presuppose.

items.text: Speculative reason must suspend dogmatic claims both for and against the soul’s immaterial permanence.

passages.note: Natural limits bar both dogmatic assertion and dogmatic counterassertion.

grounding.note: Natural limits bar both dogmatic assertion and dogmatic counterassertion.

items.text: The critique of rational psychology limits knowledge without eliminating the practical significance of the supersensible vocation of reason.

passages.note: Speculation is limited while practical ends and future orientation remain.
Speculation is limited while practical ends and future orientation remain.

grounding.note: Speculation is limited while practical ends and future orientation remain.

items.text: Mendelssohn’s proof fails because simplicity excludes extensive decomposition but not diminution by intensive degree.

passages.note: Mendelssohn overlooks intensive diminution despite the absence of extensive parts.

grounding.note: Mendelssohn overlooks intensive diminution despite the absence of extensive parts.

items.text: Problematical idealism follows from rational psychology if the self is treated as independently determinable without external conditions.

passages.note: Rationalistic psychology makes problematical idealism unavoidable.

grounding.note: Rationalistic psychology makes problematical idealism unavoidable.

items.text: Materialism and spiritualism are both underdetermined because neither can supply the required intuition for determining the self’s mode of existence.

passages.note: Neither materialism nor spiritualism determines the Ego's mode of existence.

grounding.note: Neither materialism nor spiritualism determines the Ego's mode of existence.

items.text: Antinomy differs from paralogism because reason’s demand for objective totality generates opposed claims with symmetrical plausibility.

passages.note: Paralogism is one-sided; cosmological reason produces contradictions with plausibility.

grounding.note: Paralogism is one-sided; cosmological reason produces contradictions with plausibility.

items.text: Transcendental dialectic converts metaphysical error from a defect of reasoning skill into a structural pathology of reason.

passages.note: Dialectical error is necessitated by reason's nature, not merely individual incompetence.
Dialectical error is necessitated by reason's nature, not merely individual incompetence.

grounding.note: Dialectical error is necessitated by reason's nature, not merely individual incompetence.

items.text: The self is indispensable as condition of cognition yet unavailable as object of cognition by the same means.

passages.note: The self conditions thought while remaining unavailable as an object of categorical cognition.
The self conditions thought while remaining unavailable as an object of categorical cognition.

grounding.note: The self conditions thought while remaining unavailable as an object of categorical cognition.

items.text: The more purely rational psychology becomes, the less cognitive content it can legitimately possess.

passages.note: Purity excludes empirical content, while the remaining I is perfectly contentless.
Purity excludes empirical content, while the remaining I is perfectly contentless.

grounding.note: Purity excludes empirical content, while the remaining I is perfectly contentless.

items.text: The critique destroys dogmatic metaphysics by showing that its central inferences depend on applying categories where no object has been given.

passages.note: Dogmatic inferences fail because categories require given intuition not available for the self.
Dogmatic inferences fail because categories require given intuition not available for the self.

grounding.note: Dogmatic inferences fail because categories require given intuition not available for the self.

items.text: The limitation of speculative reason functions defensively: it blocks both dogmatic affirmation and dogmatic negation of supersensible objects.

passages.note: Critical limitation blocks dogmatic affirmation and places opponents under the same renunciation.

grounding.note: Critical limitation blocks dogmatic affirmation and places opponents under the same renunciation.

items.text: The soul is repositioned from theoretical object to practical postulate-field.

passages.note: The soul is denied as speculative object while future-oriented practical use is retained.
The soul is denied as speculative object while future-oriented practical use is retained.

grounding.note: The soul is denied as speculative object while future-oriented practical use is retained.

items.text: Pure reason is self-limiting only through critique; without critique, its lawful demand for unity generates unlawful objectification.

passages.note: Natural rational procedures generate illusion until critique identifies their limits.
Natural rational procedures generate illusion until critique identifies their limits.

grounding.note: Natural rational procedures generate illusion until critique identifies their limits.

items.text: The passage from psychology to cosmology enlarges the dialectical mechanism from illicit self-objectification to systemic contradiction within the idea of the world-whole.

passages.note: The text explicitly transitions from psychological self-problem to objective cosmological synthesis.
The text explicitly transitions from psychological self-problem to objective cosmological synthesis.

grounding.note: The text explicitly transitions from psychological self-problem to objective cosmological synthesis.

items.text: The system requires that thought alone not be capable of giving its own object.

passages.note: Thought alone cannot supply an adequate object; object-cognition requires given intuition.
Thought alone cannot supply an adequate object; object-cognition requires given intuition.

grounding.note: Thought alone cannot supply an adequate object; object-cognition requires given intuition.

items.text: The system requires that logical necessity not entail ontological necessity.

passages.note: Logical necessity of subject-use does not establish existence as substance.

grounding.note: Logical necessity of subject-use does not establish existence as substance.

items.text: The system requires that self-consciousness not be self-intuition as noumenal being.

passages.note: Self-consciousness cannot cognize itself as noumenon through sensuous inner intuition.

grounding.note: Self-consciousness cannot cognize itself as noumenon through sensuous inner intuition.

items.text: The system requires that the unity required for judging not be identical with the unity of a simple substance.

passages.note: Unity and simplicity of Ego in thought do not establish a simple substance.

grounding.note: Unity and simplicity of Ego in thought do not establish a simple substance.

items.text: The system requires that the categories not have unrestricted trans-experiential validity.

passages.note: Categories require intuition and admit no merely rational trans-experiential use.
Categories require intuition and admit no merely rational trans-experiential use.

grounding.note: Categories require intuition and admit no merely rational trans-experiential use.

items.text: The system requires that the subject of experience not be fully present to itself as an object of experience.

passages.note: The subject of thought cannot thereby be presented as an object of experience.
The subject of thought cannot thereby be presented as an object of experience.

grounding.note: The subject of thought cannot thereby be presented as an object of experience.

items.text: The system requires that absence of contradiction in a metaphysical hypothesis not count as proof of objective possibility.

passages.note: Noncontradictory hypotheses admit equally founded counter-possibilities.

grounding.note: Noncontradictory hypotheses admit equally founded counter-possibilities.

items.text: The system requires that practical legitimacy not collapse into speculative cognition.

passages.note: Practical use persists without supplying theoretical knowledge of the self.
Practical use persists without supplying theoretical knowledge of the self.

grounding.note: Practical use persists without supplying theoretical knowledge of the self.

items.text: The system requires that the demand for the unconditioned not be satisfiable by direct theoretical possession of the unconditioned.

passages.note: Reason necessarily seeks unconditioned unity without possessing an adequate object for it.
Reason necessarily seeks unconditioned unity without possessing an adequate object for it.

grounding.note: Reason necessarily seeks unconditioned unity without possessing an adequate object for it.

items.text: The system requires that reason’s natural interests not be treated as sufficient grounds of knowledge.

passages.note: Theoretical incapacity remains despite practical interests and future-oriented ends.
Theoretical incapacity remains despite practical interests and future-oriented ends.

grounding.note: Theoretical incapacity remains despite practical interests and future-oriented ends.

items.text: The inaccessible object around which rational psychology turns is the self as thing in itself.

passages.note: The self as noumenon cannot be cognized through inner empirical intuition.

grounding.note: The self as noumenon cannot be cognized through inner empirical intuition.

items.text: The excluded possibility structuring the critique is intellectual intuition of oneself.

passages.note: The contrast between sensuous and intellectual intuition frames the excluded self-intuition.
The contrast between sensuous and intellectual intuition frames the excluded self-intuition.

grounding.note: The contrast between sensuous and intellectual intuition frames the excluded self-intuition.

items.text: The central foreclosure is a metaphysics in which apperception transparently reveals substance.

passages.note: Apperception does not reveal substance because substance requires intuition.
Apperception does not reveal substance because substance requires intuition.

grounding.note: Apperception does not reveal substance because substance requires intuition.

items.text: The discourse is organized by the impossibility of converting the condition of representation into a represented thing.

passages.note: Unity of consciousness is not an object-giving intuition for category application.

grounding.note: Unity of consciousness is not an object-giving intuition for category application.

items.text: The deepest denial is that reason can ground its supersensible interests by theoretical self-possession.

passages.note: Supersensible practical orientation remains after theoretical self-knowledge is refused.
Supersensible practical orientation remains after theoretical self-knowledge is refused.

grounding.note: Supersensible practical orientation remains after theoretical self-knowledge is refused.

items.text: The antinomial field is organized by the absence of any experienceable world-whole adequate to reason’s demand for absolute totality.

passages.note: Absolute phenomenal totality is a cosmical idea irreconcilable with experience.
Absolute phenomenal totality is a cosmical idea irreconcilable with experience.

grounding.note: Absolute phenomenal totality is a cosmical idea irreconcilable with experience.

items.text: Reason’s Demand: conditioned cognition → search for unconditioned unity.

passages.note: Reason necessarily proceeds toward unconditioned unity and totality.
Reason necessarily proceeds toward unconditioned unity and totality.

grounding.note: Reason necessarily proceeds toward unconditioned unity and totality.

items.text: Idea Formation: unconditioned unity → transcendental idea without adequate possible intuition.

passages.note: Reason's necessary ideas lack objects adequate to possible intuition.

grounding.note: Reason's necessary ideas lack objects adequate to possible intuition.

items.text: Illusion Mechanism: subjective necessity of reason → mistaken objective reality.

passages.note: Necessary rational procedure leads to the unavoidable attribution of objective reality.

grounding.note: Necessary rational procedure leads to the unavoidable attribution of objective reality.

items.text: Paralogistic Operation: “I think” as formal condition → treated as intuition of self → categories applied → soul-doctrine generated.

passages.note: The I think grounds soul doctrine only through illicit category application.
The I think grounds soul doctrine only through illicit category application.

grounding.note: The I think grounds soul doctrine only through illicit category application.

items.text: Critical Interruption: category validity requires intuition → no noumenal self-intuition → metaphysical predicates invalidated.

passages.note: Categories require intuition, while no inner intuition gives a noumenal self.
Categories require intuition, while no inner intuition gives a noumenal self.

grounding.note: Categories require intuition, while no inner intuition gives a noumenal self.

items.text: Residual Discipline: speculative cognition denied → dogmatic negation also denied → practical orientation preserved.

passages.note: Dogmatic affirmation and negation are barred while practical future orientation remains.
Dogmatic affirmation and negation are barred while practical future orientation remains.

grounding.note: Dogmatic affirmation and negation are barred while practical future orientation remains.

items.text: Antinomial Escalation: objective synthesis of phenomena → demand for absolute totality → opposed rational claims → cosmological conflict.

passages.note: Objective phenomenal synthesis yields unconditioned-totality claims and natural antithetic.
Objective phenomenal synthesis yields unconditioned-totality claims and natural antithetic.

grounding.note: Objective phenomenal synthesis yields unconditioned-totality claims and natural antithetic.

items.text: Global Dialectical Machine: lawful rational need → illegitimate transcendental extension → unavoidable illusion → critique as boundary-policing.

passages.note: Lawful rational production becomes unavoidable illusion until critique imposes limits.
Lawful rational production becomes unavoidable illusion until critique imposes limits.

grounding.note: Lawful rational production becomes unavoidable illusion until critique imposes limits.

items.text: Transcendental ideas lack adequate experiential objects → reason nevertheless necessarily produces them.

passages.note: Ideas lack adequate experiential objects yet arise necessarily from reason.

grounding.note: Ideas lack adequate experiential objects yet arise necessarily from reason.

items.text: Necessary production of ideas → unavoidable dialectical sophisms.

passages.note: Necessary reason generates unavoidable sophistical arguments.

grounding.note: Necessary reason generates unavoidable sophistical arguments.

items.text: Three ideas of reason → three dialectical domains: soul, world, God.

passages.note: Three kinds of dialectical arguments correspond to subject, world-totality, and being of all beings.

grounding.note: Three kinds of dialectical arguments correspond to subject, world-totality, and being of all beings.

items.text: Rational psychology selects “I think” as its sole pure datum.

passages.note: I think is explicitly the sole text of rational psychology.

grounding.note: I think is explicitly the sole text of rational psychology.

items.text: “I think” supplies logical unity only → rational psychology treats it as object-giving intuition.

passages.note: Logical unity is mistaken for intuition of the subject as object.
Logical unity is mistaken for intuition of the subject as object.

grounding.note: Logical unity is mistaken for intuition of the subject as object.

items.text: Illicit category-application → claims of substantiality, simplicity, personality, immateriality, immortality.

passages.note: Soul predicates arise from applying categories to unity of apperception.
Soul predicates arise from applying categories to unity of apperception.

grounding.note: Soul predicates arise from applying categories to unity of apperception.

items.text: Critical distinction between logical function and object-cognition → paralogism exposed.

passages.note: Logical thought-functions are distinguished from object-cognition, exposing the equivocation.
Logical thought-functions are distinguished from object-cognition, exposing the equivocation.

grounding.note: Logical thought-functions are distinguished from object-cognition, exposing the equivocation.

items.text: Speculative self-knowledge beyond experience denied → practical supersensible orientation retained.

passages.note: Speculative self-knowledge is refused while practical supersensible orientation remains.
Speculative self-knowledge is refused while practical supersensible orientation remains.

grounding.note: Speculative self-knowledge is refused while practical supersensible orientation remains.

items.text: From subjective unity of apperception → objective totality of phenomena → antinomy of cosmological reason.

passages.note: The dialectic passes from subjective unity to objective conditions in phenomena.

grounding.note: The dialectic passes from subjective unity to objective conditions in phenomena.

items.text: The “soul” is reclassified from object of pure knowledge to product of illicit transcendental inference.

passages.note: Soul-substance is reduced to an illusion from confounding consciousness with object-intuition.
Soul-substance is reduced to an illusion from confounding consciousness with object-intuition.

grounding.note: Soul-substance is reduced to an illusion from confounding consciousness with object-intuition.

items.text: Self-consciousness is split into formal condition of cognition and impossible object of noumenal cognition.

Self-consciousness is a condition of thought but cannot yield noumenal self-cognition.

grounding.note: Self-consciousness is a condition of thought but cannot yield noumenal self-cognition.

items.text: Traditional rational psychology is redrawn as a discipline of limits rather than a doctrine of the soul.

passages.note: Rational psychology is recast as a discipline setting limits to speculative reason.

grounding.note: Rational psychology is recast as a discipline setting limits to speculative reason.

items.text: Substance, simplicity, and identity are relocated from metaphysical predicates of the self to logical features of apperception unless intuition grounds them.

Simplicity and identity are analytic thought-features absent intuition-based substance cognition.

grounding.note: Simplicity and identity are analytic thought-features absent intuition-based substance cognition.

items.text: Dogmatic spiritualism and dogmatic materialism are placed under the same critical prohibition.

passages.note: Materialism and spiritualism are jointly underdetermined and dogmatic assertion is prohibited.
Materialism and spiritualism are jointly underdetermined and dogmatic assertion is prohibited.

grounding.note: Materialism and spiritualism are jointly underdetermined and dogmatic assertion is prohibited.

items.text: Immortality is displaced from speculative proof to practical orientation.

passages.note: Speculative permanence is undemonstrated, while practical future-life orientation remains.
Speculative permanence is undemonstrated, while practical future-life orientation remains.

grounding.note: Speculative permanence is undemonstrated, while practical future-life orientation remains.

items.text: Error becomes structural and transcendental rather than merely logical or psychological.

passages.note: Dialectical error is rooted in pure reason's necessary nature.
Dialectical error is rooted in pure reason's necessary nature.

items.text: The critique of the soul prepares the terrain for the critique of the world by showing how reason’s demand for the unconditioned mutates by domain.

passages.note: The psychological conclusion introduces the transition to cosmological antinomy.
The psychological conclusion introduces the transition to cosmological antinomy.

grounding.note: The psychological conclusion introduces the transition to cosmological antinomy.

items.text: Antinomy becomes visible as reason’s objective self-conflict, not as an accidental disagreement among schools.

Cosmological antithetic is reason's natural and unavoidable contradiction.

items.text: Surface: the text examines paralogisms of rational psychology and introduces antinomies of rational cosmology.

The passages introduce paralogisms of psychology and antinomy of cosmology.

grounding.note: The passages introduce paralogisms of psychology and antinomy of cosmology.

items.text: Structural: it identifies the mechanism by which reason misapplies categories beyond possible intuition.

Categories are invalidly used where no given intuition supplies an object.

grounding.note: Categories are invalidly used where no given intuition supplies an object.

items.text: What remains underdetermined is the positive status of the noumenal self; the system requires it as boundary-concept but cannot describe it.

items.text: The chief tension lies in preserving practical supersensible orientation after denying speculative access to supersensible objects.

items.text: The treatment of immortality depends on a disciplined separation between practical necessity and theoretical knowledge.

passages.note: Theoretical permanence is undemonstrable while future life retains practical standing.

grounding.note: Theoretical permanence is undemonstrable while future life retains practical standing.

items.text: Reconstruction would preserve the text’s real movement if it follows: reason’s necessary idea → illicit objectification → category-boundary critique → speculative renunciation → practical remainder → antinomial escalation.

passages.note: The sequence moves from necessary idea and illicit objectification to critique, practical remainder, and antinomy.
The sequence moves from necessary idea and illicit objectification to critique, practical remainder, and antinomy.

items.text: Problem: pure reason necessarily seeks the unconditioned totality of conditions for phenomena, but such totality cannot be given in possible experience.

passages.note: Reason demands the unconditioned; phenomenal completion is problematic.
Reason demands the unconditioned; phenomenal completion is problematic.

grounding.note: Reason demands the unconditioned; phenomenal completion is problematic.

items.text: Core thesis: cosmological ideas arise when categories are extended regressively beyond empirical limits toward absolute completeness.

passages.note: Categories are elevated regressively to unconditioned ideas.

grounding.note: Categories are elevated regressively to unconditioned ideas.

items.text: Argument type: transcendental-diagnostic; it reconstructs the necessary production of cosmological antinomies from reason’s own demand.

passages.note: Antinomy is diagnosed as reason's unavoidable self-conflict.
Antinomy is diagnosed as reason's unavoidable self-conflict.

grounding.note: Antinomy is diagnosed as reason's unavoidable self-conflict.

items.text: Directional movement: category → regressive series → demand for totality → unconditioned idea → transcendent use → antinomic conflict.

passages.note: Passages trace category, totality, transcendence, and conflict.
Passages trace category, totality, transcendence, and conflict.

grounding.note: Passages trace category, totality, transcendence, and conflict.

items.text: The argument classifies cosmological reason into four serial demands: world-composition, divisibility, causality, and existential dependence.

passages.note: Explicit enumeration of four cosmological ideas.

grounding.note: Explicit enumeration of four cosmological ideas.

items.text: The antithetic procedure suspends dogmatic decision and uses contradiction itself as the diagnostic sign of transcendental illusion.

passages.note: Conflict is staged to discover misunderstanding, not decide.

grounding.note: Conflict is staged to discover misunderstanding, not decide.

items.text: Final operative movement: reason’s need for completion exceeds the understanding’s conditions of possible experience and thereby generates equally necessary opposed claims.

passages.note: Reason's unity exceeds understanding and yields opposed necessities.
Reason's unity exceeds understanding and yields opposed necessities.

grounding.note: Reason's unity exceeds understanding and yields opposed necessities.

items.text: Pure and transcendental conceptions originate from the understanding, not from reason.

passages.note: Pure and transcendental conceptions originate in understanding.

grounding.note: Pure and transcendental conceptions originate in understanding.

items.text: Reason does not create concepts; it frees concepts of the understanding from limitation to possible experience.

passages.note: Reason frees understanding's concepts from experiential limitation.

grounding.note: Reason frees understanding's concepts from experiential limitation.

items.text: For any given conditioned, reason demands the absolute totality of its conditions.

passages.note: Explicit principle concerning a given conditioned.

grounding.note: Explicit principle concerning a given conditioned.

items.text: A category becomes a transcendental idea when reason extends it to the unconditioned.

passages.note: Reason makes the category into a transcendental idea.

grounding.note: Reason makes the category into a transcendental idea.

items.text: Reason’s demand for totality applies only to ascending regressive series of subordinated conditions.

passages.note: Totality concerns ascending regressive condition-series only.
Totality concerns ascending regressive condition-series only.

grounding.note: Totality concerns ascending regressive condition-series only.

items.text: Progressive series of consequences are not necessary demands of reason.

passages.note: Progressive consequence-series are arbitrary, not necessary.
Progressive consequence-series are arbitrary, not necessary.

grounding.note: Progressive consequence-series are arbitrary, not necessary.

items.text: Cosmological ideas concern phenomena only, not things as they may be apart from sensuous intuition.

passages.note: Ideas concern phenomena and not noumena.
Ideas concern phenomena and not noumena.

grounding.note: Ideas concern phenomena and not noumena.

items.text: Phenomena are given only under the conditions of sensibility and through successive synthesis.

passages.note: Phenomenal conditions are given through successive synthesis.

grounding.note: Phenomenal conditions are given through successive synthesis.

items.text: Absolute completeness of phenomenal synthesis is an idea whose empirical possibility remains problematic.

passages.note: Complete phenomenal synthesis remains an idea and problem.
Complete phenomenal synthesis remains an idea and problem.

grounding.note: Complete phenomenal synthesis remains an idea and problem.

items.text: The unconditioned may be conceived either as the totality of an infinite conditioned series or as an unconditioned first member within a series.

passages.note: Explicit distinction between total series and first member.

grounding.note: Explicit distinction between total series and first member.

items.text: Only categories that generate a subordinated series of conditions can yield cosmological ideas.

passages.note: Only subordinated condition-series qualify.

grounding.note: Only subordinated condition-series qualify.

items.text: There are four cosmological ideas: absolute completeness of composition, division, origination, and dependence of existence.

passages.note: Four ideas are explicitly listed.

grounding.note: Four ideas are explicitly listed.

items.text: World signifies the mathematical totality of phenomena; nature signifies their dynamical unity according to causality.

passages.note: World is mathematical; nature is dynamical.

grounding.note: World is mathematical; nature is dynamical.

items.text: Transcendent use of cosmological ideas produces assertions neither confirmable nor refutable by experience.

passages.note: Claims beyond experience admit neither confirmation nor refutation.

grounding.note: Claims beyond experience admit neither confirmation nor refutation.

items.text: Antinomies of pure reason arise naturally and unavoidably from reason’s own principles.

passages.note: Dialectical illusion is natural and unavoidable.

grounding.note: Dialectical illusion is natural and unavoidable.

items.text: Transcendental propositions beyond possible experience lack both empirical test and pure intuitive construction.

passages.note: Transcendental propositions lack intuition and experiential correction.

grounding.note: Transcendental propositions lack intuition and experiential correction.

items.text: The sceptical method in transcendental philosophy lets opposed claims conflict in order to expose the point of misunderstanding.

passages.note: Conflict discloses the point of misunderstanding.

grounding.note: Conflict discloses the point of misunderstanding.

items.text: An infinite given whole would require a completed successive synthesis, which cannot be completed.

passages.note: Infinite elapsed or coexistent whole requires impossible completion.

grounding.note: Infinite elapsed or coexistent whole requires impossible completion.

items.text: Empty time and empty space are not objects but nonentities produced when sensibility is abstracted from phenomena.

passages.note: Void space and time are termed nonentities.

grounding.note: Void space and time are termed nonentities.

items.text: Space is the form of external intuition, not a composite of simple parts.

passages.note: Space is form of intuition, not composite substance.
Space is form of intuition, not composite substance.

grounding.note: Space is form of intuition, not composite substance.

items.text: Matter as phenomenon is divisible according to the divisibility of space.

passages.note: Matter's division follows its spatial phenomenal condition.
Matter's division follows its spatial phenomenal condition.

grounding.note: Matter's division follows its spatial phenomenal condition.

items.text: Nature as possible experience requires lawful causal connection among phenomena.

passages.note: Nature requires causally lawful connected experience.
Nature requires causally lawful connected experience.

grounding.note: Nature requires causally lawful connected experience.

items.text: A causality of freedom would be an absolute spontaneity beginning a series without prior determining cause.

passages.note: Freedom is absolute spontaneity originating a series.

grounding.note: Freedom is absolute spontaneity originating a series.

items.text: Transcendental freedom, if inserted among phenomena as lawless spontaneity, conflicts with the unity of experience.

passages.note: Lawless spontaneity destroys experiential unity.
Lawless spontaneity destroys experiential unity.

grounding.note: Lawless spontaneity destroys experiential unity.

items.text: Change indicates empirical contingency, not pure intellectual contingency.

passages.note: Change proves empirical, not pure categorical, contingency.

grounding.note: Change proves empirical, not pure categorical, contingency.

items.text: A necessary cause of temporal change, if causally connected to phenomena, must itself be related to time.

passages.note: A causally connected necessary cause must belong to time.
A causally connected necessary cause must belong to time.

grounding.note: A causally connected necessary cause must belong to time.

items.text: Reason is not an independent source of pure concepts.

passages.note: Reason does not properly give birth to conceptions.

grounding.note: Reason does not properly give birth to conceptions.

items.text: Cosmological ideas are not empirical concepts.

passages.note: The unconditioned is not found in experience.

grounding.note: The unconditioned is not found in experience.

items.text: The unconditioned is not found in experience.

passages.note: Explicit exclusion of experiential unconditioned.

grounding.note: Explicit exclusion of experiential unconditioned.

items.text: Not every category can become a cosmological idea.

passages.note: Only serial categories are available.

grounding.note: Only serial categories are available.

items.text: Co-ordinated aggregates do not generate reason’s demand for absolute totality.

passages.note: Co-ordinated aggregates are excluded.

grounding.note: Co-ordinated aggregates are excluded.

items.text: Progressive consequence-series are not necessary problems of pure reason.

passages.note: Progressive synthesis is arbitrary, not necessary.

grounding.note: Progressive synthesis is arbitrary, not necessary.

items.text: Substance-accident relations do not form the relevant regressive series.

passages.note: Accidents are co-ordinated, not serially subordinated.

grounding.note: Accidents are co-ordinated, not serially subordinated.

items.text: Community among substances does not form a subordinated series of conditions.

passages.note: Community is an aggregate, not a series.

grounding.note: Community is an aggregate, not a series.

items.text: Cosmological ideas are not directed to noumena.

passages.note: Ideas concern sense-world rather than noumena.

grounding.note: Ideas concern sense-world rather than noumena.

items.text: The world as cosmological object is not a totality of things in themselves.

passages.note: Cosmological totality concerns phenomena, not intelligibles.
Cosmological totality concerns phenomena, not intelligibles.

grounding.note: Cosmological totality concerns phenomena, not intelligibles.

items.text: Antithetic is not dogmatic assertion of the opposite.

passages.note: Antithetic is explicitly distinguished from opposite dogmatism.

grounding.note: Antithetic is explicitly distinguished from opposite dogmatism.

items.text: The sceptical method is not scepticism.

passages.note: Sceptical method is explicitly distinct from scepticism.

grounding.note: Sceptical method is explicitly distinct from scepticism.

items.text: Transcendental conflict cannot be settled by empirical observation.

passages.note: Experience cannot confirm or settle transcendent claims.
Experience cannot confirm or settle transcendent claims.

grounding.note: Experience cannot confirm or settle transcendent claims.

items.text: Transcendental conflict cannot be settled by mathematical construction except where pure intuition applies.

passages.note: No pure intuitive construction is available.

grounding.note: No pure intuitive construction is available.

items.text: Void time before the world is not a possible determining object.

passages.note: Void pre-world time is a nonentity.
Void pre-world time is a nonentity.

grounding.note: Void pre-world time is a nonentity.

items.text: Void space outside the world is not a possible correlate of the world.

passages.note: Void external space lacks a world-correlate.
Void external space lacks a world-correlate.

grounding.note: Void external space lacks a world-correlate.

items.text: Space is not a real thing capable of limiting phenomena from outside.

passages.note: Space is not a self-subsistent determining thing.
Space is not a self-subsistent determining thing.

grounding.note: Space is not a self-subsistent determining thing.

items.text: Matter is not composed of spatially simple parts.

passages.note: No simple spatial part is possible in matter.
No simple spatial part is possible in matter.

grounding.note: No simple spatial part is possible in matter.

items.text: The mathematical point is not a physical part of matter.

passages.note: Point is a spatial limit, not physical part.
Point is a spatial limit, not physical part.

grounding.note: Point is a spatial limit, not physical part.

items.text: The bare representation “I” does not prove the soul’s absolute simplicity as substance in nature.

passages.note: Bare I supplies no proof of real simplicity.

grounding.note: Bare I supplies no proof of real simplicity.

items.text: Transcendental freedom is not identical with the empirical-psychological concept of free will.

passages.note: Transcendental freedom does not exhaust psychological freedom.

grounding.note: Transcendental freedom does not exhaust psychological freedom.

items.text: A law-governed freedom within nature is not freedom but nature.

passages.note: Freedom determined by laws would be nature.

grounding.note: Freedom determined by laws would be nature.

items.text: A lawless freedom within nature cannot ground connected experience.

passages.note: Lawless freedom precludes connected experience.
Lawless freedom precludes connected experience.

grounding.note: Lawless freedom precludes connected experience.

items.text: Empirical change does not prove contingency in the pure category-sense.

passages.note: Succession of states does not prove categorical contingency.

grounding.note: Succession of states does not prove categorical contingency.

items.text: The cosmological proof of a necessary being cannot legitimately become an ontological proof.

passages.note: Cosmological regress cannot saltus into pure categories.
Cosmological regress cannot saltus into pure categories.

grounding.note: Cosmological regress cannot saltus into pure categories.

items.text: A necessary being outside the world cannot be causally connected to temporal phenomena without entering relation to time.

passages.note: External cause must enter temporal phenomenal causality.

grounding.note: External cause must enter temporal phenomenal causality.

items.text: Cosmological reason operates only where a conditioned phenomenon implies an ascending series of conditions.

passages.note: Reason concerns ascending conditions of given phenomena.
Reason concerns ascending conditions of given phenomena.

grounding.note: Reason concerns ascending conditions of given phenomena.

items.text: The table of cosmological ideas is generated by selecting only those categories that yield regressive serial synthesis.

passages.note: Serial-category restriction generates the fourfold table.
Serial-category restriction generates the fourfold table.

grounding.note: Serial-category restriction generates the fourfold table.

items.text: The demand for all past time differs from indifference toward future time because past time conditions the present while future time does not.

passages.note: Past conditions the present; future does not.
Past conditions the present; future does not.

grounding.note: Past conditions the present; future does not.

items.text: Space becomes subject to cosmological regress only through the successive synthesis of its apprehension and limitation, not because its parts are intrinsically subordinated.

passages.note: Spatial regress depends on successive apprehension and limitation.

grounding.note: Spatial regress depends on successive apprehension and limitation.

items.text: Matter generates a divisional cosmological idea because every part functions as condition for the composite real in space.

passages.note: Matter's parts form regressive conditions of the real.

grounding.note: Matter's parts form regressive conditions of the real.

items.text: Causality alone among real relations yields a cosmological idea because only causes form an ascending series toward conditions of an effect.

passages.note: Only causality yields the relevant condition-series.

grounding.note: Only causality yields the relevant condition-series.

items.text: The modal cosmological idea arises only where contingent existence demands ascent toward an unconditioned necessity.

passages.note: Contingent existence ascends toward unconditioned necessity.

grounding.note: Contingent existence ascends toward unconditioned necessity.

items.text: The first antinomy’s thesis follows when an infinite past or infinite spatial whole is treated as requiring completed successive synthesis.

passages.note: Thesis rejects completed infinite successive synthesis.

grounding.note: Thesis rejects completed infinite successive synthesis.

items.text: The first antinomy’s antithesis follows when a beginning or limit is treated as requiring empty time or empty space as boundary.

passages.note: Beginning and limit entail void time or space.
Beginning and limit entail void time or space.

grounding.note: Beginning and limit entail void time or space.

items.text: The second antinomy’s thesis follows when substantial composition is treated as requiring ultimate non-composite constituents.

passages.note: Thesis infers simples from annihilating composition.

grounding.note: Thesis infers simples from annihilating composition.

items.text: The second antinomy’s antithesis follows because no simple part can be given in spatial intuition, since every real in space contains external manifoldness.

passages.note: Spatial real contains manifoldness; simple cannot be given.
Spatial real contains manifoldness; simple cannot be given.

grounding.note: Spatial real contains manifoldness; simple cannot be given.

items.text: The third antinomy’s thesis follows because lawful natural causality alone never yields an absolutely first causal ground.

passages.note: Natural causal regress lacks a real first beginning.

grounding.note: Natural causal regress lacks a real first beginning.

items.text: The third antinomy’s antithesis follows because spontaneous unconditioned causality would interrupt the lawful unity required for experience.

passages.note: Spontaneity interrupts lawful unity of experience.
Spontaneity interrupts lawful unity of experience.

grounding.note: Spontaneity interrupts lawful unity of experience.

items.text: The fourth antinomy’s thesis follows because change requires conditioned succession, and reason demands the unconditioned totality of such conditions.

passages.note: Change supplies the conditioned succession requiring ascent.

grounding.note: Change supplies the conditioned succession requiring ascent.

items.text: The fourth antinomy’s antithesis follows because an unconditioned necessary being cannot be placed either inside the conditioned temporal series or outside it while remaining causally connected to it.

passages.note: Necessary being fits neither world nor external causal role.
Necessary being fits neither world nor external causal role.

grounding.note: Necessary being fits neither world nor external causal role.

items.text: The same rational demand can generate opposed conclusions when totality is considered under different standpoints.

passages.note: Same grounds yield opposed conclusions from differing standpoints.

grounding.note: Same grounds yield opposed conclusions from differing standpoints.

items.text: The antinomy is not accidental error but a structurally necessary self-conflict of reason under transcendent employment.

passages.note: Antinomy is natural and unavoidable under reason's demand.

grounding.note: Antinomy is natural and unavoidable under reason's demand.

items.text: The sceptical method becomes necessary because no external tribunal exists for transcendental claims beyond experience.

passages.note: Beyond experience, only free conflict remains as criterion.

grounding.note: Beyond experience, only free conflict remains as criterion.

items.text: Reason converts the understanding’s categories into cosmological totalities by forcing empirical synthesis to answer a demand it cannot empirically satisfy.

passages.note: Reason elevates categories beyond phenomenally completable synthesis.
Reason elevates categories beyond phenomenally completable synthesis.

grounding.note: Reason elevates categories beyond phenomenally completable synthesis.

items.text: The antinomies are generated by the mismatch between reason’s requirement of absolute completeness and sensibility’s condition that phenomena be given only through incompleteable synthesis.

passages.note: Reason's unity conflicts with successive sensuous givenness.
Reason's unity conflicts with successive sensuous givenness.

grounding.note: Reason's unity conflicts with successive sensuous givenness.

items.text: The world becomes a problem-object: necessarily thought as totality, impossible to exhibit as totality.

passages.note: World-totality is necessarily thought but empirically problematic.
World-totality is necessarily thought but empirically problematic.

grounding.note: World-totality is necessarily thought but empirically problematic.

items.text: The same concept of the unconditioned bifurcates into two opposed models: infinite total conditioned series and first unconditioned member.

passages.note: The two models of unconditioned are explicitly distinguished.

grounding.note: The two models of unconditioned are explicitly distinguished.

items.text: Mathematical cosmology produces contradiction through quantity: the world must be complete, yet its completion would require impossible synthesis.

passages.note: Completion and empty-boundary arguments produce mathematical conflict.
Completion and empty-boundary arguments produce mathematical conflict.

grounding.note: Completion and empty-boundary arguments produce mathematical conflict.

items.text: Dynamical cosmology produces contradiction through causality and necessity: reason demands an unconditioned ground, while experience admits only lawful conditioned connection.

passages.note: Freedom and necessity arise from causal and modal regress.
Freedom and necessity arise from causal and modal regress.

grounding.note: Freedom and necessity arise from causal and modal regress.

items.text: The antithetic method transforms metaphysical dispute from contest over objects into diagnosis of the faculty that produces the dispute.

passages.note: Antithetic investigates reason's conflict and its causes.
Antithetic investigates reason's conflict and its causes.

grounding.note: Antithetic investigates reason's conflict and its causes.

items.text: The concept of nature is preserved only by refusing any lawless insertion of transcendental freedom into the empirical causal series.

passages.note: Lawless intra-natural freedom dissolves nature's lawful unity.
Lawless intra-natural freedom dissolves nature's lawful unity.

grounding.note: Lawless intra-natural freedom dissolves nature's lawful unity.

items.text: The cosmological proof of necessity collapses if it leaves empirical regress for pure categories, because such transition changes the meaning of contingency.

passages.note: Empirical contingency cannot become pure categorical contingency.
Empirical contingency cannot become pure categorical contingency.

grounding.note: Empirical contingency cannot become pure categorical contingency.

items.text: Reason’s self-conflict is not resolved by choosing thesis or antithesis; it is exposed by showing that both arise from illegitimate totalization of phenomena.

passages.note: Method exposes illusion rather than selecting a side.
Method exposes illusion rather than selecting a side.

grounding.note: Method exposes illusion rather than selecting a side.

items.text: There is no legitimate cognition of the world as a completed object outside the conditions of possible experience.

passages.note: Cosmological totality exceeds possible experience.
Cosmological totality exceeds possible experience.

grounding.note: Cosmological totality exceeds possible experience.

items.text: There is no direct intuition of the unconditioned.

passages.note: No a priori intuition exhibits transcendent synthesis.

grounding.note: No a priori intuition exhibits transcendent synthesis.

items.text: There is no empirical regress that can terminate in an object adequate to reason’s demand for absolute totality.

passages.note: Phenomenal regress cannot establish complete synthesis.

grounding.note: Phenomenal regress cannot establish complete synthesis.

items.text: There is no pure rational passage from phenomenal conditioning to noumenal determination.

passages.note: The empirical-to-intellectual transition is inadmissible.

grounding.note: The empirical-to-intellectual transition is inadmissible.

items.text: There is no standpoint from which the cosmological whole can be surveyed as both phenomenon and thing in itself.

passages.note: Phenomenal world and intelligible world cannot be conflated.

grounding.note: Phenomenal world and intelligible world cannot be conflated.

items.text: There is no lawful experience if unconditioned spontaneity is admitted as an intra-phenomenal cause.

passages.note: Intra-phenomenal spontaneity destroys experiential unity.
Intra-phenomenal spontaneity destroys experiential unity.

grounding.note: Intra-phenomenal spontaneity destroys experiential unity.

items.text: There is no demonstrable simple object within possible spatial experience.

passages.note: No absolutely simple object is given in experience.
No absolutely simple object is given in experience.

grounding.note: No absolutely simple object is given in experience.

items.text: There is no valid inference from absence of perceived manifoldness to absolute simplicity.

passages.note: Non-consciousness of manifold proves no simplicity.
Non-consciousness of manifold proves no simplicity.

grounding.note: Non-consciousness of manifold proves no simplicity.

items.text: There is no valid inference from empirical succession of opposite states to pure categorical contingency.

passages.note: Opposite successive states are not contradictory opposites.

grounding.note: Opposite successive states are not contradictory opposites.

items.text: There is no legitimate cosmological proof that determines whether necessary being is world, part of world, or beyond world.

passages.note: Cosmological proof leaves necessary being's status unsettled.
Cosmological proof leaves necessary being's status unsettled.

grounding.note: Cosmological proof leaves necessary being's status unsettled.

items.text: The absent object organizing the chapter is the world as a completed given totality.

passages.note: Completed phenomenal totality is demanded yet cannot be given.
Completed phenomenal totality is demanded yet cannot be given.

grounding.note: Completed phenomenal totality is demanded yet cannot be given.

items.text: The unformalized void is the gap between reason’s need for the unconditioned and sensibility’s inability to present it.

passages.note: Reason's completeness exceeds successive phenomenal synthesis.
Reason's completeness exceeds successive phenomenal synthesis.

grounding.note: Reason's completeness exceeds successive phenomenal synthesis.

items.text: The foreclosed possibility is a metaphysics that could decide cosmological questions while remaining within possible experience.

passages.note: Possible experience supplies no tribunal for such decisions.

grounding.note: Possible experience supplies no tribunal for such decisions.

items.text: The argument depends on the impossibility of treating the conditions of intuition as if they were properties of things in themselves.

passages.note: Sensibility conditions cannot be abstracted without losing phenomena.
Sensibility conditions cannot be abstracted without losing phenomena.

grounding.note: Sensibility conditions cannot be abstracted without losing phenomena.

items.text: The antinomies circle an unavailable tribunal: neither experience, nor mathematics, nor dogmatic reason can adjudicate transcendent cosmological claims.

passages.note: Neither intuition nor experience adjudicates transcendent propositions.

grounding.note: Neither intuition nor experience adjudicates transcendent propositions.

items.text: The deepest denial is that reason’s demand for completion licenses cognition of a completed object.

passages.note: Demanded totality remains an idea beyond cognition.
Demanded totality remains an idea beyond cognition.

grounding.note: Demanded totality remains an idea beyond cognition.

items.text: Category supplied by understanding → reason removes empirical limitation → category becomes idea of unconditioned totality.

passages.note: Explicit sequence from understanding-category to unconditioned idea.

grounding.note: Explicit sequence from understanding-category to unconditioned idea.

items.text: Given conditioned phenomenon → demand for totality of conditions → regressive synthesis → search for unconditioned.

passages.note: Given conditioned initiates regressive search for conditions.
Given conditioned initiates regressive search for conditions.

grounding.note: Given conditioned initiates regressive search for conditions.

items.text: Serial category filter → composition / division / origination / dependence → four cosmological ideas.

passages.note: Eligible serial categories produce the four ideas.

grounding.note: Eligible serial categories produce the four ideas.

items.text: Cosmological idea → transcendent use beyond possible experience → thesis and antithesis each acquire rational necessity.

grounding.note: Transcendence yields equally necessary opposing claims.

items.text: Thesis-machine: demand for completion → infinite regress impossible as completed → finite beginning, simple, freedom, necessity.

The four thesis proofs supply these completion outcomes.
The four thesis proofs supply these completion outcomes.

The four antithesis proofs supply these exclusions.
The four antithesis proofs supply these exclusions.

Phenomena-only focus rejects intellectual saltus.

grounding.note: Phenomena-only focus rejects intellectual saltus.

items.text: Four ideas → transcendent employment → antinomic theses and antitheses → each side internally necessary yet mutually destructive.

Both sides are necessary and mutually contradictory.

grounding.note: Both sides are necessary and mutually contradictory.

items.text: Antinomic conflict → sceptical method → contradiction treated as diagnostic criterion → object of dispute exposed as problematic.

items.text: Mathematical antinomies → totality of world and divisibility of matter → contradiction between completed synthesis and sensuous givenness.

First and second conflicts concern world-totality and matter.

grounding.note: First and second conflicts concern world-totality and matter.

items.text: Dynamical antinomies → freedom and necessity → contradiction between unconditioned ground and lawful empirical connection.

passages.note: Third and fourth conflicts concern freedom and necessity.
Third and fourth conflicts concern freedom and necessity.

grounding.note: Third and fourth conflicts concern freedom and necessity.

items.text: Final position of the chapter-unit → cosmological reason necessarily produces conflict when it treats ideas of totality as cognitions of objects.

passages.note: Transcendent employment necessarily produces antinomy.
Transcendent employment necessarily produces antinomy.

grounding.note: Transcendent employment necessarily produces antinomy.

items.text: Cosmology is reclassified from doctrine of the world-object into critique of reason’s demand for totality.

Dogmatic empiricism and dogmatic cosmological answers are rejected.

items.text: Cosmological ideas arise necessarily from reason’s demand for the unconditioned totality of conditioned empirical synthesis.

grounding.note: Possible experience alone gives concepts reality and object-relation.

grounding.note: Objects in space and time are real phenomena, not things in themselves.

items.text: Cosmological ideas are not arbitrary fictions.

Objective speculative cognition requires experience, not practical hopes or familiarity.

grounding.note: Finite and infinite world alternatives are each inadequate to empirical conception.

items.text: Freedom is not available as an empirical event; natural necessity is not available as an absolute totality.

Formal transcendental idealism is distinguished from empirical idealism.

grounding.note: Partisan interest is inadequate; sceptical conflict summons critical inquiry.

grounding.note: Idealism preserves empirical reality while denying self-subsistent appearances.

items.text: The system requires that the unconditioned totality of appearances not be an independently given object.
