items.text: The deepest exclusion is transcendental realism: the assumption that appearances, space, time, and the world-series subsist independently as objects in themselves.

passages.note: Transcendental realism identifies appearances with self-subsisting things.

grounding.note: Transcendental realism identifies appearances with self-subsisting things.

items.text: Conditioned empirical synthesis → reason demands unconditioned totality → cosmological idea.

passages.note: Conditioned synthesis necessarily leads reason to cosmological ideas.

grounding.note: Conditioned synthesis necessarily leads reason to cosmological ideas.

items.text: Cosmological idea + transcendental realist assumption → absolute world-object demanded.

passages.note: Treating appearances as self-subsistent makes absolute world-totality appear objective.
Treating appearances as self-subsistent makes absolute world-totality appear objective.

grounding.note: Treating appearances as self-subsistent makes absolute world-totality appear objective.

items.text: Absolute world-object + empirical categories → thesis/antithesis contradiction.

passages.note: World-totality under empirical regress yields opposed, inadequate alternatives.
World-totality under empirical regress yields opposed, inadequate alternatives.

grounding.note: World-totality under empirical regress yields opposed, inadequate alternatives.

items.text: Thesis-branch: unconditioned terminus posited → practical support + architectonic closure + speculative overreach.

passages.note: Thesis supplies practical foundations and unconditioned completion.
Thesis supplies practical foundations and unconditioned completion.

grounding.note: Thesis supplies practical foundations and unconditioned completion.

items.text: Antithesis-branch: endless empirical regress enforced → speculative discipline + loss of closure + possible dogmatic denial.

passages.note: Empiricism maintains endless inquiry and becomes wrongful only as dogmatic denial.
Empiricism maintains endless inquiry and becomes wrongful only as dogmatic denial.

grounding.note: Empiricism maintains endless inquiry and becomes wrongful only as dogmatic denial.

items.text: Sceptical exposure: each dogmatic answer is too large or too small for possible empirical conception.

passages.note: Each dogmatic answer is too great or too small for empirical conception.
Each dogmatic answer is too great or too small for empirical conception.

grounding.note: Each dogmatic answer is too great or too small for empirical conception.

items.text: Critical demand: because the problem arises from reason’s own idea, reason must diagnose its own question-form.

passages.note: Reason must seek the failure's cause in its own idea.
Reason must seek the failure's cause in its own idea.

grounding.note: Reason must seek the failure's cause in its own idea.

items.text: Transcendental-idealist key: appearances are real only within possible experience and not things in themselves.

passages.note: Appearances are real only in experience and are not things in themselves.
Appearances are real only in experience and are not things in themselves.

grounding.note: Appearances are real only in experience and are not things in themselves.

items.text: Resolution: the absolute totality of appearances is not a given object; antinomic alternatives lose constitutive force.

passages.note: Critical idealism rejects the idea's treatment as an empirically given absolute object.
Critical idealism rejects the idea's treatment as an empirically given absolute object.

grounding.note: Critical idealism rejects the idea's treatment as an empirically given absolute object.

items.text: Necessary cosmological ideas → no adequate possible experience → unavoidable antinomy.

passages.note: Necessary ideas lacking experiential objects generate unavoidable antinomy.
Necessary ideas lacking experiential objects generate unavoidable antinomy.

grounding.note: Necessary ideas lacking experiential objects generate unavoidable antinomy.

items.text: Antinomy → comparison of rational interests → thesis as dogmatic-practical-architectonic, antithesis as empiricist-speculative.

passages.note: The passages distinguish dogmatic practical interests from empiricist speculative interests.
The passages distinguish dogmatic practical interests from empiricist speculative interests.

grounding.note: The passages distinguish dogmatic practical interests from empiricist speculative interests.

items.text: Interest-analysis → exposure of illegitimate partisanship → need for critical rather than dogmatic decision.

passages.note: Interest cannot decide the conflict; impartial trial is required.
Interest cannot decide the conflict; impartial trial is required.

grounding.note: Interest cannot decide the conflict; impartial trial is required.

items.text: Critical obligation → cosmological questions must be answerable from the idea because their object is possible experience as total synthesis.

passages.note: Cosmological questions concern possible experience as total synthesis and require answer.

grounding.note: Cosmological questions concern possible experience as total synthesis and require answer.

items.text: Sceptical exposition → every dogmatic answer exceeds or falls short of empirical conception.

passages.note: The alternatives are shown to exceed or fall short of empirical conception.
The alternatives are shown to exceed or fall short of empirical conception.

grounding.note: The alternatives are shown to exceed or fall short of empirical conception.

items.text: Failure of both alternatives → suspicion of false presupposition concerning the object of cosmological ideas.

passages.note: Sceptical failure prompts suspicion of a false conception of the object.
Sceptical failure prompts suspicion of a false conception of the object.

grounding.note: Sceptical failure prompts suspicion of a false conception of the object.

items.text: False presupposition → transcendental realism identified.

passages.note: The transcendental realist explicitly treats representations as things in themselves.

grounding.note: The transcendental realist explicitly treats representations as things in themselves.

items.text: Transcendental idealism → appearances empirically real but transcendentally ideal → dissolution of cosmological dialectic.

passages.note: Transcendental idealism preserves empirical reality while displacing self-subsistence.
Transcendental idealism preserves empirical reality while displacing self-subsistence.

grounding.note: Transcendental idealism preserves empirical reality while displacing self-subsistence.

items.text: Cosmological contradiction is relocated from the world to reason’s misapplication of its own ideas.

passages.note: The failure is traced to the idea and its cognitive basis, not the world itself.
The failure is traced to the idea and its cognitive basis, not the world itself.

grounding.note: The failure is traced to the idea and its cognitive basis, not the world itself.

items.text: The thesis/antithesis opposition is reclassified as a conflict of rational interests rather than a direct contest between known objects.

passages.note: Thesis and antithesis are compared through their rational interests and principles.
Thesis and antithesis are compared through their rational interests and principles.

grounding.note: Thesis and antithesis are compared through their rational interests and principles.

items.text: Dogmatism and empiricism cease to be simple truth-options and become legitimate or illegitimate depending on their use.

passages.note: Empiricism is legitimate as maxim and illegitimate when dogmatized.

grounding.note: Empiricism is legitimate as maxim and illegitimate when dogmatized.

items.text: Practical interest is separated from speculative proof.

passages.note: Practical interest cannot be treated as speculative advancement.

grounding.note: Practical interest cannot be treated as speculative advancement.

items.text: Empirical reality is detached from thing-in-itself reality.

passages.note: Empirical reality is affirmed while thing-in-itself reality is denied to appearances.

grounding.note: Empirical reality is affirmed while thing-in-itself reality is denied to appearances.

items.text: The world-whole is reclassified from object to regulative idea of possible empirical synthesis.

passages.note: World-totality is treated as an idea concerning synthesis, not an empirical object.
World-totality is treated as an idea concerning synthesis, not an empirical object.

grounding.note: World-totality is treated as an idea concerning synthesis, not an empirical object.

items.text: Ignorance of things in themselves becomes a boundary of cognition, not a warrant for either affirmation or denial.

passages.note: Unknown transcendental objects cannot license either cognition or dogmatic denial.
Unknown transcendental objects cannot license either cognition or dogmatic denial.

grounding.note: Unknown transcendental objects cannot license either cognition or dogmatic denial.

items.text: Possible experience becomes the tribunal for objective validity of speculative concepts.

passages.note: Possible experience alone gives concepts reality and object-relation.

grounding.note: Possible experience alone gives concepts reality and object-relation.

items.text: Scepticism becomes methodological catharsis rather than final negation.

passages.note: Sceptical method is described as a cathartic establishing criticism.

grounding.note: Sceptical method is described as a cathartic establishing criticism.

items.text: Transcendental idealism becomes not an optional doctrine but the condition for resolving the antinomy.

passages.note: The section explicitly names transcendental idealism as the key to solution.

grounding.note: The section explicitly names transcendental idealism as the key to solution.

items.text: Surface: reason confronts contradictory answers to whether the world has a beginning, spatial limit, simple parts, freedom, and necessary being.

passages.note: The four clusters of cosmological alternatives are explicitly enumerated.
The four clusters of cosmological alternatives are explicitly enumerated.

grounding.note: The four clusters of cosmological alternatives are explicitly enumerated.

items.text: Structural: antinomy arises from applying categories and empirical regress to the absolute totality of appearances as if it were a determinate object.

passages.note: Absolute totality is imposed on empirical regress and yields contradiction.
Absolute totality is imposed on empirical regress and yields contradiction.

grounding.note: Absolute totality is imposed on empirical regress and yields contradiction.

items.text: Metacritical: the task shifts from choosing between thesis and antithesis to diagnosing the conditions under which the question becomes contradictory.

passages.note: The task becomes critical inquiry into the question's cognitive presupposition.
The task becomes critical inquiry into the question's cognitive presupposition.

grounding.note: The task becomes critical inquiry into the question's cognitive presupposition.

items.text: Epistemic: objective cognition is restricted to possible experience; ideas of reason regulate inquiry but do not constitute objects.

passages.note: Experience sets objective validity; cosmological ideas lack constitutive object-relation.
Experience sets objective validity; cosmological ideas lack constitutive object-relation.

grounding.note: Experience sets objective validity; cosmological ideas lack constitutive object-relation.

items.text: Practical: morality and religion are shown to have interests endangered by dogmatic empiricism but not secured by speculative dogmatism.

passages.note: Dogmatic thesis appears to support morality while dogmatic empiricism injures practical interest.
Dogmatic thesis appears to support morality while dogmatic empiricism injures practical interest.

grounding.note: Dogmatic thesis appears to support morality while dogmatic empiricism injures practical interest.

items.text: Ontological: appearances are empirically real representations, not self-subsistent things in themselves.

passages.note: Appearances are representations, empirically real but not self-subsistent.
Appearances are representations, empirically real but not self-subsistent.

grounding.note: Appearances are representations, empirically real but not self-subsistent.

items.text: Temporal: past, future, and distant objects are real only as possible continuations within lawful experience, not as completed totalities given outside experience.

passages.note: Past and distant objects are real only through possible experiential progression.
Past and distant objects are real only through possible experiential progression.

grounding.note: Past and distant objects are real only through possible experiential progression.

items.text: Systemic: reason’s architectonic demand for unity is necessary for system-building yet produces illusion when treated as cognition of totality.

passages.note: Architectonic unity is necessary yet its totalizing employment creates antinomy.
Architectonic unity is necessary yet its totalizing employment creates antinomy.

grounding.note: Architectonic unity is necessary yet its totalizing employment creates antinomy.

items.text: The axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the chapter’s core machine: cosmological idea → antinomy → interest-analysis → critical obligation → transcendental-idealist solution.

passages.note: The section sequence supplies the stated core argumentative machine.
The section sequence supplies the stated core argumentative machine.
The section sequence supplies the stated core argumentative machine.
The section sequence supplies the stated core argumentative machine.

grounding.note: The section sequence supplies the stated core argumentative machine.

items.text: The reconstruction depends centrally on the distinction between empirical reality and transcendental ideality.

passages.note: Empirical reality and transcendental ideality are jointly stated.

grounding.note: Empirical reality and transcendental ideality are jointly stated.

items.text: What remains underdetermined is the full positive solution of each antinomy; this unit prepares the key rather than executing every resolution.

passages.note: The supplied text introduces transcendental idealism as the key without completing individual resolutions.

grounding.note: The supplied text introduces transcendental idealism as the key without completing individual resolutions.

items.text: The structure is internally coherent if possible experience is accepted as the sole standard of speculative objective validity.

passages.note: Possible experience is stated as the sole source of conceptual reality.

grounding.note: Possible experience is stated as the sole source of conceptual reality.

items.text: The strongest point is the exposure of both thesis and antithesis as sharing the same false object-presupposition.

passages.note: Both alternatives motivate exposure of the shared false object-conception.
Both alternatives motivate exposure of the shared false object-conception.

grounding.note: Both alternatives motivate exposure of the shared false object-conception.

items.text: The main fault line is the tension between practical reason’s dependence on thesis-like supports and critique’s refusal to grant those supports speculative validity.

passages.note: Practical supports are associated with thesis, but speculative use is criticized.
Practical supports are associated with thesis, but speculative use is criticized.

grounding.note: Practical supports are associated with thesis, but speculative use is criticized.

items.text: A secondary tension lies in demanding complete answers to cosmological questions while redefining satisfactory answer as critical dissolution rather than dogmatic determination.

passages.note: A complete answer is required, yet it is critical rather than dogmatic.
A complete answer is required, yet it is critical rather than dogmatic.

grounding.note: A complete answer is required, yet it is critical rather than dogmatic.

items.text: Reconstruction from these items would preserve the real movement of the text, provided “solution” is understood as transcendental diagnosis, not metaphysical settlement.

passages.note: Solution proceeds through transcendental diagnosis, not objective dogmatic settlement.
Solution proceeds through transcendental diagnosis, not objective dogmatic settlement.

grounding.note: Solution proceeds through transcendental diagnosis, not objective dogmatic settlement.

items.text: Problem: pure reason generates cosmological antinomies by demanding absolute totality in the series of conditions for given phenomena.

passages.note: The dialectical argument demands the whole series and absolute totality of conditions.

grounding.note: The dialectical argument demands the whole series and absolute totality of conditions.

items.text: Diagnosis: the antinomy rests on equivocation between conditioned objects as things in themselves and conditioned objects as phenomena.

passages.note: The passage identifies equivocation between transcendental and empirical meanings of conditioned.

grounding.note: The passage identifies equivocation between transcendental and empirical meanings of conditioned.

items.text: Critical move: the demand for totality is legitimate only as a rule for empirical regress, not as cognition of an object given in itself.

passages.note: Totality is valid only as a rule for empirical regress, not as an object-constituting axiom.

grounding.note: Totality is valid only as a rule for empirical regress, not as an object-constituting axiom.

items.text: Mathematical antinomies are dissolved by denying that the world-whole is given as either finite or infinite in itself.

passages.note: The world is denied as a finite or infinite whole existing in itself.

grounding.note: The world is denied as a finite or infinite whole existing in itself.

items.text: Dynamical antinomies are resolved by distinguishing empirical conditions within phenomena from intelligible conditions outside the phenomenal series.

passages.note: Dynamical series admit an intelligible heterogeneous condition outside the phenomenal series.

grounding.note: Dynamical series admit an intelligible heterogeneous condition outside the phenomenal series.

items.text: Final position: reason’s cosmological ideas have no constitutive use for objects, but retain regulative force for extending experience and limiting dogmatism.

passages.note: Reason is non-constitutive but regulative for the continued extension of experience.
Reason is non-constitutive but regulative for the continued extension of experience.

grounding.note: Reason is non-constitutive but regulative for the continued extension of experience.

items.text: If the conditioned is given, reason requires a regress to its conditions.

passages.note: A given conditioned analytically requires regress to its conditions.

grounding.note: A given conditioned analytically requires regress to its conditions.

items.text: A required regress to conditions does not entail that the complete series of conditions is already given.

passages.note: Phenomenal regress is required without all conditions being already given.

grounding.note: Phenomenal regress is required without all conditions being already given.

items.text: If conditioned and condition are things in themselves, the complete series of conditions is given with the conditioned.

passages.note: For things in themselves, the whole conditional series is given with the conditioned.

grounding.note: For things in themselves, the whole conditional series is given with the conditioned.

items.text: Phenomena are not things in themselves but empirical representations given only through intuition and apprehension.

passages.note: Phenomena are described as empirical representations given only in empirical synthesis.

grounding.note: Phenomena are described as empirical representations given only in empirical synthesis.

items.text: Phenomenal conditions are given only through successive empirical regress.

passages.note: Phenomenal conditions can be established only through actual successive regress.

grounding.note: Phenomenal conditions can be established only through actual successive regress.

items.text: Absolute totality cannot be predicated of a phenomenal series as an object existing in itself.

passages.note: The phenomenal world is never a completely given unconditioned whole.

grounding.note: The phenomenal world is never a completely given unconditioned whole.

items.text: The cosmological syllogism is fallacious because its major uses “conditioned” transcendentally while its minor applies it empirically.

passages.note: The major is transcendental while the minor is empirical, producing sophisma figurae dictionis.

grounding.note: The major is transcendental while the minor is empirical, producing sophisma figurae dictionis.

items.text: Opposed cosmological judgements may both be false when they presuppose an invalid condition.

passages.note: Dialectically opposed judgments can both be false when the world is not given in itself.

grounding.note: Dialectically opposed judgments can both be false when the world is not given in itself.

items.text: The world as totality of phenomena is not given as a whole in intuition.

passages.note: We have a conception of the universe but no intuition of it as a whole.

grounding.note: We have a conception of the universe but no intuition of it as a whole.

items.text: Reason’s cosmological principle is regulative when it prescribes continued regress; it is false when treated as constitutive of an object.

passages.note: The principle regulates regress and is false when treated as constitutive objective reality.

grounding.note: The principle regulates regress and is false when treated as constitutive objective reality.

items.text: No empirical regress may terminate in an absolutely unconditioned phenomenal member.

passages.note: Every empirical condition remains conditioned, requiring continued search for a higher member.

grounding.note: Every empirical condition remains conditioned, requiring continued search for a higher member.

items.text: Mathematical cosmological series admit only homogeneous phenomenal conditions.

passages.note: Only sensuous conditions that belong to the series are admissible in mathematical series.

grounding.note: Only sensuous conditions that belong to the series are admissible in mathematical series.

items.text: Dynamical cosmological series may allow a heterogeneous intelligible condition not belonging to the phenomenal series.

passages.note: Dynamical series admit a heterogeneous intelligible condition beyond the series.

grounding.note: Dynamical series admit a heterogeneous intelligible condition beyond the series.

items.text: Natural necessity governs all events insofar as they are phenomena.

passages.note: Natural causality is an exceptionless law governing every phenomenon.

grounding.note: Natural causality is an exceptionless law governing every phenomenon.

items.text: Freedom, if thinkable, is intelligible causality capable of originating a phenomenal series without itself being temporally conditioned.

passages.note: Intelligible reason originates a phenomenal series while remaining beyond time-conditioned causality.

grounding.note: Intelligible reason originates a phenomenal series while remaining beyond time-conditioned causality.

items.text: An intelligible necessary being, if thinkable, is not a member of the empirical series but a non-empirical ground of the series.

passages.note: A necessary being is a non-empirical intelligible condition, not a series-member.

grounding.note: A necessary being is a non-empirical intelligible condition, not a series-member.

items.text: The intelligible ground of phenomena may be thought but not cognized or determined by predicates of experience.

passages.note: The intelligible character must be thought but cannot be immediately cognized.

grounding.note: The intelligible character must be thought but cannot be immediately cognized.

items.text: Critical reason can prove the non-contradiction of nature with freedom or intelligible necessity, but not the actuality of freedom or a necessary being.

passages.note: The passages deny proof of actuality while affirming non-opposition and consistency.
The passages deny proof of actuality while affirming non-opposition and consistency.

grounding.note: The passages deny proof of actuality while affirming non-opposition and consistency.

items.text: The regress required by reason is not the possession of a completed totality.

passages.note: Required regress does not authorize inference to a given absolute totality.

grounding.note: Required regress does not authorize inference to a given absolute totality.

items.text: Phenomena are not self-subsistent things.

passages.note: Phenomena are mere representations rather than things in themselves.

grounding.note: Phenomena are mere representations rather than things in themselves.

items.text: The world is not an object given as a completed whole prior to regress.

passages.note: The world exists only in empirical regress, not independently as a whole.

grounding.note: The world exists only in empirical regress, not independently as a whole.

items.text: The cosmological antinomies are not resolved by proving one dogmatic side victorious.

passages.note: Both sides are dismissed as claims lacking grounds rather than one side being established.

grounding.note: Both sides are dismissed as claims lacking grounds rather than one side being established.

items.text: Dialectical opposition is not analytic contradiction.

passages.note: The passage distinguishes dialectical opposition from analytical contradiction.

grounding.note: The passage distinguishes dialectical opposition from analytical contradiction.

items.text: The world is not finite in itself.

passages.note: The world is neither a finite whole in itself nor a thing in itself.

grounding.note: The world is neither a finite whole in itself nor a thing in itself.

items.text: The world is not infinite in itself.

passages.note: The world is neither an infinite whole in itself nor a thing in itself.

grounding.note: The world is neither an infinite whole in itself nor a thing in itself.

items.text: The empirical regress is not a constitutive determination of the object.

passages.note: Regress is a rule for proceeding, not a constitutive determination of an object.

grounding.note: Regress is a rule for proceeding, not a constitutive determination of an object.

items.text: The regulative principle does not disclose what the object is.

passages.note: The rule says only how to proceed, not what the object is.

grounding.note: The rule says only how to proceed, not what the object is.

items.text: The unconditioned cannot be found as an empirical object.

passages.note: The absolutely unconditioned cannot be discovered in experience.

grounding.note: The absolutely unconditioned cannot be discovered in experience.

items.text: Infinite divisibility does not mean that a body consists of an actually infinite number of parts.

passages.note: Infinite division does not establish an actually infinite aggregate of parts.

grounding.note: Infinite division does not establish an actually infinite aggregate of parts.

items.text: Freedom is not an exception inserted into the chain of phenomenal causality.

passages.note: Free intelligible causality and natural phenomenal causality coexist in the same action.

grounding.note: Free intelligible causality and natural phenomenal causality coexist in the same action.

items.text: Natural causality is not abolished by intelligible causality.

passages.note: Natural necessity remains complete even where intelligible freedom is considered.

grounding.note: Natural necessity remains complete even where intelligible freedom is considered.

items.text: Moral imputation is not grounded in empirical causation alone.

passages.note: Blame is grounded in reason's independent causality despite empirical determining conditions.

grounding.note: Blame is grounded in reason's independent causality despite empirical determining conditions.

items.text: The necessary being is not an empirical first member of the series.

passages.note: The necessary being is expressly denied membership, including highest membership, in the series.

grounding.note: The necessary being is expressly denied membership, including highest membership, in the series.

items.text: The intelligible is not available as an explanatory object within experience.

passages.note: The intelligible is not available for empirical explanation or exposition.

grounding.note: The intelligible is not available for empirical explanation or exposition.

items.text: The antinomy arises when a logical demand for conditions is converted into an ontological possession of totality.

passages.note: The demand for regress becomes illicit only when phenomenal conditions are treated as already given totality.
The demand for regress becomes illicit only when phenomenal conditions are treated as already given totality.

grounding.note: The demand for regress becomes illicit only when phenomenal conditions are treated as already given totality.

items.text: The cosmological syllogism is valid for things in themselves but invalid for phenomena.

passages.note: The inference holds for things in themselves but becomes fallacious when applied to phenomena.
The inference holds for things in themselves but becomes fallacious when applied to phenomena.

grounding.note: The inference holds for things in themselves but becomes fallacious when applied to phenomena.

items.text: The world cannot be judged as finite or infinite because such predicates require the world to be given as an object in itself.

passages.note: Finite and infinite predicates require the world to be a thing in itself.

grounding.note: Finite and infinite predicates require the world to be a thing in itself.

items.text: The failure of both opposed mathematical cosmological claims indirectly supports transcendental ideality.

passages.note: The failure of finite and infinite alternatives is presented as indirect proof of transcendental ideality.

grounding.note: The failure of finite and infinite alternatives is presented as indirect proof of transcendental ideality.

items.text: Reason retains authority only as a rule of inquiry, not as a source of supersensible object-knowledge.

passages.note: Reason provides a rule of regress but no information about a supersensible object.

grounding.note: Reason provides a rule of regress but no information about a supersensible object.

items.text: The empirical regress must always continue wherever no empirical limit is given.

passages.note: Absent an empirical limit, each condition requires search for a higher condition.

grounding.note: Absent an empirical limit, each condition requires search for a higher condition.

items.text: Regress in cosmical magnitude is indefinite, not infinite, because the world-whole is not given in intuition.

passages.note: Cosmical regress is called indefinitum because the world-whole is not given in intuition.

grounding.note: Cosmical regress is called indefinitum because the world-whole is not given in intuition.

items.text: Regress in the division of a given continuum proceeds to infinity because the whole is given in intuition and its parts are conditions internal to it.

passages.note: Division proceeds in infinitum because the whole and its internal parts are given together in intuition.

grounding.note: Division proceeds in infinitum because the whole and its internal parts are given together in intuition.

items.text: Mathematical antinomies must be dissolved by denying the shared presupposition of a world-whole existing in itself.

passages.note: Mathematical antinomy disappears by rejecting the world as a whole existing in itself.

grounding.note: Mathematical antinomy disappears by rejecting the world as a whole existing in itself.

items.text: Dynamical antinomies admit reconciliation because condition and conditioned need not be homogeneous members of one phenomenal series.

passages.note: Dynamical reconciliation follows from heterogeneous intelligible conditions outside the phenomenal series.

grounding.note: Dynamical reconciliation follows from heterogeneous intelligible conditions outside the phenomenal series.

items.text: The same action can be naturally necessary as phenomenon and free as grounded in intelligible causality.

passages.note: One action is naturally necessary as phenomenon and free relative to intelligible causality.

grounding.note: One action is naturally necessary as phenomenon and free relative to intelligible causality.

items.text: Practical freedom depends on the thinkability of transcendental freedom.

passages.note: Practical freedom is stated to be based on the transcendental idea of freedom.

grounding.note: Practical freedom is stated to be based on the transcendental idea of freedom.

items.text: Moral responsibility presupposes that reason can be thought as a complete causal ground independent of sensuous determination.

passages.note: Imputation presupposes reason as a complete cause able to determine conduct independently of empirical conditions.

grounding.note: Imputation presupposes reason as a complete cause able to determine conduct independently of empirical conditions.

items.text: A necessary being may be thought without interrupting empirical regress because it is not an empirical member of that regress.

passages.note: A necessary intelligible being does not interrupt the empirical series because it is not within it.

grounding.note: A necessary intelligible being does not interrupt the empirical series because it is not within it.

items.text: Empirical science remains intact because intelligible grounds neither replace nor suspend phenomenal causal laws.

passages.note: Physical explanation continues fully under empirical causal laws despite intelligible grounds.

grounding.note: Physical explanation continues fully under empirical causal laws despite intelligible grounds.

items.text: The critical solution converts cosmological metaphysics from object-assertion into rule-governed inquiry.

passages.note: The chapter converts constitutive cosmological assertion into a regulative rule of inquiry.
The chapter converts constitutive cosmological assertion into a regulative rule of inquiry.

grounding.note: The chapter converts constitutive cosmological assertion into a regulative rule of inquiry.

items.text: Antinomy becomes a diagnostic instrument: reason’s self-conflict exposes the illegitimate reification of phenomena.

passages.note: Antinomy exposes the false initial supposition that phenomena are things in themselves.
Antinomy exposes the false initial supposition that phenomena are things in themselves.

grounding.note: Antinomy exposes the false initial supposition that phenomena are things in themselves.

items.text: Transcendental idealism functions as the only architecture in which reason’s demand for the unconditioned and understanding’s demand for empirical law can coexist.

passages.note: Phenomenal lawfulness and intelligible freedom coexist only when phenomena are not things in themselves.
Phenomenal lawfulness and intelligible freedom coexist only when phenomena are not things in themselves.

grounding.note: Phenomenal lawfulness and intelligible freedom coexist only when phenomena are not things in themselves.

items.text: The mathematical/dynamical distinction reorganizes the antinomy: homogeneous series require dissolution, heterogeneous series permit reconciliation.

passages.note: Homogeneous mathematical series yield dismissal, while heterogeneous dynamical series permit reconciliation.
Homogeneous mathematical series yield dismissal, while heterogeneous dynamical series permit reconciliation.

grounding.note: Homogeneous mathematical series yield dismissal, while heterogeneous dynamical series permit reconciliation.

items.text: The unconditioned is displaced from empirical discoverability to intelligible thinkability.

passages.note: The unconditioned is unavailable in experience but can be posited as intelligible condition.
The unconditioned is unavailable in experience but can be posited as intelligible condition.

grounding.note: The unconditioned is unavailable in experience but can be posited as intelligible condition.

items.text: Freedom is preserved not by weakening natural necessity, but by relocating causality across two registers.

passages.note: Freedom is made compatible with natural necessity by distinguishing intelligible and phenomenal relations.

grounding.note: Freedom is made compatible with natural necessity by distinguishing intelligible and phenomenal relations.

items.text: The necessary being is protected from empirical refutation only by being denied empirical determinability.

passages.note: Empirical contingency cannot decide the possibility or impossibility of an intelligible necessary being.

grounding.note: Empirical contingency cannot decide the possibility or impossibility of an intelligible necessary being.

items.text: Critical limitation has a double edge: it blocks dogmatic metaphysics and blocks dogmatic empiricism.

passages.note: Reason is bounded against transcendent theories and empirical understanding against denying the intelligible.

grounding.note: Reason is bounded against transcendent theories and empirical understanding against denying the intelligible.

items.text: It must not be true that phenomena are things in themselves.

passages.note: The passage rejects treating phenomena as things in themselves.

grounding.note: The passage rejects treating phenomena as things in themselves.

items.text: It must not be true that the complete world-series is given independently of empirical synthesis.

grounding.note: Physico-theology is insufficient alone and recurs to cosmological reasoning.

items.text: Experience does not disclose absolute necessity.

passages.note: Nothing empirically given can be absolutely necessary.

grounding.note: Nothing empirically given can be absolutely necessary.

items.text: The empirical regress of causes does not license passage to a transcendent first cause.

passages.note: An empirical causal regress cannot validly infer a first cause beyond experience.

grounding.note: An empirical causal regress cannot validly infer a first cause beyond experience.

items.text: The impossibility of completing an infinite empirical regress does not prove an absolutely necessary being.

passages.note: The inference from an allegedly impossible infinite regress is rejected.

grounding.note: The inference from an allegedly impossible infinite regress is rejected.

items.text: The absence of contradiction in a concept is not equivalent to transcendental possibility.

passages.note: Logical non-contradiction is distinguished from transcendental possibility.

grounding.note: Logical non-contradiction is distinguished from transcendental possibility.

items.text: The totality of reality as concept is not thereby an existing object.

passages.note: A concept does not establish the existence of its object.

grounding.note: A concept does not establish the existence of its object.

items.text: The Supreme Being is not a member of the empirical causal chain.

passages.note: As an empirical-series member, the Supreme Being would itself require a condition.

grounding.note: As an empirical-series member, the Supreme Being would itself require a condition.

items.text: The Supreme Being cannot be inferred as an empirical cause without becoming conditioned.

passages.note: An intelligible cause cannot be connected by empirical causal laws.

grounding.note: An intelligible cause cannot be connected by empirical causal laws.

items.text: Natural order does not prove a creator of matter.

passages.note: Natural order concerns the world's form, not the production of matter.

grounding.note: Natural order concerns the world's form, not the production of matter.

items.text: Design proves, at most, an architect proportioned to the world’s form, not an all-sufficient creator of the world’s substance.

passages.note: The argument proves only an architect limited by material.

grounding.note: The argument proves only an architect limited by material.

items.text: The predicates “immense,” “astonishing,” and “immeasurable” do not yield a determinate concept of divine perfection.

passages.note: Such predicates merely express observer-relative praise, not determinate perfection.

grounding.note: Such predicates merely express observer-relative praise, not determinate perfection.

items.text: Speculative theology is not the ground of religion unless joined to practical reason.

passages.note: Rational theology requires grounding in moral laws.

grounding.note: Rational theology requires grounding in moral laws.

items.text: Deistic cognition of a primal being is not yet determinate theistic cognition of a living, intelligent author.

passages.note: Deism yields an indeterminate primal cause; theism affirms an intelligent author.
Deism yields an indeterminate primal cause; theism affirms an intelligent author.

grounding.note: Deism yields an indeterminate primal cause; theism affirms an intelligent author.

items.text: The limits of speculative reason do not authorize atheistic demonstration.

passages.note: Arguments barring affirmation equally bar speculative denial.

grounding.note: Arguments barring affirmation equally bar speculative denial.

items.text: The cosmological proof begins with experience but abandons experience when it must determine the necessary being.

passages.note: The proof starts from experience but leaves it to determine necessity.

grounding.note: The proof starts from experience but leaves it to determine necessity.

items.text: The cosmological proof gains its apparent force only by smuggling in the ontological inference it claims to avoid.

passages.note: Its ostensible experiential basis conceals ontological reasoning.

grounding.note: Its ostensible experiential basis conceals ontological reasoning.

items.text: If every absolutely necessary being is identified with the ens realissimum, then conversion yields that the ens realissimum is necessary, reproducing the ontological proof.

passages.note: Conversion of the necessity proposition makes every ens realissimum necessary.

grounding.note: Conversion of the necessity proposition makes every ens realissimum necessary.

items.text: The transcendental use of causality outside experience is meaningless, not merely unverified.

passages.note: Causality beyond possible experience is called useless and meaningless.

grounding.note: Causality beyond possible experience is called useless and meaningless.

items.text: Reason must seek a necessary basis for conditioned existence while being unable to identify any empirical thing as necessary.

passages.note: Reason demands a necessary basis but cannot think any individual thing necessary.

grounding.note: Reason demands a necessary basis but cannot think any individual thing necessary.

items.text: Necessity and contingency cannot be objective predicates of things as they are in themselves within speculative cognition.

passages.note: Necessity and contingency are denied as objective properties of things.

grounding.note: Necessity and contingency are denied as objective properties of things.

items.text: The idea of a necessary being functions heuristically: it commands systematic unity without adding an object to cognition.

passages.note: Necessary-ground ideas guide systematic inquiry without supplying an object.
Necessary-ground ideas guide systematic inquiry without supplying an object.

grounding.note: Necessary-ground ideas guide systematic inquiry without supplying an object.

items.text: The physico-theological proof can legitimate teleological investigation of nature without proving theology.

passages.note: Design animates and directs natural inquiry but does not establish theology.
Design animates and directs natural inquiry but does not establish theology.

grounding.note: Design animates and directs natural inquiry but does not establish theology.

items.text: Any attempt to move from world-order to an all-sufficient cause must supplement empirical analogy with cosmological and ontological reasoning.

passages.note: World-order reasoning passes through cosmology to ontological completion.

grounding.note: World-order reasoning passes through cosmology to ontological completion.

items.text: All speculative proofs reduce to the ontological proof as their final ground of necessity.

passages.note: Physico-theology rests on cosmology, which rests on ontology.

grounding.note: Physico-theology rests on cosmology, which rests on ontology.

items.text: Since the ontological proof fails, speculative reason has no successful proof of God.

passages.note: Speculative theology is fruitless because every proof ultimately needs ontological support.
Speculative theology is fruitless because every proof ultimately needs ontological support.

grounding.note: Speculative theology is fruitless because every proof ultimately needs ontological support.

items.text: The same limits that prevent proof of God also prevent speculative disproof of God.

passages.note: The inability to affirm a Supreme Being also invalidates speculative denial.

grounding.note: The inability to affirm a Supreme Being also invalidates speculative denial.

items.text: Transcendental theology remains valid as conceptual discipline, not as existential demonstration.

passages.note: Its valid role is negative conceptual correction rather than demonstration.
Its valid role is negative conceptual correction rather than demonstration.

grounding.note: Its valid role is negative conceptual correction rather than demonstration.

items.text: A moral postulate differs structurally from speculative proof because it proceeds from what ought to be, not from what is.

passages.note: Practical cognition concerns what ought to be and grounds postulation in moral necessity.

grounding.note: Practical cognition concerns what ought to be and grounds postulation in moral necessity.

items.text: Speculative theology is structurally parasitic on an impossible operation: the conversion of rational need into objective existence.

passages.note: Reason converts its need for necessity into an existent object by hypostatizing a regulative idea.
Reason converts its need for necessity into an existent object by hypostatizing a regulative idea.

grounding.note: Reason converts its need for necessity into an existent object by hypostatizing a regulative idea.

items.text: The three proof-forms form a dependency-chain: physico-theology depends on cosmology; cosmology depends on ontology; ontology fails because existence is not contained in concepts.

passages.note: The explicit dependency chain ends where conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.
The explicit dependency chain ends where conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.

grounding.note: The explicit dependency chain ends where conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.

items.text: God, for speculative reason, is not an object discovered beyond experience but the hypostatized form of reason’s demand for systematic unity.

passages.note: The Supreme Being is presented as the hypostatized principle of systematic unity.

grounding.note: The Supreme Being is presented as the hypostatized principle of systematic unity.

items.text: The critique does not abolish the idea of God; it changes its status from constitutive cognition to regulative ideal.

passages.note: The critique retains the ideal only as regulative rather than constitutive.

grounding.note: The critique retains the ideal only as regulative rather than constitutive.

items.text: The failure of speculative proof produces a double boundary: no dogmatic theology and no dogmatic atheism.

passages.note: The same reasoning excludes dogmatic affirmation and dogmatic denial.

grounding.note: The same reasoning excludes dogmatic affirmation and dogmatic denial.

items.text: Empirical purposiveness can intensify conviction and guide inquiry, but it cannot generate apodeictic theological knowledge.

passages.note: Natural purposiveness strengthens conviction and inquiry but lacks demonstrative certainty.
Natural purposiveness strengthens conviction and inquiry but lacks demonstrative certainty.

grounding.note: Natural purposiveness strengthens conviction and inquiry but lacks demonstrative certainty.

items.text: The highest speculative function of theology is negative: to police illegitimate predicates and prevent reason from mistaking its own idea for an object.

passages.note: Theology's highest speculative utility is negative conceptual purification.
Theology's highest speculative utility is negative conceptual purification.

grounding.note: Theology's highest speculative utility is negative conceptual purification.

items.text: Practical reason is positioned as the only remaining possible source for rationally meaningful affirmation of God.

passages.note: Positive rational theology is denied to speculation and reserved for moral postulation.
Positive rational theology is denied to speculation and reserved for moral postulation.

grounding.note: Positive rational theology is denied to speculation and reserved for moral postulation.

items.text: It must not be true that concepts alone can posit their objects.

passages.note: A concept cannot establish the existence of its object.

grounding.note: A concept cannot establish the existence of its object.

items.text: It must not be true that causality retains objective validity outside possible experience.

passages.note: Causality loses objective meaning beyond possible experience.
Causality loses objective meaning beyond possible experience.

grounding.note: Causality loses objective meaning beyond possible experience.

items.text: It must not be true that empirical completeness can be transformed into transcendent completion.

passages.note: Empiricism cannot attain absolute totality and instead makes a transcendent leap.
Empiricism cannot attain absolute totality and instead makes a transcendent leap.

grounding.note: Empiricism cannot attain absolute totality and instead makes a transcendent leap.

items.text: It must not be true that reason’s demand for unity reveals the structure of things in themselves.

passages.note: Reason's necessary-ground demand is subjective and regulative, not ontological disclosure.
Reason's necessary-ground demand is subjective and regulative, not ontological disclosure.

grounding.note: Reason's necessary-ground demand is subjective and regulative, not ontological disclosure.

items.text: It must not be true that the psychological necessity of an idea proves the metaphysical necessity of an object.

passages.note: Reason's felt need is not a credential of objectivity and is prone to hypostasis.
Reason's felt need is not a credential of objectivity and is prone to hypostasis.

grounding.note: Reason's felt need is not a credential of objectivity and is prone to hypostasis.

items.text: It must not be true that the world’s order is proportionate to an infinite divine cause.

passages.note: World magnitude and order cannot be measured against omnipotence or highest wisdom.

grounding.note: World magnitude and order cannot be measured against omnipotence or highest wisdom.

items.text: It must not be true that the impossibility of imagining an endless regress entails the existence of a first transcendent term.

passages.note: The alleged impossibility of an infinite causal series does not justify the inference.

grounding.note: The alleged impossibility of an infinite causal series does not justify the inference.

items.text: It must not be true that theological predicates derived from human intelligence can be univocally applied to the Supreme Being.

passages.note: Human-art analogy is limited, while transcendental critique removes anthropomorphic determinations.
Human-art analogy is limited, while transcendental critique removes anthropomorphic determinations.

grounding.note: Human-art analogy is limited, while transcendental critique removes anthropomorphic determinations.

items.text: It must not be true that speculative incapacity licenses denial of what speculative reason cannot cognize.

passages.note: Speculative inability to establish God equally bars demonstration of nonexistence.

grounding.note: Speculative inability to establish God equally bars demonstration of nonexistence.

items.text: It must not be true that natural theology can bypass transcendental critique by appealing to common sense, admiration, or empirical vividness.

passages.note: Empirical admiration and rhetorical force cannot make physico-theology demonstrative.
Empirical admiration and rhetorical force cannot make physico-theology demonstrative.

grounding.note: Empirical admiration and rhetorical force cannot make physico-theology demonstrative.

items.text: The absent object organizing the chapter is a cognizable God available to speculative reason; the entire critique turns on this object’s unavailability.

passages.note: No experience can be adequate to the idea, and transcendental theology yields no result.
No experience can be adequate to the idea, and transcendental theology yields no result.

grounding.note: No experience can be adequate to the idea, and transcendental theology yields no result.

items.text: The forbidden operation is hypostasis: treating a formal demand of reason as an independently existing being.

passages.note: The passages explicitly identify hypostatizing an idea and transforming regulative into constitutive.
The passages explicitly identify hypostatizing an idea and transforming regulative into constitutive.

grounding.note: The passages explicitly identify hypostatizing an idea and transforming regulative into constitutive.

items.text: The foreclosed possibility is a seamless bridge from experience to the unconditioned.

passages.note: Reason cannot bridge the abyss between empirical causal series and intelligible being.

grounding.note: Reason cannot bridge the abyss between empirical causal series and intelligible being.

items.text: The hidden abyss is the impossibility of grounding existence itself without converting reason’s need for ground into illusion.

passages.note: Unconditioned necessity is an abyss: reason requires a ground but cannot begin from one.
Unconditioned necessity is an abyss: reason requires a ground but cannot begin from one.

grounding.note: Unconditioned necessity is an abyss: reason requires a ground but cannot begin from one.

items.text: The disallowed theological desire is apodeictic certainty concerning God from theoretical reason.

passages.note: Apodeictic certainty about necessary existence is denied to speculative proof.
Apodeictic certainty about necessary existence is denied to speculative proof.

grounding.note: Apodeictic certainty about necessary existence is denied to speculative proof.

items.text: The terminal absence is an object adequate to the transcendental idea; no possible experience can supply it.

passages.note: No possible experience can be congruent with the transcendental idea.
No possible experience can be congruent with the transcendental idea.

grounding.note: No possible experience can be congruent with the transcendental idea.

items.text: Rational Need Layer: conditioned existence/order activates reason’s demand for complete grounding.

passages.note: Reason's need for necessary grounding arises from the empirical regress.

grounding.note: Reason's need for necessary grounding arises from the empirical regress.

items.text: Regress Layer: reason seeks an unconditioned terminus for the series of conditions.

passages.note: Reason seeks completion of the regress through a necessary basis.

grounding.note: Reason seeks completion of the regress through a necessary basis.

items.text: Conceptual Determination Layer: the unconditioned terminus is determinable only through the concept of the ens realissimum.

passages.note: Only ens realissimum is said to determine a necessary being completely.

grounding.note: Only ens realissimum is said to determine a necessary being completely.

items.text: Illicit Conversion Layer: the concept adequate to necessity is treated as proving necessary existence.

passages.note: The concept of highest reality is converted into a proof of necessity.

grounding.note: The concept of highest reality is converted into a proof of necessity.

items.text: Collapse Layer: cosmological and physico-theological proofs reduce to the ontological proof.

passages.note: Physico-theology reduces to cosmology, and cosmology to ontology.

grounding.note: Physico-theology reduces to cosmology, and cosmology to ontology.

items.text: Critical Boundary Layer: since existence cannot be derived from concepts and causality is immanent to experience, speculative proof fails.

passages.note: Causality is experiential and conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.
Causality is experiential and conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.

grounding.note: Causality is experiential and conceptual analysis cannot establish existence.

items.text: Regulative Reassignment Layer: the Supreme Being is retained as an ideal guiding systematic unity, not as a constitutively known object.

passages.note: The Supreme Being remains a regulative principle of systematic unity.

grounding.note: The Supreme Being remains a regulative principle of systematic unity.

items.text: Negative-Theological Utility Layer: transcendental theology purifies the concept of God and blocks both dogmatic affirmation and dogmatic denial.

passages.note: Negative theology purifies the concept while invalidating both affirmation and denial.

grounding.note: Negative theology purifies the concept while invalidating both affirmation and denial.

items.text: Practical Deferral Layer: any positive rational ground for affirming God must arise from moral necessity, not speculative cognition.

passages.note: Moral necessity is the only proposed source of positive rational theology.
Moral necessity is the only proposed source of positive rational theology.

grounding.note: Moral necessity is the only proposed source of positive rational theology.

items.text: Need for unconditioned ground → attempted speculative proof → cosmological appeal to existence → dependence on ens realissimum → ontological collapse → failure.

passages.note: Necessary-ground need enters cosmology, reaches ens realissimum, and collapses into ontology.
Necessary-ground need enters cosmology, reaches ens realissimum, and collapses into ontology.
Necessary-ground need enters cosmology, reaches ens realissimum, and collapses into ontology.

grounding.note: Necessary-ground need enters cosmology, reaches ens realissimum, and collapses into ontology.

items.text: Empirical order → inference to intelligent cause → insufficiency for creator/all-sufficient being → recourse to cosmological necessity → ontological collapse → failure.

passages.note: Design reaches only an architect and then recurs through cosmology to ontology.
Design reaches only an architect and then recurs through cosmology to ontology.
Design reaches only an architect and then recurs through cosmology to ontology.

grounding.note: Design reaches only an architect and then recurs through cosmology to ontology.

items.text: Failure of proof → analysis of illusion → regulative reinterpretation of necessity → preservation of ideal without object-cognition.

passages.note: The dialectical illusion is explained by reassigning necessity to regulative use.
The dialectical illusion is explained by reassigning necessity to regulative use.

grounding.note: The dialectical illusion is explained by reassigning necessity to regulative use.

items.text: Speculative limitation → rejection of dogmatic theology → rejection of dogmatic atheism → negative purification of theological concept → opening toward moral theology.

passages.note: Speculation yields neither dogmatic theology nor atheism, but purification and moral deferral.
Speculation yields neither dogmatic theology nor atheism, but purification and moral deferral.
Speculation yields neither dogmatic theology nor atheism, but purification and moral deferral.

grounding.note: Speculation yields neither dogmatic theology nor atheism, but purification and moral deferral.

items.text: The field of theological proofs is reorganized into three apparent routes but one real dependency-chain ending in ontology.

passages.note: The three routes are explicitly arranged as a chain ending in ontology.

grounding.note: The three routes are explicitly arranged as a chain ending in ontology.

items.text: Experience is reclassified from proof-ground to occasion for reason’s regulative demand.

passages.note: Experience only leads reason toward necessity; systematic unity has regulative status.
Experience only leads reason toward necessity; systematic unity has regulative status.

grounding.note: Experience only leads reason toward necessity; systematic unity has regulative status.

items.text: Absolute necessity is displaced from object-predicate to subjective-regulative principle of reason.

passages.note: Necessity is shifted from objective predicate to subjective-regulative principle.

grounding.note: Necessity is shifted from objective predicate to subjective-regulative principle.

items.text: Natural design is reclassified as heuristic support for inquiry, not demonstrative evidence of divine existence.

passages.note: Design guides and encourages inquiry but is insufficient as proof.
Design guides and encourages inquiry but is insufficient as proof.

grounding.note: Design guides and encourages inquiry but is insufficient as proof.

items.text: The Supreme Being is shifted from speculative object to transcendental ideal.

passages.note: The Supreme Being is a speculative ideal whose reality is undecidable.

grounding.note: The Supreme Being is a speculative ideal whose reality is undecidable.

items.text: The critique redraws the boundary between immanent principles of understanding and transcendent misuse of those principles.

passages.note: Immanent experiential principles are opposed to transcendent theological use.
Immanent experiential principles are opposed to transcendent theological use.

grounding.note: Immanent experiential principles are opposed to transcendent theological use.

items.text: Deism and theism are separated by the difference between an indeterminate primal cause and a living intelligent author.

passages.note: The passages distinguish primal cause from a living intelligent author.
The passages distinguish primal cause from a living intelligent author.

grounding.note: The passages distinguish primal cause from a living intelligent author.

items.text: Theological discourse is divided into speculative impossibility, negative conceptual discipline, and possible practical postulation.

passages.note: Speculative failure, negative utility, and practical postulation are separately stated.
Speculative failure, negative utility, and practical postulation are separately stated.
Speculative failure, negative utility, and practical postulation are separately stated.

grounding.note: Speculative failure, negative utility, and practical postulation are separately stated.

items.text: Atheism loses speculative demonstrability for the same reason dogmatic theism loses it.

passages.note: The arguments preventing proof also prevent speculative atheistic denial.

grounding.note: The arguments preventing proof also prevent speculative atheistic denial.

items.text: Moral theology becomes structurally necessary if any rational theology is to have positive force.

passages.note: Only moral laws are offered as a possible foundation for rational theology.
Only moral laws are offered as a possible foundation for rational theology.

grounding.note: Only moral laws are offered as a possible foundation for rational theology.

items.text: Surface: examination of cosmological, physico-theological, and speculative theological proofs of God.

passages.note: The passages introduce cosmological, physico-theological, and speculative-theological critique.
The passages introduce cosmological, physico-theological, and speculative-theological critique.
The passages introduce cosmological, physico-theological, and speculative-theological critique.

grounding.note: The passages introduce cosmological, physico-theological, and speculative-theological critique.

items.text: Structural: exposure of proof-dependency, where empirical and cosmological arguments secretly require ontological inference.

passages.note: Empirical and cosmological reasoning are exposed as dependent on ontology.
Empirical and cosmological reasoning are exposed as dependent on ontology.

grounding.note: Empirical and cosmological reasoning are exposed as dependent on ontology.

items.text: Transcendental: determination of the valid domain of causality, necessity, contingency, and synthetic cognition.

passages.note: These passages delimit necessity, contingency, causality, and synthetic cognition to experience.
These passages delimit necessity, contingency, causality, and synthetic cognition to experience.
These passages delimit necessity, contingency, causality, and synthetic cognition to experience.

grounding.note: These passages delimit necessity, contingency, causality, and synthetic cognition to experience.

items.text: Regulative: reinterpretation of the Supreme Being as an ideal governing systematic unity in the explanation of phenomena.

passages.note: The Supreme Being is recast as a regulative ideal of systematic explanation.

grounding.note: The Supreme Being is recast as a regulative ideal of systematic explanation.

items.text: Apophatic: denial that speculative reason can either affirm or negate God as an object.

passages.note: Pure reason can neither affirm nor negate the Supreme Being's reality.
Pure reason can neither affirm nor negate the Supreme Being's reality.

grounding.note: Pure reason can neither affirm nor negate the Supreme Being's reality.

items.text: Metastrategic: relocation of theology from speculative demonstration to conceptual purification and practical/moral possible grounding.

passages.note: Theology is retained for conceptual correction and possible moral grounding.
Theology is retained for conceptual correction and possible moral grounding.

grounding.note: Theology is retained for conceptual correction and possible moral grounding.

items.text: Ontological/Temporal: refusal to treat eternity, necessity, or first cause as cognizable determinations of a thing-in-itself through theoretical reason.

passages.note: Necessary and eternal predicates are ideals, not theoretical cognition of a thing in itself.
Necessary and eternal predicates are ideals, not theoretical cognition of a thing in itself.

grounding.note: Necessary and eternal predicates are ideals, not theoretical cognition of a thing in itself.

items.text: The axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the chapter’s main movement: all speculative proofs fail because they exceed the conditions of possible experience and depend on ontological inference.

passages.note: The proof chain fails because it requires ontology and exceeds experiential conditions.
The proof chain fails because it requires ontology and exceeds experiential conditions.
The proof chain fails because it requires ontology and exceeds experiential conditions.

grounding.note: The proof chain fails because it requires ontology and exceeds experiential conditions.

items.text: The system is internally coherent if the critical restriction of synthetic cognition to possible experience is granted.

passages.note: The stated critical restriction makes all speculative transcendental theology fruitless.

grounding.note: The stated critical restriction makes all speculative transcendental theology fruitless.

items.text: The strongest structural point is the dependency-collapse of cosmological and physico-theological proofs into the ontological proof.

passages.note: The explicit three-stage dependency culminates in the ontological proof.

grounding.note: The explicit three-stage dependency culminates in the ontological proof.

items.text: The most load-bearing distinction is constitutive cognition versus regulative use.

passages.note: The central distinction is explicitly regulative versus constitutive use.

grounding.note: The central distinction is explicitly regulative versus constitutive use.

items.text: What remains underdetermined is the later positive grounding of moral theology, which is invoked but not demonstrated here.

passages.note: Moral postulation is announced but its argument is expressly postponed.

grounding.note: Moral postulation is announced but its argument is expressly postponed.

items.text: The critique depends on compression where it treats the ontological proof as already refuted and imports that failure into the later proofs.

passages.note: The later proof-collapse relies on the already rejected ontological procedure.
The later proof-collapse relies on the already rejected ontological procedure.
The later proof-collapse relies on the already rejected ontological procedure.

grounding.note: The later proof-collapse relies on the already rejected ontological procedure.

items.text: The main structural tension is that reason necessarily demands the unconditioned while being forbidden to cognize it speculatively.

passages.note: Reason must seek necessity while no individual object may be known as necessary.
Reason must seek necessity while no individual object may be known as necessary.

grounding.note: Reason must seek necessity while no individual object may be known as necessary.

items.text: Reconstruction from this extraction would preserve the real movement: proof-attempt → hidden ontological dependence → transcendental invalidation → regulative preservation → practical deferral.

passages.note: The passages supply the stated movement from proof through collapse and critique to regulation and morality.
The passages supply the stated movement from proof through collapse and critique to regulation and morality.

The passages supply the stated movement from proof through collapse and critique to regulation and morality.

grounding.note: The passages supply the stated movement from proof through collapse and critique to regulation and morality.

items.text: Problem: pure reason necessarily generates transcendental ideas that exceed possible experience yet cannot be dismissed as mere error.

passages.note: Reason naturally exceeds experience, while ideas retain a legitimate aim.
Reason naturally exceeds experience, while ideas retain a legitimate aim.

grounding.note: Reason naturally exceeds experience, while ideas retain a legitimate aim.

items.text: Core distinction: ideas are not false in themselves; they become dialectical only when employed constitutively rather than regulatively.

passages.note: Ideas become delusive through transcendent misemployment, not intrinsically.
Ideas become delusive through transcendent misemployment, not intrinsically.

grounding.note: Ideas become delusive through transcendent misemployment, not intrinsically.

items.text: Reframing: reason’s proper object is not things directly but the systematic employment of the understanding.

passages.note: Reason immediately relates to and systematizes understanding.

grounding.note: Reason immediately relates to and systematizes understanding.

items.text: Thesis: transcendental ideas have objective but indeterminate validity as regulative principles for the systematic unity of empirical cognition.

passages.note: Ideas have objective yet undetermined validity as regulative rules.
Ideas have objective yet undetermined validity as regulative rules.

grounding.note: Ideas have objective yet undetermined validity as regulative rules.

items.text: Movement: dialectical illusion → critique of transcendent misuse → discovery of immanent regulative function → deduction of speculative ideas as heuristic schemas.

passages.note: The sequence moves from illusion through restriction to heuristic regulation.
The sequence moves from illusion through restriction to heuristic regulation.
The sequence moves from illusion through restriction to heuristic regulation.
The sequence moves from illusion through restriction to heuristic regulation.

grounding.note: The sequence moves from illusion through restriction to heuristic regulation.

items.text: Final position: reason cannot extend knowledge beyond experience, but it necessarily organizes experience toward maximum systematic unity.

passages.note: Speculation cannot exceed experience but directs cognition toward unity.
Speculation cannot exceed experience but directs cognition toward unity.

grounding.note: Speculation cannot exceed experience but directs cognition toward unity.

items.text: All inferences that claim cognition beyond possible experience are fallacious and groundless.

passages.note: Beyond-experience inferences are called fallacious and groundless.

grounding.note: Beyond-experience inferences are called fallacious and groundless.

items.text: Human reason naturally tends to overstep the limits of possible experience.

passages.note: Reason has a natural inclination to overstep experience.

grounding.note: Reason has a natural inclination to overstep experience.

items.text: Transcendental ideas belong naturally to reason as categories belong naturally to understanding.

passages.note: Ideas belong to reason as categories belong to understanding.

grounding.note: Ideas belong to reason as categories belong to understanding.

items.text: Ideas mislead only through misemployment, not through their mere existence.

passages.note: Only employment, not the idea itself, is transcendent or immanent.

grounding.note: Only employment, not the idea itself, is transcendent or immanent.

items.text: An idea is transcendent when applied as if an adequate object corresponded to it.

passages.note: Transcendent use applies an idea to a falsely adequate object.

grounding.note: Transcendent use applies an idea to a falsely adequate object.

items.text: An idea is immanent when applied only to the empirical employment of the understanding.

passages.note: Immanent use applies the idea to understanding in experience.

grounding.note: Immanent use applies the idea to understanding in experience.

items.text: Reason has no immediate relation to objects; it relates immediately to the understanding.

passages.note: Reason relates immediately to understanding, not objects.

grounding.note: Reason relates immediately to understanding, not objects.

items.text: Reason does not constitute objects; it gives unity to the understanding’s cognitions.

passages.note: Reason arranges concepts and gives their unity.

grounding.note: Reason arranges concepts and gives their unity.

items.text: The proper function of reason is to produce systematic unity among cognitions.

passages.note: Reason arranges cognitions into a system.

grounding.note: Reason arranges cognitions into a system.

items.text: Systematic unity requires the idea of a whole that precedes and orders the cognition of parts.

items.text: The cluster solves the problem of how cognition can possess necessity, strict universality, and objective validity when human cognition begins through sensuous affection.

Its decisive operation is the separation of empirical occasion from transcendental validity-source, then the internal decomposition of that validity-source into pure intuition and pure conceptual synthesis.
The system becomes a transcendental-juridical architecture: it does not ask what objects are absolutely, but by what right cognition claims necessary object-validity.
The directional movement is not linear exposition but recursive restriction: each source of cognition is authorized only by being confined to possible experience.
Sensibility first supplies the field of possible givenness through space and time; understanding then supplies the formal unity under which the given manifold becomes thinkable as object.
Synthetic a priori cognition is not solved by a single faculty but by the coordinated finitude of receptivity and spontaneity.
The cluster’s real motion is spiral: necessity forces the a priori; the a priori forces critique; critique forces limitation; limitation retroactively secures objectivity within experience.

Closure is provisional and juridical, not doctrinal: mathematics and possible experience receive partial grounding, while metaphysics is suspended until pure concepts receive deduction and are confined in use.
[Persistent] Human cognition begins with experience but cannot derive its necessity, strict universality, or objective validity from experience.
[Persistent] Cognition requires two irreducible sources: sensibility gives objects through intuition, and understanding thinks objects through concepts.
[Persistent] Neither intuition without concepts nor concepts without corresponding intuition constitutes cognition.
[Mutating] The a priori first appears as non-empirical validity, then becomes formal sensuous givenness in space and time, then becomes pure conceptual unity in the categories.
[Persistent] Necessity and strict universality function as diagnostic marks of a priori cognition and as exclusions of empirical derivation.
[Emergent] Synthetic a priori cognition requires a non-empirical synthesis grounded jointly in pure intuition and pure understanding, not in concepts alone.
[Persistent] Space and time are pure a priori forms of sensibility: empirically real for possible experience and transcendentally ideal with respect to things in themselves.
[Emergent] Objectivity is redefined as necessary validity for possible experience under subjective but universal conditions of givenness and synthesis.
[Mutating] The subject mutates from empirical knower into the formal site of conditions under which objects can appear and be thought.
[Persistent] Things in themselves are thinkable as limiting correlates but not cognizable through human sensibility or pure understanding.

[Attractor] Possible experience is the governing boundary that simultaneously authorizes mathematics, natural-scientific objectivity, and the legitimate use of pure concepts while excluding transcendent speculation.
[Persistent] Metaphysics is unavoidable as a tendency of reason but illegitimate as dogmatic science unless subjected to critique of the sources, scope, and limits of a priori cognition.
[Emergent] Critique operates by converting alleged objective determinations into conditions of cognition, then testing their domain of legitimate application.
[Mutating] Logic shifts from formal correctness to transcendental object-relation: it is canon when restricted, dialectic when misused as organon.
[Terminal] The cluster terminates in the necessity of transcendental deduction: categories must prove their right to apply to objects because their origin alone cannot justify objective validity.
