Affect behaves as a transferable magnitude whose destination depends on conjunction: it passes into a dominant passion, a pursued end, or a sympathizing group.

Stabilization is pleasurable only relative to a prior disturbance: orderly facility resolves resistance and belief resolves doubt, but prolonged facility can eliminate the contrast required for interest.
Familiarity has opposed effects because it operates through distinct mediators: it removes novelty under custom while strengthening relation and ideational proximity in informational curiosity.

Conduct can precede the motive later attributed to it: repeated action generates inclination, pursuit generates concern for its end, and sympathetic response organizes behavior without knowledge of the initiating object.

The distribution of passions is governed partly by processing cost: low-reflection mechanisms diffuse broadly, difficult inquiry requires concentrated exercise, and passive repetition weakens when independent activation is absent.

Affective construction is powerful but not unlimited: every recursive process requires an initially available sensible effect, natural emotion, engaging idea, tolerable action, or instinctive disposition.
The subject becomes a path-dependent configuration of sensitivities, habits, beliefs, transmitted passions, and acquired concerns rather than a fixed rational origin.
Affective time is nonlinear: recurrence produces thresholds and phase changes rather than mere accumulation, while later outputs revise the conditions of subsequent encounters.
Ends can be temporally posterior to action: inclination, concern, and the pain of failure may be generated by the process they later appear to motivate.
Epistemic motivation is naturalized without being normatively secured: affect explains why inquiry and belief occur but not why truth deserves pursuit.
The individual is affectively porous: sympathy, conjunction, and imagined utility allow social force to operate without shared propositions or benevolent intentions.
Effective agency occupies a moving interval between inert facility and unmastered agitation, using enough resistance, attention, and success to sustain active motion.
Affective universality is compatible with mechanistic plurality: common passions need not arise through identical cognitive, associative, instinctive, temporal, or epistemic routes.
Causal explanation must decompose nominal passions into source, enabling condition, transfer mechanism, temporal phase, and completion or termination condition.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Novelty loop: unfamiliarity → resistance → excitation → amplified passion → repetition → novelty-decay → facility → inclination → further repetition → languor or reversal.
Inquiry loop: represented importance → fixed attention → difficult exercise → pleasure → transferred concern for the end → heightened stakes of success and error → renewed pursuit.
Informational-curiosity loop: relation or novelty → forceful but unstable idea → painful vacillation → demand for belief → vivification and fixation → relief.
Sympathetic escalation loop: perceived passion → affective communication → conjunction → intensified collective passion → stronger perceptible passion.
Active-habit loop: performance supplies excitation → repetition produces facility and inclination → inclination increases performance → performance renews its own support.
Transfer attractor: affect generated at one site migrates toward the object, end, passion, or group most strongly related to the generating operation.

Excitatory-band attractor: the system repeatedly seeks sufficient force to secure attention and motion without crossing into overwhelming resistance, painful vacillation, or affect-destroying facility.
Comparative-confirmation loop: a prior human passion theory predicts animal behavior, analogy interprets that behavior as passion, and the interpreted behavior then corroborates the theory.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Initial endowment: sensible valence, instinct, natural emotion, or ideational salience supplies the minimum difference on which affective processing can operate.
Differential input: vary cognitive capacity, repetition, difficulty, relation, assurance, or activity mode while holding other factors comparatively stable.
Mediation: input encounters resistance, facility, attention, association, sympathy, exercise, vivacity, or fixation rather than producing passion immediately.
Channel selection: cognitive power, temporal phase, and active/passive mode determine which mediator becomes effective.
Affective conversion: the mediator generates pleasure, pain, agitation, relief, or transmitted passion, which then augments or redirects the operative affection.
Recursive transfer: generated affect becomes inclination, acquired concern, social amplification, or demand for stabilized belief.
Iteration: the output alters the next encounter, producing reinforcement, tranquillity, exhaustion, intensified pursuit, or reversal.
Conditional closure: recurring operations establish a general dynamic architecture, while instinct, irreducible salience, and unspecified thresholds preserve causal plurality.

Fixed object-value challenged → controlled variation introduced → mediating operation isolated → affect generated or transmitted → force transferred to passion, end, or group → recurrence changes operating conditions → inclination, stabilization, amplification, exhaustion, or reversal.

Species-general sensitivity → cognition-dependent channel selection → active/passive bifurcation → threshold-sensitive temporal iteration → acquired concern and collective force → conditional processual closure.
The human–animal divide is replaced by affective continuity with graded cognitive access to different mechanisms.
Object-centered affect is replaced by a relational field in which history, mental operation, attention, and transmission determine experienced force.
Cognition is reclassified from sovereign source to variable mechanism: it may be unnecessary, limiting, enabling, effortful, or affect-generating.
Repetition becomes a threshold-governed phase process rather than a synonym for reinforcement or familiarity.
Motivation is divided into original pleasure, enabling condition, transferred concern, and completion condition, allowing ends to be produced by activity.
Social coordination becomes intelligible without shared causal knowledge, species identity, retaliation calculation, or genuine benevolence.
Truth, utility, and natural valence are reclassified as inputs whose motivational force depends on mediation rather than as self-executing causes.
Contradictory effects cease to demand separate faculties once degree, sequence, transfer, and active/passive mode become available as explanatory variables.
Surface level: animal affections, the contrary effects of custom, scientific pursuit, and informational curiosity supply heterogeneous cases of variable passion.
Structural level: sensible effects, association, instinct, sympathy, resistance, facility, attention, cognitive exercise, belief, and doubt form interacting affective mediators.
Metastrategic level: apparent contradictions are decomposed by controlled comparison into source, condition, mode, threshold, transfer, and phase.
Ontological / Temporal level: sensitive life is continuous across species but internally historical, with present passions produced by successive encounters and recursive modifications.
Epistemic level: animal passion is inferred analogically, while human truth-seeking is explained genealogically; neither procedure yields direct access to an intrinsically truth-governed interior.
Methodological / Performative level: the cluster performs its own theory by repeatedly exposing a fixed explanation to variation until hidden mediators, reversals, and bifurcations appear.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Species-general springs coexist with peculiar parental instinct, leaving uncertain whether instinct belongs to the common architecture or marks an irreducible exception.
The processual account depends on natural goods, emotions, saliences, and repugnances whose origin it does not explain, limiting its apparent constructivism.
Familiarity weakens passion by removing novelty but can strengthen curiosity by increasing relation; the architecture distinguishes mediators without specifying their relative dominance.
Uncertainty is enabling within active pursuit but painful as doxastic vacillation; the boundary between productive openness and destabilizing alternation remains underdetermined.
Belief explains vivid fixation and relief without securing truth, separating the motivational closure of curiosity from epistemic correctness.
Spirits, sympathy, instinct, attention, and belief provide heterogeneous causal vocabularies whose functional coordination exceeds their explicit theoretical integration.
Animal behavior confirms a theory imported through human analogy, producing an evidential loop whose corroborative force is real but not fully independent.
Difficulty mutates from resistant agitation in unfamiliar apprehension into pleasurable exertion in active discovery.
Cognition mutates from a dispensable condition of elementary passion into a principal source of scientific pleasure.
Relation mutates from an obvious association between beings into an operator that fixes attention, vivifies ideas, and transfers concern to ends.
Stability mutates from pleasurable tranquillity into affect-destroying languor under excess, while belief-stability remains pleasurable because it terminates vacillation.
The end mutates from an antecedently valued object into a product of action-generated passion and relational transfer.
Sympathy mutates from direct interanimal communication into a faint imaginative mechanism that supports attention without producing genuine concern.
Affective reality appears as an excitable network in which objects, ideas, actions, and organisms become nodes for the circulation and conversion of pleasure, pain, attention, and passion.
The subject is a permeable and temporally accumulated switching-point rather than a sovereign center: it receives, amplifies, habituates, pursues, transfers, and stabilizes forces.
Time is a sequence of phase transitions in which repetition and pursuit alter the mechanism that will govern the next encounter.
Viable navigation consists in regulating relation, resistance, attention, repetition, and activity so that affect remains forceful without collapsing into repugnance, vacillation, or languor.
Collective life is an amplification circuit in which passion can cross bodies and organize conduct before its origin is consciously represented.

The global axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster if affect is retained as mediated, transferable, path-dependent, degree-sensitive, and cognitively gated rather than intrinsically object-fixed.
The system is coherent at this scale as a plural dynamic architecture, but not as a reduction to one physiological or psychological mechanism.

The architecture is strongest where differential variation separates content from operation and where affective transfer explains the production of amplified passions, inclinations, and acquired ends.
It remains underdetermined at thresholds of cognition, facility, salience, success, and relation, and at the origin of instinctive or naturally affective endowments.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if recursive sequence and functional reversal are retained; flattening difficulty, familiarity, stability, or cognition into fixed causes would destroy the system.
The indispensable remainder resistant to axiomatic reduction is the evidential and causal bridge supplied by analogy, spirits, instinct, and compressed appeals to sympathy or attention.

The governing problem is how partial passions, scarce transferable goods, and social dependence can generate determinate and morally authoritative juridical relations without innate justice or antecedent property rights.
Justice is reconstructed as an artificial but necessary rule-system: natural conditions necessitate coordination, but neither natural impulse nor independent reason directly supplies its form.
The argument becomes a combined motivational genealogy, institutional ontology, psychological jurisprudence, and reductive test of rival natural-right models.
First-order self-interest threatens cooperation; reflective self-interest redirects the same passion into reciprocal restraint and gradually stabilized expectations.
Stabilized possession does not recognize pre-existing property but generates property, right, and obligation as duties constituted by justice.

The establishment of property creates a second-order allocation problem: general utility requires determinate titles but cannot derive their particular content, so imagination and antecedent relations select juridical forms.
Because possessory, temporal, spatial, causal, and associative relations remain gradual or conflicting, municipal law imposes binary closure where natural criteria underdetermine title.
Interest first establishes observance; the perceived utility of the resulting system then produces sympathetic approval, education, reputation, and institutional reinforcement.

The movement is recursive and sedimentary rather than linear: passion generates restraint, restraint generates rights, rights require stipulative determination, and moralization feeds the determinate system back into conduct as second nature.
[Persistent] Society is necessary under conditions in which human weakness, partial affection, conflicting self-love, and scarce transferable goods make unregulated possession unstable.
[Persistent] A moral predicate cannot supply the first motive for the conduct whose morality it evaluates; institutional genesis must therefore begin from pre-moral passions and interests.
[Attractor] Justice is artificial without being arbitrary: it is convention-dependent in origin but functionally necessitated by durable human and material conditions.
[Persistent] Convention arises through mutually known, conditionally reciprocal restraint grounded in common interest and repeated experience, not through an antecedent promise or sovereign command.
[Mutating] Self-interest changes function across scales: immediate acquisition destabilizes society, while reflective and coordinated self-interest generates the rules that restrain acquisition.
[Terminal] Property is not antecedent to justice but is constituted as a socially enforced relation of duties, expectations, rights, and exclusions.
[Emergent] The convention stabilizing possession does not itself assign goods; institutional existence and juridical individuation are distinct generative problems.
[Emergent] Property has a dual determination: general utility necessitates settled allocation, while imagination and antecedent relations principally specify who receives which title.
[Persistent] Stable justice requires society-wide general and inflexible rules because case-sensitive judgments of need, merit, fitness, or immediate utility reproduce partiality and contention.

[Mutating] Title is temporally layered: present possession governs founding settlement, while occupation, prescription, accession, and succession govern differentiated acquisition within established society.
[Emergent] Juridical outputs are integral and binary even though their psychological, utilitarian, temporal, and relational grounds vary by degree.
[Terminal] Municipal law supplies practical closure where natural association and public utility fail to determine a unique title.
[Attractor] The justice of an act derives from its position within a socially advantageous rule-system rather than from its isolated consequences.
[Persistent] Justice has a temporally divided foundation: common interest generates observance before sympathy with public utility generates moral approval.

[Attractor] Once established, convention, juridical determination, moral approbation, education, reputation, and government form a reinforcing system that converts artificial rules into durable dispositions.
[Stable identity] Justice remains an artificial virtue throughout: neither its necessity, its utility, nor its affective approval converts it into an innate moral principle.
[Functional recurrence] Stability of possession first solves social conflict, then reappears as an insufficient general rule whose allocation gap generates the detailed property regime.
[Escalation] Property moves from an effect of stabilized possession, to a differentiated system of relational titles, to evidence that juridical reality is institutionally constituted.

[Mutation] Utility first explains why justice is necessary, then becomes insufficient to specify particular titles, and finally becomes the public effect whose contemplation moralizes the completed system.
[Reversal] Self-love changes from the principal source of possessory conflict into the originating material of reciprocal restraint and unintended public advantage.

[Displacement] Imagination migrates from a general psychological faculty of associative completion into a juridical mechanism that joins persons to objects, extends titles, and structures inheritance.
[Mutation] Generality changes from reciprocal abstention governing possession into differentiated but society-wide rules whose inflexibility suppresses case-specific natural motivation.
[Terminal transformation] Present possession produces founding title but disappears as a perpetual criterion once its founding work is complete; occupation and restitution require its restriction.
[Migration] Graduality moves from possessory probability and temporal association into a general challenge to the integral form of property, right, and obligation.

[Absorption] Sympathy begins as the explanation of moral approval and is absorbed into a larger institutional feedback loop involving public judgment, education, reputation, and stabilized compliance.

[Disappearance after structural work] Universal benevolence, direct public concern, private benevolence, and an innate sense of justice disappear as originating motives after forcing the transition to convention and reflected interest.

[Local-to-scaling] The semantic disambiguation of “nature” remains preparatory machinery, but it scales upward by preventing artificial justice from being classified as unnatural, arbitrary, or morally defective.
[Local] The detailed taxonomies of occupation, prescription, accession, and succession remain lower-layer jurisprudential machinery; only their common relational and temporal structure scales upward.
[Scales upward] The convention of stable possession becomes the cluster’s constitutive threshold between physical control and normative property.

[Bridge] Imagination bridges institutional necessity and determinate title by converting natural relations of proximity, causality, duration, scale, and kinship into socially stabilized juridical attachments.
[Bridge] The priority of motive over moral judgment bridges the sentimental theory of virtue and the institutional genealogy by requiring pre-moral interest to precede moral obligation.
[Catalyst] The gradation test converts local observations about fluid possession and natural motivation into a general explanation of why juridical decision requires imposed binary closure.
[Superseded] Present possession is indispensable at the founding threshold but becomes invalid as a universal title once an established regime supports restitution and differentiated acquisition.
[Recoded] Education, reputation, and political reinforcement do not originate justice; they recode an established convention as honor, duty, and second nature.
[Local] The solitary state of nature remains an analytical fiction used to isolate passions from understanding; the cluster does not require it as an actual historical stage.

[Peripheral] Consensual transfer and promise-performance mark the broader perimeter of justice, but the current architecture develops possession and property rather than independently reconstructing those laws.
Justice cannot be explained by property or right antecedent to convention because those juridical relations are effects of justice.
Justice is not an innate passion, peculiar natural virtue, or direct expression of ordinary impartial motivation.
Property is not an intrinsic, sensible, corporeal, or independently real quality of an object.
Neither reason, public utility, personal fitness, nor natural association supplies a complete and exact code of particular titles.
Stable justice cannot remain continuously responsive to individual need, merit, character, benevolence, or optimal use.
Convention cannot be founded on a prior promise, and authoritative law cannot be treated as the original source of moral intelligibility.
Universal humanity, private benevolence, and direct concern for the public good cannot generate the original invariant rules of justice.
Isolated consequences cannot determine justice independently of the general rule-system to which an act belongs.
Social necessity does not prove natural implantation, while artificiality does not entail dispensability or arbitrariness.
Neither present possession nor recoverable original title can remain the permanent and exhaustive foundation of ownership.
The architecture requires the primordial-rights model to be false: no pre-social subject-object bond can obligate others before convention institutes duties.
Self-grounding normativity is inadmissible: morality cannot generate its own first motive, and justice cannot presuppose the rights it constitutes.
A rationalist jurisprudence capable of deducing every title from immutable relations must be false because relational grounds remain graded, conflicting, and psychologically mediated.
A continuously optimizing distributive model must be excluded because recurrent reassignment by need, merit, or use would dissolve the stability justice exists to produce.
Legal determinacy cannot be assumed to mirror an equally determinate natural terrain; binary verdicts exceed their gradual justificatory grounds.
Social order cannot require benevolent collective design: coordinated private interests may generate public utility without intending it as a shared end.
Historical priority cannot confer perpetual juridical authority because temporal distance changes the force of relations and permits prescription to displace obscured origins.
The inference from indispensability to innateness must remain invalid; otherwise justice’s functional necessity would erase the distinction between natural passion and artificial strategy.
Justice occupies the absence of a naturally impartial legislative passion capable of converting partial desire directly into universal conduct.
Property occupies the absence of a natural and stable “mine and thine” persisting independently of reciprocal recognition, duty, and law.
Municipal decision occupies the absence of a final adjudicative measure beneath convention, imagination, utility, and positive stipulation.
No seamless middle term connects gradual grounds of entitlement to the integral rights demanded by social coordination.
The unavailable possibility organizing the system is a property order that is simultaneously perfectly stable, continuously equitable, naturally exact, and responsive to every particular case.
The pre-conventional individual is denied the status of a complete rights-bearing subject; juridical individuality emerges only within stabilized relations of reciprocal conduct.
The first convention generates property only in general form; the allocation rules then individuate that constituted relation by attaching particular persons to particular goods.
Utility, imagination, and law perform irreducible functions: utility demands settlement, imagination selects relational titles, and law terminates disputes where those relations conflict.

Artificial order is generated by natural faculties without directly expressing natural impulse: reflection redirects interest, imagination formats title, and sympathy subsequently moralizes the result.
Reciprocal expectation solves the regress of institutional origin, while stabilized rules convert that non-promissory coordination into duties that can later support promises and transfer.
The system can be non-arbitrary at the level of its social function while remaining stipulative at particular boundaries: necessity governs the existence of settlement, not every detail of its form.
Title can change without physical alteration because juridical change occurs in socially organized expectations and duties rather than in the object’s sensible properties.
Prescription demonstrates that time is constitutive rather than merely chronological: it redistributes title by weakening one relation and strengthening another in sentiment.
Public utility changes temporal status from an unintended effect of coordinated self-interest into the contemplated object that elicits moral approval.

Moral approval stabilizes a determinate title-system whose particular assignments are not independently derivable from utility; sympathy sanctions the beneficial scheme rather than rationally deducing each title.
Juridical impartiality is not the expression of an impartial originating motive but the institutional suppression of variable motives through invariant rules.

The grounds of justice divide into genetic interest, systemic utility, imaginative title-formation, authoritative closure, and sentimental sanction; no single ground performs every legitimating function.

Normative order has a distributed sequence unavailable to any single mechanism: pre-moral coordination establishes stability, relational rules individuate property, authoritative decisions close residual ambiguity, and sympathy moralizes the completed system.
Institutions do not merely regulate antecedent objects; they constitute property as an object of moral judgment and then produce sentiments that appear to recognize its authority.
Legal universality is manufactured impartiality: it arises from invariant application across persons, not from universal benevolence, metaphysical equality, or naturally impartial motives.
Stable justice requires rigidity at the level of ordinary application but mutability at the level of legal form, since positive rules must settle changing and previously underdetermined relations.
Local stipulation is contained by global necessity: particular boundary decisions may lack unique natural derivation while the demand for determinate settlement remains non-arbitrary.
Juridical legitimacy is architecturally plural rather than foundationally unitary: origin, function, form, decision, and moral force are assigned to different mechanisms.

The property regime is path-dependent: founding possession establishes initial distributions, established titles structure later associative extensions, and prescription allows elapsed time to overwrite recoverable origin.

Agency is neither sovereign moral choice nor passive determination by appetite; it is the capacity of partial agents to reflect, coordinate, internalize general rules, and act through instituted relations.

Justice recursively converts natural instability into normative reality: passions generate convention, convention generates rights, rights reorganize conduct, and reorganized conduct reinforces the convention’s affective authority.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Immediate interest → possessory conflict → reflection on long-range advantage → reciprocal restraint → social stability → enlarged interest in preserving restraint.
Conditional restraint → repeated reciprocal conduct → confidence in others’ restraint → stronger expectations → convention capable of sustaining further compliance.
Stable possession → property relation → differentiated titles → determinate expectations → increased stability of possession.
Systemic advantage → sympathetic approval → education and reputation → internalized probity → stronger adherence → more visible systemic advantage.
Possession escalates from causal power over an object, to stabilized social expectation, to constituted property, to integral juridical right.
Graded relations → conflicting title pressures → municipal decision → binary settlement → new relational baselines from which subsequent titles are generated.
Determinate settlement is the principal attractor: utility, imagination, general rules, and positive law converge not on perfect allocation but on terminated controversy.
Artificiality becomes a generative machine rather than a negative classification when convention converts natural conflict into universal rules and those rules become morally internalized.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Human weakness + social dependence + partial affection + scarce transferable goods → instability of possession and threat to cooperation.
Motivational circularity + failure of universal benevolence, direct public concern, and natural justice → requirement for a pre-moral artificial genesis.
Immediate self-interest + reflection on long-range systemic advantage → second-order redirection of acquisitive passion.
Reciprocal expression + conditional restraint + repeated experience → non-promissory convention and stabilized expectations.
Stable expectations of abstention and restoration → justice and injustice → property, right, and obligation.
General property relation → unresolved person-good allocation → rejection of case-specific fitness and immediate utility.
Demand for determinate settlement + associative imagination → title through antecedent person-object relations.
Founding present possession → restriction within established society → occupation, prescription, accession, and succession as differentiated title operations.
Graded possessory power + temporal weakening + conflicting salience → natural underdetermination → municipal stipulation → binary juridical closure.
Socially advantageous rule-system → interested observance → sympathetic moral approval → education, reputation, and political reinforcement → recursive institutional stabilization.
Partial passion + scarce transferable goods + social dependence → unstable possession and coordination failure.
Coordination failure + motivational circularity → elimination of innate justice and antecedent moral obligation.
Immediate self-interest → reflective redirection → reciprocal non-promissory convention.
Reciprocal convention → stable possession → constituted property, right, and obligation.
Constituted property → allocation gap → general-rule requirement.
General utility + associative imagination → temporally differentiated title forms.
Gradual and conflicting relations → municipal closure → integral juridical verdicts.
Systemic utility → sympathetic approval → internalized duty → recursive reinforcement of the conventionally constituted order.
The natural/artificial opposition is redrawn: natural passions and psychological associations generate artificial institutions whose necessity does not make them innate.
Property shifts from an object-quality or pre-social right into a norm-mediated relation constituted by duties, expectations, and socially secured title.
Possession and property become distinguishable: causal control supplies raw relational material, while justice converts selected possession into normative ownership.
Utility is decomposed into systemic necessity and moral sanction, while particular title-generation is reassigned primarily to imagination and positive settlement.
Self-interest is split into first-order destabilization and second-order institutional strategy, collapsing the opposition between egoistic passion and social order.
Impartiality shifts from an assumed motive to an institutional effect of universal and inflexible application.
Municipal law is reclassified from discovery of pre-existing natural right into authoritative completion of an underdetermined relational field.
Time becomes juridically productive: founding moments, duration, obscured origins, succession, and institutional sedimentation alter title without altering objects.
Moral obligation is separated from natural obligation and legal determination: interest establishes conduct, law determines relations, and sympathy supplies approbation.
Genealogical reading becomes mandatory: established categories such as property, right, duty, and justice cannot be projected backward to explain the processes that constitute them.
[Surface] The explicit objects are justice, stable possession, property, acquisition, title, adjudication, and the moral approval attached to their observance.
[Structural] Partial passions, scarcity, reciprocal expectations, general rules, associative imagination, municipal closure, and sympathetic reinforcement form the operative institutional system.

[Metastrategic] Explanation proceeds by reversing presumed dependencies: motives precede moral predicates, justice precedes property, systemic utility precedes approval, and legal decision completes rather than discovers natural determinacy.

[Ontological / Temporal] Reality contains no object-inherent property; juridical relations emerge gradually, change through temporal and institutional mediation, and become integral only through rule-governed recognition.

[Methodological / Performative] The system performs its thesis through successive elimination, inversion, differentiation, and forced closure: its method reproduces the passage from fluid natural materials to determinate artificial relations.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Inflexible juridical rules are generated from fluid, context-sensitive, and sometimes contradictory relations, leaving rigidity dependent upon materials that cannot themselves justify rigidity.
Justice is declared non-arbitrary at the systemic level, yet municipal law must stipulate boundaries for which no unique natural or utilitarian solution exists.
Property is constituted by justice, but the genealogy relies on pre-juridical possession; coherence requires strict separation between physical control and morally secured property.
General utility necessitates determinate title but underdetermines particular title, creating a gap between the justification of having a property system and the justification of its distributions.
Justice is both an offspring of passion and contrary to ordinary passionate conduct; the reconciliation depends on an implicit distinction between first-order impulse and second-order strategy.
Integral rights remain in tension with gradual possession, utility, associative force, and ordinary judgments of partial entitlement.
The convention is structurally intelligible as reciprocal expectation, but its exact historical emergence, thresholds of confidence, and transition into authoritative law remain underdetermined.
Self-love mutates from destabilizing appetite into reflective coordination once its object expands from immediate acquisition to preservation of the social system.
Possession mutates from causal power over an object into constant socially secured possession and then into an integral property relation.
Utility mutates from the cause of institutional necessity into an insufficient title criterion and finally into the object of moral contemplation.
Present possession changes valence from a peace-preserving founding rule into a seizure-authorizing principle that must be rejected in established society.
Public good changes from an absent originating intention into an emergent effect and then into the object that generates moral approbation.
Artificiality changes from a possible objection to justice into the positive name for passion’s second-order capacity to generate necessary universal order.
Reality is figured as a layered conversion machine: unstable passions become reciprocal expectations, expectations become rules, rules become rights, and rights become morally charged habits.
The subject is a partial desiring node capable of reflection, association, sympathy, and internalization rather than a pre-social bearer of complete rights or an impartial moral will.
Time is sedimentary and transformative: repetition creates confidence, duration alters title, institutional age weakens origins, and reinforcement converts artifice into second nature.
Law is a hard binary shell constructed over a graded field of possessory power, utility, salience, proximity, duration, and sentiment.

Navigation remains possible through reflective coordination, general-rule revision, and authoritative settlement, but not through escape to natural property, unrestricted equity, or case-by-case passionate judgment.

The global axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the cluster’s central machine: social instability, reflected interest, reciprocal convention, constituted property, relational title, legal closure, and subsequent moralization.

The system remains underdetermined concerning the exact historical emergence of convention, the relative causal weight of utility and imagination, and the thresholds governing possession, prescription, and comparative importance.
Coherence is preserved only if physical possession, constituted property, interested observance, legal determination, and moral approbation remain distinct explanatory moments.
The architecture is strongest where it reverses conceptual priority from property to justice and distinguishes utility’s demand for settlement from imagination’s production of particular title.

Reconstruction depends on sequencing and recursive return: convention must precede property, title determination must follow general stabilization, and moral sanction must feed back only after social utility becomes visible.
The element most resistant to axiomatic reduction is authoritative boundary production: the system demonstrates its necessity but cannot derive every decision from a common natural measure.

The reconstruction preserves the actual movement from motivational and ontological negation through institutional generation and juridical differentiation to practical closure and recursive moral reinforcement.

The central problem is to generate stable moral and political authority from partial passions, variable sympathy, limited benevolence, and fallible rulers without invoking reason, original contract, or unconditional command.

The cluster becomes a recursive naturalistic genealogy: interest and affect generate local valuations; social interaction generalizes them; generalized norms then exceed, correct, and sometimes reverse their originating conditions.
Public security, useful or agreeable character, and benevolent relational effects supply the first-order materials from which allegiance, virtue, and merit arise.
Because first-order sentiment varies with position, distance, interest, and fortune, moral stability requires general rules, common standpoints, and socially corrected judgment.
Evaluation therefore shifts from isolated acts and immediate outcomes to durable dispositions, natural tendencies, relational roles, and institutional functions.
Generalization gives normativity temporal reach: allegiance may persist after its immediate interest weakens, and virtue may survive accidental failure or attenuated sympathy.

Temporal persistence is not absoluteness: recurrent anti-functional conduct establishes a generalized counter-rule that converts anger into blame, cruelty into vice, and destructive government into resistance-authorizing tyranny.
The movement is spiral rather than linear: natural limitation → social stabilization → normative excess → corrective reclassification; closure is conditional, relational, and non-algorithmic.
[Persistent] Normative authority is generated within ordinary human nature: interest, pleasure, uneasiness, and sympathetically apprehended relations furnish its operative materials.
[Persistent] Human motivation is partial, variable, and passion-bound; neither rulers nor spectators occupy a naturally impartial or morally transformed position.
[Persistent] Sympathy makes the effects of qualities on others available to spectators who possess no direct private interest in those effects.
[Attractor] Shared moral order is produced by generalizing situated responses into stable rules, common standpoints, and publicly usable evaluative language.
[Persistent] The principal evaluative object is a durable tendency or function, not an isolated act, transient feeling, or accidental outcome.
[Mutating] Interest and utility change scope across the cluster: they uniquely sanction political allegiance but constitute only part of the plural basis of moral approval.
[Mutating] Artifice does not create ultimate value; it coordinates natural limitations and interests into promises, government, justice, good-breeding, and stable moral discourse.
[Emergent] Generalized judgment acquires relative autonomy from its origin: it can preserve obligation beyond immediate interest and preserve esteem despite weak affection, distance, or bad fortune.
[Emergent] A legitimate exception must itself be generalizable: repeated anti-functional conduct, not private injury or isolated failure, authorizes normative reversal.
[Persistent] Corrected judgment, occurrent affection, moral language, and practical motivation remain distinct layers and need not converge.

[Terminal] Offices, capacities, passions, and dispositions acquire moral valence from their direction and relational effects; systematic reversal of function produces reclassification from virtue or authority into vice or enmity.

[Attractor] The cluster converges on a conditionally ordered relational field: character is judged across its roles and government by its protective function, while no single utility calculus governs every moral source.
[Stable identity] Sympathy retains its function as affective transmission: another’s pleasures and pains become spectator sentiments capable of grounding approval, affection, blame, and hatred.
[Mutation] Interest moves from the cause of convention and exclusive sanction of allegiance to one evaluative relation among usefulness, immediate agreeableness, self-regard, and regard for others.
[Functional recurrence] The general point of view, common standard, general moral rule, and general opinion perform homologous work: they convert situated responses into socially stable verdicts.
[Reversal] Generalization first stabilizes allegiance and moral language, then becomes the mechanism by which recurrent abuses establish an exception to obedience.
[Domain expansion] Natural tendency migrates from the evaluation of personal dispositions under bad fortune to the evaluation of government under repeated historical performance.
[Absorption] The natural/artificial distinction ceases to divide sources of moral authority and instead marks different scales and mechanisms of coordinated benefit.
[Escalation] Neutral capacities become morally charged through direction: benevolence makes power useful, while ambition or cruelty converts capacity and office into magnified harm.

[Disappearance after structural work] Promise, custom, and imitation disappear as original grounds once they have exposed the need for a prior interest capable of generating and transmitting allegiance.

[Absorption after diagnostic use] Pride, tenderness, modesty, and heroic elevation remain local test cases, but their higher-order result is retained as evaluative pluralism and the separation of inward merit from social presentation.
[Mutation] Negative passion moves from constitutionally fitting anger to moral blame and, under public, recurrent, and severe injury, to resistance against tyrannical power.

[Local] The regress from promise through convention to interest is specific machinery for dismantling contractual allegiance; its scalable result is the dependence of artificial norms on prior human interests.

[Local] The detailed mechanics of pride, comparison, heroic elevation, and conventional modesty remain a stress test of the four-source moral system rather than a global account of political authority.
[Local] Tenderness and qualified anger establish the dual sources and degree-sensitivity of benevolent merit but do not independently determine the limits of allegiance.
[Scales upward] Correction for distance, private position, current disposition, and fortune becomes the cluster-wide mechanism for separating stable judgment from immediate affect.
[Scales upward] Evaluation by durable tendency scales from personal character to institutional function and supplies the shared grammar of virtue, vice, legitimacy, and tyranny.
[Bridge] Artificial justice and government are coordinated schemes whose moral standing depends on general benefit rather than the independent value of every isolated act.
[Catalyst] The distinction between originating cause and persisting moral rule forces the transition from simple causal genealogy to a temporal account of normative inertia and correction.

[Superseded] Utility monism, raw sympathetic intensity, isolated outcome evaluation, and absolute allegiance are jointly replaced by plural sources, corrected judgment, dispositional appraisal, and conditional authority.
Moral and political authority is not founded by affect-free reason, a prepolitical promise, or arbitrary political imposition.
Convention, custom, imitation, and education can transmit or regulate norms but cannot supply their original evaluative force.
Neither the spectator’s private interest nor raw sympathetic intensity can function as a stable universal standard.
Isolated action, accidental success, and momentary institutional performance do not exhaust the value of a durable disposition or function.
Moral generality does not require universal benevolence, equal emotional concern, or complete practical self-sacrifice.
Public utility does not exhaust virtue, even though public interest remains the specific natural sanction of political allegiance.
Office, power, capacity, naturalness, and immediate agreeableness do not carry self-validating moral worth.
Passive obedience is not absolute, but resistance is not authorized by every private injury; both obedience and opposition remain answerable to generalized public function.
The cluster cannot admit a self-grounding norm severed from human affect, interest, social practice, and relational consequence; such a norm would make its genealogies causally idle.
Radical affective incommensurability must be false: without transferable passions and sufficiently shared operations, neither sympathy nor common moral language could arise.
No positional privilege—first-person interest, spectator proximity, or political office—can confer universal evaluative authority.

General rules cannot be either identical with their immediate causes or wholly independent of them: identity would prevent stability, while independence would make correction and resistance impossible.

Accidental failure and stable anti-tendency cannot be morally indistinguishable; without their separation, bad fortune would destroy virtue and recurrent tyranny would remain protected as mere mischance.
Shared moral order cannot require convergence among verdict, affection, and action; human partiality would otherwise make stable discourse and generalized political judgment unavailable.
The absent center is an external moral tribunal: no view from nowhere, rational relation, natural sovereign title, or transcendent obligation terminates evaluation.
Universal affection is unavailable; generalized judgment substitutes for a motivational impartiality that ordinary human constitution cannot sustain.
Unmediated access to moral reality is unavailable: character and authority appear only through signs, inferred tendencies, historical patterns, and relational effects.
The system lacks a common metric capable of calculating conflicts among utility, immediate agreeableness, self-regard, fitting anger, and the threshold of intolerable tyranny.
An authority permanently immune to historical reversal is ontologically inadmissible: human frailty makes recurrent anti-function unavoidable and preserves the possibility of a counter-rule.
Corrected standpoint converts resistance from a response to private injury into a judgment that public protection has failed across a generalizable class of cases.

Dispositional evaluation distinguishes accidental failure from systematic anti-function: bad fortune need not destroy virtue, but recurrent oppression reveals a settled institutional tendency and cancels authority.

Government is evaluable as an artificial virtue operating through a coordinated scheme: its justification belongs to the general security it produces, not to the independent benefit of every governmental act.
Political power is a morally indeterminate capacity whose valence is fixed by direction: office can coordinate justice, but ambition or cruelty can turn the same capacity into enlarged public harm.
Sympathy supplies the missing moral link between public utility and disinterested judgment, allowing allegiance to be morally intelligible without an original promise.

A calm judgment that allegiance has ceased may precede effective resistance because generalized verdict, habitual obedience, private affection, and motivating passion operate at different intensities.

Fitting anger and legitimate resistance share a proportional structure: negative response becomes justified when harm is severe, attributable to durable agency, and no longer confined to isolated resentment.

Convention is a secondary coordination technology: custom transmits allegiance, good-breeding regulates pride, and social discourse stabilizes judgment, but none supplies the ultimate end by which it is assessed.

Political obligation remains more narrowly functional than virtue: immediate tenderness or agreeableness may confer merit on character, but cannot preserve allegiance after government systematically destroys public security.
The cluster produces a relational-dispositional ontology: persons and institutions are what their durable powers are fitted to produce for themselves and others under socially adequate conditions.

Moral objectivity becomes endogenous without becoming private: shared human constitution, sympathetic transmission, and standpoint correction stabilize judgments that no individual interest can dictate.
Normative time is layered: tendencies persist beneath accidents, rules persist beyond immediate causes, and repeated historical failure eventually changes the classification of the object.

Resistance becomes an internal operation of moral judgment rather than an external suspension of order: the same generalized functionality that authorizes allegiance also identifies its terminal failure.
Power has no autonomous moral title; its worth is derivative from the passions directing it and the relational field of benefit or injury it organizes.
The subject divides into partial agent, sympathetic spectator, corrected judge, and potential political resister; these positions communicate but do not collapse into one another.

The terminal moral order is plural but bounded: utility, immediate agreeableness, self-regard, and regard for others coexist, while role-destroying cruelty and protection-destroying tyranny mark outer limits.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Partial sympathy → contradictory situated judgments → conversational correction → common standpoint → stable moral language → renewed correction of situated judgment.

Insecurity → invention of government → public protection → allegiance → general-rule inertia → rulerly abuse → historical generalization → resistance exception → reaffirmation of protection as the criterion.
Conduct or expression → inference to character → sympathetic pleasure or pain → approval or blame → love, anger, and social response → new conduct and expression available for judgment.
Natural limitation → artificial coordination → stabilized conduct → acquired moral force → functional reassessment of the coordinating institution.
Immediate effect → correction for distance or fortune → evaluation of natural tendency → preservation under accidental failure or reversal under recurrent anti-function.
Uneasiness → anger or blame → attribution to durable harmful character → recurrence and public generalization → phase change from private resentment to legitimate resistance.

The dominant attractor is role-sustaining relational function: dispersed analyses of benevolence, character, justice, government, cruelty, and tyranny converge on whether a disposition makes shared relations supportable.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Human constraints: limited generosity + variable sympathy + insecurity + persistent rulerly passion.
Relational encounter: conduct, passion, or institution produces advantage, harm, pleasure, uneasiness, protection, or exposure.
Transmission: direct interest and sympathy convert relational effects into allegiance, approval, affection, blame, or anger.
Destabilization: distance, private interest, fortune, and divergent position generate variable or contradictory verdicts.
Generalization: common standpoint + general rule + social discourse correct local variation and stabilize evaluative language.
Object construction: isolated event → inferred durable disposition; individual benefit → coordinated scheme; office-holder → protective or destructive institutional function.
Temporal test: accidental failure preserves standing through natural tendency; recurrent anti-function generates vice, tyranny, and a generalized exception.
Terminal output: plural virtue + role-complete relational judgment + conditional allegiance + morally internal resistance.

Partial affection and public insecurity → relational effects → interest and sympathetic uptake → conflict among situated responses → common standpoint and general rules → dispositional-functional evaluation → normative stabilization → recurrent-failure test → conditional moral-political order.
Immediate sentiment → correction for distance and fortune → calm judgment → stable moral language, while practical passion remains only partially transformed.
Sustained beneficial tendency → virtue or authority; accidental obstruction → preserved standing; recurrent relational harm → vice or tyranny → anger, blame, or resistance.

Morality and politics become continuous in generative grammar without becoming identical in criterion: both arise from human effects and generalized judgment, but allegiance remains specifically tied to public protection.

The moral object shifts from event to architecture: durable character, relational disposition, coordinated scheme, and institutional function replace isolated action as the principal unit of evaluation.
Impartiality is reclassified from affective neutrality to socially corrected judgment compatible with unequal concern and limited motivation.
The natural/artificial opposition collapses as a division of moral sources and survives only as a distinction between immediate relational benefit and coordinated systemic benefit.
Obedience and resistance cease to be moral opposites: resistance becomes the generalized corrective form taken by allegiance when government reverses its constitutive function.
Power and ability are reclassified as directed capacities rather than intrinsic merits; benevolence, ambition, cruelty, and institutional role determine their social valence.
Time becomes evaluatively constitutive: tendency corrects fortune, habit extends obligation, and recurrent history supplies evidence for terminal reclassification.
Adequate reading now requires separation of cause, standard, verdict, motive, and presentation; treating them as one level would erase the system’s principal corrections and tensions.
Surface level: the cluster classifies benevolence, pride, anger, cruelty, political allegiance, tyranny, and resistance.
Structural level: sympathy, interest, general rules, corrected standpoints, dispositional inference, and artificial coordination produce stable moral and political judgments.

Metastrategic level: struggle is reframed as classification of tendencies and functions; intervention becomes legitimate when private grievance is converted into a general judgment of recurrent relational failure.

Ontological / Temporal level: reality consists of durable yet fallible affective agents and institutions whose standing persists through accidents but mutates under accumulated evidence of anti-function.
Methodological / Performative level: genealogical regress, objection-correction, analogical transfer, and stress cases perform the movement from situated response to generalized architecture.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Public interest is presented as the exclusive original sanction of allegiance, while virtue has four sources and benevolence two; the cluster supplies no rule determining how far moral pluralism enters political evaluation.
General moral opinion is declared infallible in the political argument, but elsewhere the common standard is a constructed correction whose mechanism and unique content remain underdetermined.

Natural tendency protects character from accidental outcomes, whereas allegiance is canceled by destructive performance; no exact criterion separates temporary failure from evidence of settled anti-function.
Calm verdict can diverge from actual affection and motivation, yet resistance requires practical mobilization; the passage from moral authorization to effective political action remains unspecified.
Utility, immediate agreeableness, self-regard, heroic elevation, tenderness, and fitting anger lack a common weighting rule, leaving conflicts among approved sources irreducibly qualitative.

Goodness is judged within a limited relational sphere, while allegiance appeals to public interest and general opinion; the transition from connected persons to the relevant political public remains compressed.
Moral rules must exceed their original causes to secure constancy but remain dependent on those causes to permit correction; the architecture requires this unresolved relative autonomy.
Interest mutates from causal origin of convention, to sanction of allegiance, to one sympathetically mediated source of moral approval.
General rule mutates from stabilizer of obedience into generator of the exception that terminates obedience.
Character mutates from an inferred personal disposition into a model for institutional identity, permitting the magistrate–tyrant distinction to be read as functional reclassification.
Anger mutates from an inherent, degree-sensitive passion into blame and finally into a generalized political response to recurrent public harm.
Artifice mutates from a suspected source of arbitrary moral invention into the necessary coordination layer through which natural interests and sentiments acquire stable social form.

Reality is implicitly a network of affective relays and functional arrangements: passions transmit, standpoints correct, conventions stabilize, and recurrent effects reclassify the nodes that produced them.
The subject is neither sovereign reason nor passive appetite but a divided agent-spectator whose local passions can be generalized in judgment without being extinguished in action.
Time is a layered filter: habit preserves rules, counterfactual tendency survives accidents, and accumulated history converts repeated failure into a phase change of moral status.

Struggle remains possible as functional diagnosis and generalized correction: one navigates between private resentment and passive obedience by identifying durable, public, and recurrent anti-function.

The cluster is reconstructible from six indispensable components: affective-interest genealogy, sympathy, corrected standpoint, dispositional tendency, artificial coordination, and generalized exception.

The reconstruction remains underdetermined at three points: the content of the common standard, the weighting of plural moral sources, and the threshold separating misgovernment from resistance-authorizing tyranny.
The system is coherent only if cause and moral rule, immediate affection and corrected judgment, accidental outcome and durable tendency, and private injury and public failure remain distinct.
The architecture is strongest where one generalizing mechanism explains both normative stability and corrective reversal, and where one dispositional grammar evaluates both character and government.

Reconstruction depends on recursive sequencing rather than source order: local sentiment must generate social correction, correction must produce temporal excess, and excess must encounter recurrent failure before conditional closure appears.

No indispensable structural component resists reduction, but the exact phenomenological weighting of pride, tenderness, anger, common opinion, and intolerable oppression remains irreducibly qualitative.

The governing problem is how a science confined to perceptual materials can explain mental productivity, ordered experience, factual assent, and practical reality without appealing to inaccessible essence or independently given forms.

The global thesis is anti-additive: simple content derives from impressions, while order, space, time, existence, and belief contribute no autonomous elemental content beyond the perceptions they organize or intensify.

The architecture differentiates three irreducible explanatory dimensions: provenance determines available content, relation and order determine configuration, and force determines cognitive and practical efficacy.
Sensation asymmetrically grounds ideas, but ideas return as productive relays within reflection, memory, imagination, association, belief, passion, and action.
Mental organization proceeds through preservation, release, recombination, associative weighting, and spatiotemporal arrangement rather than through either passive copying or sovereign creation.
Because existence adds no representational content, actuality is reconstructed as regulated vivacity transferred from present impressions through customary relations to absent or future ideas.

The subject consequently becomes a relay and regulator within a distributed perception-machine, while reality becomes operationally available through stable effects rather than intrinsic representation.
Anomalies and counterfeits do not terminate the machine; they recursively force universal claims to mutate into qualified regularities governed by provenance, steadiness, scope, and correction.

The movement is spiral: empirical restriction → perceptual decomposition → recursive mediation → relational organization → ontological de-addition → intensive actualization → second-order correction → bounded closure at unknown origins and unrepresented reality.
[Attractor] A science of human nature must reconstruct the perceptual medium through which evidence, inference, belief, and every other science operate.
[Persistent] Legitimate inquiry proceeds from experienced perceptions, operations, relations, and effects rather than from speculative access to mental or external essence.
[Persistent] Simple ideational content is asymmetrically dependent on antecedent impression-material, even when later ideas become causally productive.

[Emergent] Provenance, arrangement, and force constitute distinct explanatory coordinates: what an idea contains, how it is ordered, and how efficaciously it is conceived cannot be reduced to one another.
[Mutating] The idea is first a derivative copy, then a recombinable component, an associative node, and finally a force-bearing mediator of belief, passion, and action.
[Attractor] Mental production is asymmetrically recursive: sensory grounding remains one-way, while downstream perceptions repeatedly exchange the roles of effect, antecedent, and regulator.
[Emergent] Novelty is relational and intensive rather than elemental: new complexes, abstractions, expectations, and reality-effects arise without unprecedented simple content.
[Mutating] Order changes from a preserved feature of experience into a manipulable arrangement, an associative pathway, and the constitutive form of spatial and temporal appearance.
[Emergent] Stable mental regularity is generated by associative tendency and custom, which constrain transitions without imposing demonstrative necessity or abolishing imaginative variation.
[Persistent] Space and time are content-bearing orders of coexistence and succession, not independent impressions or empty containers.
[Emergent] Existence contributes no additional represented quality; factuality must therefore be generated through a difference in the manner and force of conception.
[Mutating] Force and vivacity develop from taxonomic marks into transmissible causal quantities, then into regulated quantities whose epistemic status depends on pedigree and steadiness.
[Emergent] A present impression anchors inference, supplies transferable vivacity, and gives absent or future objects current motivational efficacy.

[Attractor] Practical reality is stable, regulated presence within the perception-system: an idea becomes real for the mind insofar as it persistently governs inference, passion, expectation, and conduct.
[Emergent] Epistemic legitimacy is genealogical and second-order: it requires admissible content, permissible relational application, and a force-producing history capable of surviving correction.

[Terminal] Explanation terminates at maximally general experienced relations while sensory origins, associative attraction, external actuality, and the final authority of corrective rules remain undisclosed.
[Stable identity] Experience remains the admissible field from the initial science of human nature through compositional analysis and the genealogy of factual assent.
[Functional recurrence] Observation mutates into perceptual classification, source-audit, compositional decomposition, tracking of associative effects, and diagnosis of force-producing pedigrees.
[Escalation] The copy principle moves from a claim about simple ideas to a general constraint on imagination, abstraction, spatiotemporal predication, and existential representation.
[Mutation] The idea changes from faint effect into reflective cause, recombinable component, associated transition-node, and practically efficacious object of belief.
[Mutation] Order changes from a standard of mnemonic fidelity into the common machinery of recombination, association, extension, duration, and customary expectation.
[Domain migration] Association moves from a gentle relation among freely recombinable ideas into the customary mechanism that selects factual alternatives and transmits vivacity.

[Escalation and reversal] Vivacity progresses from perception-classification and mnemonic discrimination to belief-production, then reverses when poetry, passion, and madness show that intensity cannot warrant itself.
[Absorption] Existence disappears as an independent content-question after its non-addition becomes the constraint forcing factual difference into modal and causal explanation.
[Reversal] Separability first authorizes imaginative liberty, then becomes a negative test excluding empty space, bare time, and other structures detached from every positive content.
[Escalation] Causation migrates from temporal dependence and ideational association to productive capacity, social authority, force transmission, and the regulation of belief.
[Terminal transformation] Ignorance changes from a disciplinary deficiency into a constitutive boundary permitting operational explanation without essential, causal, or metaphysical completion.

[Disappearance through absorption] Separate faculty names lose final explanatory status as memory, imagination, judgment, passion, and volition become differentiated operations within one distributed perception-system.
[Local] The initial diagnosis of philosophical controversy motivates the metascientific project but does not govern the later machinery of order, association, and belief.
[Local] The missing shade remains an exception to strict copy-priority rather than an alternative source of the current-level architecture.
[Local] Exact mnemonic vivacity, the sensory source of extension, and content-filled minima remain local criteria whose broader function is only to constrain unconstrained separation.
[Local] The exhaustiveness of the three associative relations and the extension of causation into social subordination are domain-specific claims, not universal axioms of the whole meta-cluster.
[Scales upward] The prohibition on essence-first explanation becomes the common boundary governing perceptions, faculties, space, time, existence, belief, and reality.
[Scales upward] The copy principle becomes a general genealogy of admissible content, while the distinction between content and operation prevents genealogy from collapsing into passive replay.
[Bridge] Ideas connect sensory derivation to reflection, memory, recombination, association, factual belief, and practical action.
[Bridge] Association and custom connect relational order to intensive actuality by converting recurrent transitions into channels of transferred vivacity.
[Catalyst] Poetry, eloquence, passion, and madness are local cases that scale only as stress tests forcing belief to mutate from raw vividness into regulated intensity.

[Superseded and recoded] Linear copy chronology, passive receptivity, sealed faculties, empty forms, and intrinsic actuality-markers are replaced by asymmetrical recursion, relational organization, and second-order genealogy.
Mental science is not deduction from a known substance, essence, or standpoint external to the faculties under investigation.
No operation of memory, imagination, abstraction, association, or belief can generally originate unprecedented simple content.
Copy-dependence entails neither passive replay nor preservation of every original conjunction, order, intensity, or practical effect.
Relations, order, space, and time are not independent substances or additional simple impressions superadded to their terms.
Existence and belief are not predicates or representational components attached to an otherwise incomplete object-idea.
Mental regularity is neither demonstrative necessity nor random succession; factual assent likewise cannot be generated by conceptual contradiction alone.
No intrinsic semantic feature distinguishes an actual object from the same object merely conceived, and no positive representation discloses extra-perceptual being as such.
Felt intensity, imaginative completeness, repetition, or rhetorical force cannot independently authenticate factual conviction.
The subject is neither a sovereign creator nor an autonomous judge insulated from custom, association, affect, bodily condition, and recursive correction.
Scientific adequacy does not require access to ultimate sensory causes, the metaphysical basis of association, or the intrinsic nature of external actuality.
The architecture requires the falsity of any model in which cognition can ground itself from outside perceptual mediation.
It excludes first-cause foundationalism: knowledge of stable derivative relations cannot depend on prior disclosure of their ultimate origin.
It rejects both the passive receptacle and sovereign producer, requiring a mind that transforms inherited materials without becoming their absolute source.
It disqualifies independent forms and empty frameworks: no positive order, space, time, relation, or generality survives the removal of all content-bearing terms.
It excludes direct representational realism and any intrinsic actuality-sign capable of transporting thought beyond perceptual content into the essence of external being.
It excludes rationalist factuality: conceivability, contradiction, and necessary connection cannot select among contrary matters of fact.
It cannot identify causal genesis with epistemic warrant, because the same associative and intensive mechanisms can produce ordinary belief, education, persuasion, fiction, and pathology.
It cannot admit an independent tribunal of correction without violating perceptual closure, yet it cannot abandon correction without collapsing factual belief into successful vivification.
The first governing absence is absolute sensory origin: sensation grounds the entire machine while the cause of its first appearance remains outside it.
The second governing absence is pure order without ordered content: relation, empty space, bare time, and wholly indeterminate generality are inadmissible.
The third governing absence is a necessary mental bond: association and custom occupy its functional place while remaining defeasible tendencies.
The deepest ontological absence is positively knowable mind-independent actuality; reality persists as correlate, anchor, and corrective term without becoming represented essence.
The absent subject is a sovereign spontaneous origin capable of creating content, governing transitions, and certifying its own beliefs without inherited impressions or natural tendencies.
The terminal absence is a noncircular authority for general rules: correction must regulate force from within the same customary perception-system whose products it evaluates.
Restriction of primitive content produces rather than suppresses mental productivity: impression-derived elements become recursively recombinable, associatively routable, and intensively variable.
The full architecture requires a three-axis audit: genealogy tests content, relational analysis tests configuration and application, and force-pedigree tests factual assent.
Space, time, existence, and belief obey one de-additive rule: apparent higher-order structures are reconstructed as arrangements or modes of perception rather than additional ingredients.

Ideas are the machine’s central switching elements because they preserve sensory derivation while serving as causes of reflection, units of recombination, nodes of association, and bearers of practical reality.
Association becomes the bridge between formal order and factuality: recurrent relations first stabilize imaginative transitions and then channel vivacity from present impressions into belief.
Time has a dual generated structure: succession produces duration, while present impressions project force across succession so that remembered, absent, and future objects act now.

Fiction divides along two independent axes: a complex may be compositionally legitimate because its materials are admissible yet doxastically counterfeit because its vivacity lacks regulated factual pedigree.
Epistemic reading must become recursively genealogical, tracing not only where an idea’s content originated but also how its arrangement and degree of conviction were produced.

The system yields practical realism without positive metaphysical realism: perceptually generated ideas can organize conduct as realities despite lacking an intrinsic representation of independent actuality.

Power operates through two linked channels: productive capacity associates authority and obedience, while rhetoric, repetition, and affect modulate the vivacity by which such relations become practically compelling.

The system’s principal operator is also its principal debt: causation establishes perceptual dependence, associative priority, social power, force transfer, and corrective pedigree before its own nature is secured.
Because corrective rules arise within the same associative field they regulate, epistemic security can only be reflexive, comparative, and qualified rather than absolutely foundational.
The meta-cluster produces an anti-additive ontology: apparent mental and formal entities are reconstructed as sourced contents, relational configurations, or intensive modes.
Mind becomes a distributed transformation machine rather than a substance or faculty hierarchy: it receives, copies, preserves, separates, routes, intensifies, and regulates perceptions.
Actuality becomes a system-effect generated when admissible content is placed within a stable associative route and supplied with regulated practical force.
The subject is decentered twice: it is neither the source of primitive content nor the sovereign author of the order and force by which its ideas govern it.
Time is neither an empty continuum nor simple chronology; it is generated succession recursively reorganized by memory, expectation, custom, and present force-transfer.
Agency becomes navigational: freedom consists in recombination, selective attention, rerouting, and reflective correction within constraints imposed by content, association, and affect.
Scientific foundation is converted into recursive self-audit: secure inquiry tracks sources, relations, force-transfers, anomalies, and corrections while refusing claims to absolute origin.

Political and rhetorical vulnerability is structural rather than accidental because the same relational and intensive machinery that enables authority, expectation, and action also permits capture by repetition, eloquence, and passion.
The machine generates qualified naturalism: explanatory closure belongs to recurrent operations and effects, while metaphysical closure is systematically withheld.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Total production loop: sensation → idea → reflection → memory or imagination → associative routing → belief → passion and action → renewed vivification or reflective correction.

Restriction–proliferation loop: simple content is constrained → complexes are recombined → relations stabilize transitions → force actualizes selected complexes → new reflective effects return to the system.
Genealogical audit loop: impression-source → permissible operation → application test → force-pedigree → correction → renewed audit of the resulting perception.
Order loop: experienced arrangement → mnemonic conservation → imaginative release → associative regeneration → spatiotemporal constitution → customary expectation.
Actualization loop: present impression → customary transition → transferred vivacity → factual belief → practical efficacy → passion → amplified object-idea.
Counterfeit-correction loop: nonstandard vivification → belief-like force → error or capture → source-reflection → general-rule discounting → graded restoration of conviction.

Boundary loop: inquiry reaches inaccessible origin or reality → withdraws to observable effects → formulates a qualified regularity → encounters anomaly → restricts scope without abandoning the machine.

Attractor convergence: ideas organize recursive production, order organizes relational form, regulated vivacity organizes actuality, and inaccessible reality remains the recessed term around which correction circulates.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Scientific dependence on human faculties → human nature installed as the metascientific field.
Unavailable essence and ultimate origin → experienced perceptions, operations, relations, and effects become the admissible evidence.
Perceptual decomposition → impressions/ideas + simple/complex → isolable units of provenance and operation.
Sensory grounding + ideational return → asymmetrically recursive perception-chain.
