Recurrence differentiated by force and fidelity → memory preserves experienced order while imagination releases components for recombination.
Free recombination + recurrent regularity → resemblance, contiguity, and causation weight transitions without necessitating them.
Analysis of organized content → coexistence and succession reconstructed as extension and duration rather than empty forms.
Existential non-addition + content invariance → factual difference relocated from representation to manner of conception.
Present impression + customary relation → transferred vivacity → steady intensified idea → belief → passion and action.
Affective amplification or counterfeit vivification → source-sensitive reflection and general rules → qualified correction without metaphysical closure.
Foundational disorder → human faculties identified as the common medium of scientific judgment.
Human mediation → empirical restriction → mental life decomposed into perceptions and genealogical dependencies.
Linear copy genealogy → division of impressions → ideas become recursively productive mediators.
Productive ideas → memory/imagination bifurcation → separation and recombination of inherited contents.
Free recombination → associative regulation → stable but defeasible relational pathways.
Relational analysis → space and time reconstructed as content-bearing coexistence and succession.
Existential non-addition → belief-surplus problem → customary force-transfer → practical actualization.
Counterfeit vivacity → second-order genealogy → regulated conviction → unresolved return to unrepresented reality.
Foundation is reclassified from possession of first causes into disciplined reconstruction of perceptual provenance, organization, and force.
Mind is remapped from substance and faculty hierarchy into a recursive field of perceptions differentiated by source, order, transition, and intensity.
Content, relation, and force become separable analytic dimensions, allowing identical materials to support memory, fiction, abstraction, belief, or practical action.
The opposition between receptivity and productivity collapses into asymmetric recursion, while the opposition between freedom and determination collapses into bounded, tendency-weighted navigation.
Space, time, existence, and belief are removed from the category of independent additions and redistributed among arrangement, succession, manner, and force.
Fact and fiction become neighboring configurations differentiated not by elemental content but by composition, associative route, steadiness, provenance, and practical efficacy.
Causation becomes a cross-domain operator spanning perceptual genealogy, associative transition, productive capacity, social authority, belief-generation, and affective feedback.
Reading becomes operational and second-order: apparent entities must be decomposed into sources, configurations, force-transfers, exclusions, and corrective histories.
[Surface] The explicit field comprises human nature, impressions, ideas, memory, imagination, association, space, time, existence, belief, passion, fiction, and factual judgment.

[Structural] Copying, recurrence, separation, recombination, associative routing, ordered coexistence and succession, force-transfer, affective feedback, and correction form one distributed mechanism.
[Metastrategic] Metaphysical disputes are converted into audits of perceptual origin, relational operation, permissible application, causal pedigree, and susceptibility to correction.

[Ontological / Temporal] Reality available to thought consists of content-bearing events and configurations; time is generated succession recursively reorganized by memory, custom, expectation, and present practical force.

[Methodological / Performative] The system performs its claims by decomposing apparent unities, denying unsupported additions, reconstructing operational relations, testing them against anomalies, and replacing universality with qualified recursive regulation.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Causal succession, associative efficacy, force-transfer, and causal pedigree do indispensable explanatory work before causation itself has received a secured analysis.

The copy principle strains against the missing shade, abstraction’s selective suppression of detail, and the use of separability to deny forms that cannot be detached from every content-bearing instance.
The declared observational science of ordinary conduct remains incompletely integrated with introspective taxonomy, deprivation tests, and phenomenological judgments of force.
Association is both an original tendency and a customary acquisition, leaving unresolved how innate relational susceptibility and learned pathways divide explanatory labor.
Perceptual closure denies positive access to external actuality, yet sensory causation, reality-connection, and correction continue to invoke it as an operative constraint.
Force and vivacity classify impressions, memory, imagination, belief, passion, and counterfeit conviction without a stable metric or exact threshold across these functions.

Custom generates ordinary factual assent, but education, repetition, rhetoric, and pathology can use the same mechanism to generate invalid assent; causal genesis and warrant remain only partially separated.
General rules correct first-order force but lack an independently specified origin and authority, risking circular dependence on the beliefs and customs they are meant to regulate.
The science intended to secure all inquiry remains reflexive because it uses perception, comparison, causal inference, custom, and correction to establish the authority of those same operations.
Idea mutates from derivative copy into the common relay connecting sensation, reflection, recombination, order, association, belief, and action.
Order mutates from retained arrangement into a productive relation, spatiotemporal form, customary route, and condition of expectation.
Association mutates from a nonnecessary bond among ideas into the causal channel through which present experience selects factual alternatives and transfers vivacity.
Force mutates from a mark of perception-type into a transmissible psychological currency and then into a regulated quantity whose source matters more than its raw magnitude.
Existence mutates from an explicit ontological object into a zero-addition rule, while reality mutates into a causal and corrective relation governing belief.
Fiction mutates from lawful recombination into genealogical or doxastic excess when either its application outruns perceptual order or its vivacity imitates factual authority.
Reality is imaged as an asymmetrically grounded network of content-bearing events whose copied elements circulate through recursive circuits of order, association, and force.
The mind is an archive-workshop-routing system: it preserves sequences, cuts and recombines components, weights pathways, transfers intensity, and applies corrective feedback.
The subject is a switching relay and regulatory threshold rather than an originating substance; natural tendencies, habits, passions, bodily states, and reflection compete to direct its ideas.
Time is a pulse of content-bearing succession folded by memory and expectation, with present impressions drawing absent and future objects into current causal efficacy.

Navigation consists in tracing provenance, decomposing arrangements, following associative routes, measuring force by pedigree, correcting counterfeits, and stopping where perceptual relations no longer support explanation.
The current-level axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the engine if provenance, relational order, and intensive force remain distinct but recursively connected dimensions.
The strongest architecture is the conversion of restricted perceptual content into relationally productive and practically efficacious ideas without granting autonomous elemental creation.
The system is coherent at the operational level provided genetic priority, relational configuration, intensive manner, causal genesis, and epistemic warrant are not collapsed into one order.
The architecture remains underdetermined at the mechanisms of ideational return, associative attraction, vivacity transfer, exact thresholds of belief, and the authority of corrective rules.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only through sequencing and recursive return: sensory grounding must precede recombination, recombination must generate association, and existential non-addition must precede intensive belief.
The indispensable residues resistant to axiomatic reduction are sensory origin, the lived quality of force, mind-independent actuality, causal necessity, and the noncircular basis of correction.

The minimal reconstruction succeeds as a bounded naturalistic machine, not as metaphysical closure: it explains how perceptions generate order and reality-effects while preserving the absences that make such explanation necessary.

The central problem is how the same natural mechanisms can generate warranted causal judgment, metaphysical fiction, operational selfhood, affective valuation, and social hierarchy without access to intrinsic powers or an external rational tribunal.

The governing thesis is that relation-conditioned transitions become effective through force, vivacity, repetition, and retention; their outputs depend on how comparison, custom, circumstance, and social topology route them.

At this scale the argument becomes a recursive naturalistic reconstruction: substantial bearers, intrinsic powers, autonomous faculties, and primitive passions are displaced by networks of perceptions, affects, transitions, gates, and feedback.
The directional movement is foundational subtraction → operational transition → productive overextension → anomaly or contradiction → restrictive differentiation → socially recursive application.
Comparison becomes the principal branching operator: controlled difference isolates causal circumstances, while retained contrast converts another’s condition into an altered estimate of the self.

The social-affective field is not an external application of the cognitive system; it exposes how vivacity, authority, custom, and relation recursively produce the objects, values, and judgments they appear merely to register.
The subject accordingly mutates from a rejected substantial bearer into a temporally variable relay, represented object, comparator, and feedback-node within cognitive and social processes.

Closure is operational and recursively skeptical: inquiry preserves tested mechanisms while denying final decomposition, intrinsic value, affective neutrality, and any standpoint outside the operations under examination.
[Persistent] Legitimate explanation begins from perceptions, affects, experienced conjunctions, and observable transformations rather than from unknown substances or intrinsic productive powers.
[Persistent] Relation is causally effective only through the transitions it facilitates, preserves, interrupts, or redirects; it is not an inert predicate or an intrinsically binding nexus.
[Mutating] Force and vivacity migrate from determinants of conviction into the general currency by which cognitive, affective, and social representations become operative.
[Persistent] Repetition, habit, and custom stabilize transitions without converting psychological regularity, practical necessity, or social circulation into truth.
[Attractor] Imagination is the indispensable medium of synthesis and the endogenous source of fictive completion, overextension, constructed sentiment, and self-confirming error.
[Mutating] Comparison changes from controlled experimental differentiation into affective opposition, retaining the common operation of preserving difference while reversing its epistemic function.

[Mutating] Causation expands from regular conjunction among discriminated circumstances into gated conversion and recursive feedback in which effects alter subsequent causes, judgments, and relations.
[Emergent] Anomalies and contradictions reveal unrestricted principles by their excesses and force their conversion into range-bound, threshold-dependent mechanisms.
[Attractor] Normative correction is immanent: broader comparison, discriminating variation, skeptical restraint, and recursive audit regulate the same natural operations that generate error.
[Mutating] The self has no warranted status as a substantial origin but remains operative as a vivid relay, represented object, temporal comparator, and socially altered magnitude.
[Persistent] Natural production and felt efficacy do not establish representational truth, epistemic warrant, intrinsic value, or source-fidelity.
[Emergent] Social value is generated in circulation: transmitted satisfaction, reflected judgment, comparative opposition, and recursive uptake constitute rank and self-estimation.
[Emergent] Relational proximity and intensity possess no intrinsic valence; they amplify whichever epistemic, sympathetic, or comparative transformation controls the route.
[Emergent] Time is an active operator of projection, attenuation, retention, durable attribution, and feedback rather than a neutral container for stable objects and subjects.

[Terminal] The viable endpoint is a reflexive science of human nature that preserves empirically useful causal and affective mechanisms under permanent semantic, experimental, skeptical, and relational correction.
[Stable Identity] Experienced conjunction remains the minimum causal input, although its output expands from expectation to bodily influence, affective conversion, and social feedback.
[Escalation] Vivacity moves from explaining unequal conviction to animating belief and passion, then becomes the transmissible currency of a social-affective network.

[Mutation] Imagination changes from a producer of causal expectation and fictive object-unity into the general medium of cognition, then into a simulator capable of constructing another’s absent emotion.
[Functional Recurrence] Custom recurs as first-order projection, second-order regulation, affective stabilization, and constructive expectation, with renewed overextension at every phase.
[Reversal] Comparison changes from a corrective instrument that exposes suppressed differences into a social operator that preserves difference as inverse self-estimation.
[Migration] Relation migrates from conjunction, separability, and spatial compatibility into cognitive gating, self-reference, social proximity, directed transmission, and comparative interaction.
[Terminal Transformation] The self moves from an absent invariant bearer to an operational object and finally to a socially constituted relay-comparator whose states are generated through feedback.

[Escalation] Cause shifts from whole-object identity to operative circumstance, then to domain-specific conversion, and finally to nonlinear circuits in which generated passions modify their own conditions.
[Mutation] Contradiction changes from a stimulus for metaphysical repair into a diagnostic of unrestricted transition and then into a controlled anomaly for reconstructing social-affective routing.

[Disappearance] Substance, autonomous reason, intrinsic value, primitive social instinct, and sovereign selfhood disappear after their explanatory work is redistributed across relation, force, custom, comparison, and feedback.
[Lower-Layer Local] Particular rules for isolating causal circumstances remain local experimental instruments; their scalable function is recursive differentiation under counterinstance.
[Lower-Layer Local] Spatial compatibility, soul-substance, immortality, and the exact gates of pride and humility remain local problems rather than current-level explanatory centers.
[Lower-Layer Local] Fame, wealth-esteem, pity, envy, malice, and the constitutional conjunctions of love or hatred remain local outputs of the broader relational machine.
[Scaled] Relation-mediated force scales upward as the common architecture connecting belief, causal inference, affective conversion, and social valuation.

[Bridge] Experimental circumstance-analysis and affective threshold-gating jointly establish that causal mechanisms are individuated by controlled differences in routing, not by whole-object classification.
[Bridge] The operational self of the skeptical and affective analyses becomes the relay-comparator required by social transmission and reflected valuation.
[Catalyst] Social anomalies demonstrate that unchanged content or objective condition can generate opposed effects, forcing causation to include sequence, topology, retention, and mode selection.
[Recoded] Causal identity is recoded from an intrinsic power or whole object into a reproducible transformation distributed across input, relation, force, gate, and feedback.
[Current-Level Emergent] Philosophy becomes a reflexive regulation of cognitive and social-affective machinery rather than a separate faculty judging nature from outside.
No substantial bearer, intrinsic causal power, or affective essence is required where relations and transformations among perceptions can perform the explanatory work.
No autonomous reason, sovereign self, or neutral tribunal can validate cognition and value independently of imagination, habit, affect, and social relation.
Relation is not static, symmetric, intrinsically efficacious, or valence-bearing; its force depends on direction, continuity, comparison, competition, and mediation.
Stable content, representation, or objective condition does not guarantee stable belief, judgment, passion, or value.
Imagination and custom can neither be granted unrestricted authority nor eliminated, because both successful operation and systematic error depend on them.
No unrestricted explanatory principle survives: causal uniformity, pure understanding, universal relation, and primitive passion-laws all require domain, threshold, or circumstance restrictions.
Neither felt conviction nor sympathetic uptake guarantees warrant, truth, intrinsic worth, or faithful access to another’s interior state.
No final correction abolishes custom, closes causal decomposition, fixes self-worth, or establishes a nonparticipatory position outside the relational system.
The architecture requires the falsity of any model that assigns cognition, passion, and social valuation to autonomous faculties governed by independent laws.
It requires an external standpoint to be unavailable: correction must occur through reorganized experience, comparison, custom, and relation rather than through an Archimedean criterion.
It excludes purely linear causality because belief reinforces repetition, passion recruits judgment, esteem amplifies satisfaction, and altered relations become new causes.
It cannot admit an invariant subject whose identity, rationality, and worth remain insulated from temporal force, remembered relation, testimony, and comparison.
It excludes universal commensurability: epistemic warrant, conviction, pleasure, welfare, public esteem, and comparative self-value cannot be reduced to one scale.
It also excludes absolute irregularity, because recursive correction requires provisionally stable kinds, repeatable transitions, retained impressions, and reproducible relational effects.
It cannot admit an affect-free methodology, because evidential uptake, inquiry, skeptical recovery, authority, and correction remain operations of force within human nature.
The system is organized around an absent metaphysical interior: neither causal power, substantial self, nor another person’s authentic feeling is directly available as an explanatory ground.
The deepest unavailable possibility is a common metric capable of aligning truth, felt conviction, welfare, social esteem, and self-worth.
No view from outside human nature can determine the legitimacy of custom, imagination, sympathy, or comparison without using those same operations.
No final alignment joins what nature produces to what is true or good; natural belief, practical stability, social value, and affective intensity can all diverge from warrant and welfare.
The architecture lacks a general metric for mode selection and activation: it cannot finally specify when custom becomes rule, relation becomes force, or sympathy yields to comparison.
Final repose is inadmissible because every stabilization can become a new habit, fiction, hierarchy, or compound circumstance requiring renewed differentiation.

Causal judgment and social passion are two scales of one natural engine: relation organizes transition, force makes it operative, and gating determines whether the result becomes inference, fiction, attachment, or comparison.
Comparison bifurcates normatively: controlled difference corrects causal projection, whereas retained contrast can intensify envy or self-elevation without improving truth-tracking.

The distinction between warrant and conviction extends into the social field: authority, praise, familiarity, and reflected esteem can amplify assent or self-belief independently of evidential regularity.
Once the substantial self is removed, cognitive and social analyses converge on a subject constituted by incoming force, retained relations, comparative positioning, and recursive self-attribution.
Constructive sympathy extends the theory of endogenous error: a representation can generate a real affective consequence even when it does not faithfully reproduce its alleged source.

General rules are simultaneously corrective and productive: they can restrain prejudicial inference, stabilize inquiry, or construct expected passions that reinforce the social model from which they arose.
Causal explanation becomes irreducibly recursive in the social domain because outputs such as belief, hatred, esteem, and envy alter the judgments and relations governing subsequent transitions.

Strategic intervention follows the same logic as experiment: instead of positing new faculties, alter authority, proximity, concurrence, associative continuity, or comparative framing and observe the transformed output.

Social topology becomes epistemically relevant because testimony and judgment acquire force through authority and relation; inquiry must therefore distinguish evidential content from its route of affective uptake.
Moderate skepticism cannot require affective neutrality; it must regulate the unavoidable forces by which custom, curiosity, testimony, and social relations sustain inquiry.
Ontology becomes an operational field of heterogeneous events connected by recurrent, force-bearing, and directionally weighted transitions without known substantial support.
The subject becomes a distributed effect of organization: impressions, habits, memories, testimony, comparisons, and reflected sentiments converge temporarily as self-reference.

Epistemic normativity becomes topological and regulatory: warrant depends on how transitions survive counterinstance, variation, competing routes, and recursive feedback rather than on their subjective force alone.
Social reality is causally productive rather than representationally secondary: circulated affect generates rank, self-estimation, attachment, antagonism, and the evidential force of judgments.
Time becomes recursively constitutive: repetition projects futures, distance modulates conviction, retention enables comparison, and reflected consequences become new present causes.
Human agency is non-sovereign but strategically variable: subjects cannot suspend the machinery of transition, yet they can alter routes, circumstances, associations, and comparative fields.
Error is not external noise but productive excess internal to successful machinery; every mechanism capable of stabilizing cognition or society can also fabricate ontology, sentiment, or hierarchy.
The science of human nature becomes experimentally recursive: anomalies are treated as variations revealing hidden routing conditions rather than as immediate grounds for inventing new faculties.
No ethical or epistemic virtue inheres in connectedness itself; intensified relation can support disciplined comparison, prejudice, sympathy, rivalry, or self-confirming passion.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Repetition → custom → facilitated transition → vivified belief or action → renewed conjunction forms the basal cognitive loop.
Fluent transition → projected unity or power → contradiction → fictive repair or controlled differentiation forms the principal epistemic bifurcation.
General mechanism → anomalous output → restrictive gating → provisional stabilization → renewed anomaly forms the meta-cluster’s dominant escalation sequence.
Inquiry → skeptical intensification → affective interruption → natural restoration → constrained inquiry forms the recurrent anti-foundational spiral.
Sign or condition → represented affect → vivacity transfer or construction → passion → judgment or desire → altered condition forms the social feedback loop.
Satisfaction → sympathetic esteem → reflected esteem → intensified satisfaction forms a status-producing loop in which social value recursively augments its own cause.
Comparison → altered self-position → passion → attention to the comparative relation → intensified or severed comparison forms the recursive rivalry loop.
“Relation” becomes the principal machine when it expands from observed connection into a directed infrastructure governing inference, attribution, simulation, comparison, and intervention.
Human nature is the hidden attractor: causal method, skeptical regulation, selfhood, passion, and social hierarchy converge on the recursive organization of relation-mediated force.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Initialize heterogeneous perceptions, qualities, pleasures, pains, persons, and represented conditions without an independently appearing support.
Organize inputs through conjunction, resemblance, contiguity, succession, self-reference, authority, proximity, durability, and directed relational pathways.
Add force through vivacity, pleasure, pain, passion, retained impression, or customary propensity; relation without force remains explanatorily incomplete.
Repetition and general rules stabilize transitions into expectation, attribution, self-reference, and socially anticipated affect.
Route stabilized force through causal projection, imaginative completion, sympathetic appropriation, or comparative opposition to generate belief, object-unity, passion, and social value.
Detect excess through contrary instance, fictive ontology, contradictory belief, affective overgeneration, reversed valence, or self-confirming judgment.
Bifurcate excess into simulated closure or controlled restriction through semantic audit, circumstance-analysis, skeptical diffidence, threshold-gating, and relational rerouting.
Feed generated beliefs and passions back into custom, judgment, authority, reflected esteem, and comparative positioning, thereby modifying subsequent inputs and routes.
Submit every provisional stabilization to renewed variation, including the rules, classifications, and social models produced by earlier correction.
Terminate only metaphysical completion: preserve recursive empirical and social-affective inquiry while withholding final necessity, intrinsic baseline, and external validation.
Hidden substance, intrinsic power, autonomous reason, and primitive passion → demand for experiential and operational justification.
Justificatory demand → decomposition into perceptions, qualities, affects, conjunctions, and relations.
Decomposition → relation-conditioned transition animated by force, vivacity, repetition, and custom.
Animated transition → belief, projected unity, apparent placement, self-attribution, sympathy, and comparison.
Unrestricted transition → prejudice, metaphysical fiction, contradictory belief, affective overgeneration, and reversed social valence.
Excess and anomaly → controlled difference, semantic restraint, skeptical restriction, relational gating, and mode differentiation.
Restricted mechanism → recursive belief, reflected esteem, passion-generated judgment, and strategic alteration of relational routes.
Recursive feedback → nonterminal science of human nature constrained by experiment and skepticism but lacking final thresholds, intrinsic baselines, or external closure.
The substance–faculty map is replaced by a field of heterogeneous events, directed relations, force-bearing transitions, and recursive outputs.
Reason, imagination, passion, and error cease to name autonomous agencies and become differently regulated phases of one natural economy.
Causation is redrawn as a transformation architecture: conjunction supplies repeatability, relation supplies routing, force supplies efficacy, and gating supplies differential output.
The self is reclassified from hidden bearer to a temporally extended and socially permeable relay-comparator.
Evidence becomes multidimensional: comparative regularity determines warrant, vivacity determines uptake, and social topology determines which judgments acquire force.
Comparison is split into experimental discrimination and affective inversion, dissolving any assumption that heightened contrast is intrinsically rational or irrational.
Social hierarchy is reclassified as recursively generated affective adjacency rather than the passive registration of intrinsic rank.
Error becomes a phase of productive machinery whose limits are disclosed through overgeneration rather than a foreign corruption added to otherwise pure faculties.
Intervention and interpretation shift from naming hidden entities to varying circumstances, tracing routes, separating force from content, and testing how feedback transforms the field.
Surface level: causal judgment, substance and soul, skeptical inquiry, pride and humility, reputation, affection, pity, envy, and malice appear as distinct explicit problems.
Structural level: relation, repetition, vivacity, imagination, comparison, custom, retention, and feedback generate and differentiate the surface phenomena.
Metastrategic level: inquiry intervenes by widening comparison, varying circumstances, restricting overgeneralization, and rerouting authority or proximity rather than invoking new faculties.
Ontological / Temporal level: reality is a field of heterogeneous events in ordered and retained relations; identity, causation, selfhood, and value are provisional products of temporal organization.
Social / Political level: authority, publicity, custom, reflected esteem, proximity, and comparison distribute the force by which judgments and hierarchies become operative.

Methodological / Performative level: the architecture performs its thesis by producing excess, converting anomaly into controlled variation, and recursively subjecting its own rules and stabilizations to renewed audit.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The same custom and imagination generate error and correction, leaving the distinction between legitimate and illegitimate transition immanent and never completely secured.
Necessary connection is denied, yet causal method depends on strong uniformity, stable kinds, and reproducible transitions whose practical authority exceeds their ontological grounding.
A common transition architecture must explain heterogeneous outputs, but each domain introduces gates and constitutional supplements that resist complete unification.
The substantial self is rejected, yet correction, passion, memory, and comparison require persistent self-reference whose continuity remains operationally necessary but ontologically unspecified.
Force and relation are indispensable explanatory variables, but no quantitative rule determines sufficient vivacity, adequate repetition, decisive relation, or conversion threshold.
Sympathy and comparison can derive opposed affects from the same condition, but the architecture lacks a general selector determining which mode dominates.
Nature restores belief, action, and affective order without vindicating them, preserving a structural separation between practical efficacy and epistemic or ethical legitimacy.

Corrective inquiry is itself socially and affectively routed through authority, curiosity, testimony, and vivacity, threatening any claim that experimental regulation is insulated from the mechanisms it diagnoses.
Relation mutates from observed conjunction into a directed and weighted infrastructure for causation, self-reference, sympathy, comparison, and intervention.
Vivacity mutates from a measure of conviction into the common activation threshold for belief, passion, social transmission, and self-alteration.
Imagination mutates from associative completion into a general productive medium and finally into constructive social simulation.
Comparison mutates from experimental control into a social operation that converts retained affect into inverse self-evaluation.
The self mutates from excluded substance into operational object and then into a socially generated magnitude within recursive feedback.
Cause mutates from whole-object identity into discriminated circumstance, gated conversion, and feedback circuit.
Skepticism mutates from denial of intrinsic power into recurrent regulation of cognitive and social-affective mechanisms without terminating their operation.

Reality appears as a recursive laboratory-network: heterogeneous events form nodes, relations form weighted pathways, force animates transmission, and feedback continually alters the field being investigated.
The subject is a permeable relay-comparator that receives force, projects expectation, simulates others, measures itself through retained differences, and returns the result as judgment or action.
Time is a nested circuit rather than a line: repetition becomes projection, retained affect becomes comparison, durable attribution becomes identity, and reflected consequence becomes new cause.

The remaining struggle is over routing rather than transcendence: viable correction alters circumstances, relations, authorities, associations, and comparative distances while remaining inside the machinery of human nature.

The axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the meta-cluster if unsupported heterogeneity, relation-mediated force, customary stabilization, differential gating, recursive feedback, and immanent correction are retained together.
The architecture remains underdetermined concerning stable kinds, adequate repetition, causal individuation, mode selection, relation thresholds, and the continuity of the operational self.
The system is coherent at this scale as a recursive operational naturalism, not as a deductive foundation, unified metric, or final reconciliation of cognition and affect.

Its strongest architecture is the conversion of failed intrinsic explanations into a distributed machine capable of generating belief, error, selfhood, passion, hierarchy, and their correction from related operations.
Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if foundational subtraction is followed by operational return, and operational return by anomaly, restriction, feedback, and renewed audit.

The architecture is weakest where it assigns regulatory authority to broader custom, experiment, moderation, or social certification without fully deriving their superiority from the machinery they regulate.

The indispensable residue resistant to axiomatic reduction is differential force and selection: neither the intensity activating a transition nor the rule choosing among projection, sympathy, direct survey, and comparison is fully calculable.

The central problem is how mediated, partial, historically variable affect can generate stable property, justice, moral judgment, and political authority without intrinsic value, innate right, or an external normative tribunal.

The governing thesis is that normative order is an endogenous construction: affective forces are redirected through repetition, reflection, reciprocal expectation, generalization, and institutional determination until they acquire authority over their own conditions of origin.

At this scale, the argument becomes a recursive naturalistic genealogy joined to a functional test: it reconstructs the genesis of norms and then evaluates them by the relational effects they durably produce.

The movement proceeds from object-side value to affective mediation, from mediated passion to convention, from convention to constituted juridical objects, and from institutional utility to generalized moral authority.

Relation becomes the trans-scalar operator: it transfers affect, associates persons with goods, establishes duties, communicates consequences, and supplies the field in which character and authority receive moral classification.

Repetition converts outputs into conditions: encountered force becomes inclination, reciprocal restraint becomes convention, convention becomes second nature, and generalized judgment becomes normative inertia.
Stability is necessary but nonterminal: rules must resist local passion, yet accumulated anti-function can reactivate correction and reverse property claims, moral standing, or political allegiance.

The real movement is spiral and sedimentary: affect generates artifice, artifice reorganizes affect, moralization stabilizes artifice, and historical failure returns the stabilized system to functional reassessment.

Closure is conditional and distributed: shared operations unify the architecture, but instinctive endowment, stipulative boundaries, plural moral sources, and qualitative thresholds prevent reduction to one mechanism or final algorithm.
[Persistent] Pleasure, pain, interest, uneasiness, sympathy, and acquired concern are the indispensable materials from which social and normative order must be generated.

[Attractor] Affective, juridical, and moral value is relationally constituted: objects, goods, persons, dispositions, and offices acquire force or status through mediated relations rather than intrinsic properties alone.
[Persistent] Present force and authority are path-dependent effects of prior encounters, repeated conduct, stabilized expectations, institutional history, and accumulated evaluations.
[Mutating] Partiality is both destabilizing material and generative resource: immediate passion produces conflict, while reflected, coordinated, and generalized partiality produces durable order.
[Mutating] Reflection is not a sovereign source of value; it changes the scale, temporal horizon, and organization of passions already in operation.

[Persistent] A generated category cannot explain its own genesis: acquired ends cannot presuppose antecedent concern, justice cannot presuppose property, and allegiance cannot presuppose contractual obligation.
[Attractor] Artifice is necessary without being arbitrary when durable natural limitations require second-order coordination but do not independently determine the form of that coordination.
[Persistent] Convention begins as mutually legible, conditionally reciprocal conduct whose repetition stabilizes expectation before explicit moral obligation or authoritative command.

[Terminal] Institutions constitute normative objects: stabilized possession becomes property, coordinated benefit becomes justice, and protective function becomes political authority only within rule-governed relations.
[Emergent] Integral rights and stable verdicts require imposed closure because their affective, possessory, utilitarian, and relational grounds remain gradual, conflicting, and underdeterminate.

[Mutating] Utility changes function across the architecture: it motivates coordination, necessitates institutions, sanctions rule-systems, and tests political authority, but does not uniquely determine every title or exhaust moral merit.
[Mutating] Sympathy expands from affective transmission into institutional sanction and standpoint generalization, while never becoming universal benevolence or complete motivational impartiality.
[Attractor] Impartiality is manufactured by general rules, corrected standpoints, and invariant application rather than discovered in an originally impartial subject.
[Persistent] Durable tendency, coordinated scheme, and relational function outrank isolated action, immediate consequence, and accidental outcome as objects of normative evaluation.
[Emergent] Generated norms acquire relative autonomy: they can outlast their immediate motives, redirect later passions, and authorize judgments unavailable at the moment of their origin.
[Terminal] Legitimate reversal must itself be generalized: accumulated, public, and recurrent anti-function—not isolated dislike or private injury—can terminate established authority.
[Terminal] The resulting order is endogenous, relational, plural, and conditionally stable; no single affective, legal, utilitarian, or moral mechanism completes every stage.

[Stable identity] Pleasure and pain remain the basic currency, but their function expands from direct affective modulation into support for inclination, institutional observance, moral approval, blame, and resistance.
[Domain expansion] Relation moves from association and affective transfer to juridical attachment and finally to the evaluative field in which dispositions and institutions acquire moral identity.

[Functional recurrence] Repetition successively produces habit, reciprocal confidence, institutional sedimentation, stable moral language, and historical evidence of durable function or anti-function.

[Mutation] Stability changes from affective relief into possessory security, juridical rigidity, normative inertia, and finally a condition vulnerable to reversal when it protects recurrent anti-function.

[Escalation] Sympathy begins as inter-organismic communication, becomes approval of public utility, and culminates in corrected moral judgment capable of evaluating strangers, institutions, and political effects.
[Mutation] Cognition shifts from an affective channel-selector into reflective interest, genealogical correction, and standpoint adjustment; its function is organizational rather than value-creating.
[Reversal] Self-interest changes from immediate acquisitive disruption into reciprocal restraint and then into allegiance to a system whose generalized rules can oppose immediate interest.

[Mutation] Utility moves from an affectively mediated input to the necessity of settlement, then to institutional sanction, and finally to a functional criterion capable of withdrawing political authority.

[Reversal] General rules first suppress local variability and preserve authority beyond immediate causes; recurrent public failure then produces a counter-rule that authorizes reclassification and resistance.

[Absorption] The natural/artificial distinction is absorbed into a layered model in which natural affects and limitations supply materials while artificial coordination produces objects, rules, standpoints, and second-order dispositions.

[Terminal transformation] Normative objects cease to appear antecedent to their relations: affective value, property, moral character, and political authority become stabilized outcomes of mediation, institution, and functional judgment.

[Local] Species comparison, cognitive thresholds, excitatory bands, and the detailed mechanisms of curiosity remain affective diagnostics; their scalable result is the mediated and phase-sensitive constitution of motivation.

[Local] Occupation, prescription, accession, succession, and municipal title rules remain juridical implementations; their scalable result is that gradual relations require socially imposed determinacy.
[Local] Pride, tenderness, anger, allegiance, and tyranny remain differentiated moral-political cases; their scalable result is evaluation by durable relational tendency and generalizable exception.

[Scales upward] Affective mediation becomes the substrate of institutional genesis: passions can be redirected, transferred, and stabilized because they are not fixed responses to intrinsic object-values.

[Scales upward] Path-dependence becomes sedimentary social ontology: repeated encounters create inclinations, repeated restraint creates convention, and repeated evaluation creates stable authority or evidence of anti-function.
[Bridge] Affective transfer and sympathy connect individual passion to public normativity by allowing generated force and perceived consequences to cross persons, practices, and institutions.
[Bridge] Relation and imagination connect affective association to juridical and moral object-construction: the same relational field joins ideas, persons, goods, duties, and evaluative roles.
[Catalyst] The possibility that conduct generates its later motive scales into the claim that observance can precede duty and that institutional authority can be retrospectively moralized.

[Recoded] Instinct, scarcity, limited benevolence, and shared affective constitution are retained not as complete explanations but as boundary conditions constraining what recursive construction can generate.

[Superseded] Intrinsic value, pre-social property, naturally impartial motivation, and absolute political title are replaced by mediated force, constituted relation, corrected judgment, and conditional function.
No intrinsic object-quality is sufficient to determine affective force, juridical ownership, moral merit, or political authority.
Sovereign reason, innate justice, and an affect-free moral standpoint cannot originate the architecture.
Pre-social property, natural right, promise, or contract cannot explain institutions that must first constitute rights, duties, and authoritative expectations.
Universal benevolence and motivational impartiality cannot generate or continuously sustain general social rules.
Utility cannot serve as a self-executing and exhaustive measure of affect, title, virtue, or every particular institutional act.
Stable order cannot remain continuously responsive to immediate feeling, private interest, isolated need, individual merit, or case-specific optimization.
Natural relations do not contain the binary boundaries required by property, legal decision, stable moral verdict, or political classification.
Isolated consequences, accidental outcomes, or singular failures cannot determine the status of a rule, disposition, or institution independently of its durable tendency.
Neither repetition nor generalization guarantees permanent reinforcement: accumulated stability may terminate affect, conceal injustice, or generate a counter-rule against recurrent anti-function.
No office, law, property distribution, moral consensus, or political authority is absolutely immune to historical reclassification.
A fixed subject–object ontology must be false: both subjects and objects must remain penetrable by affective history, social expectation, and relational classification.

The pre-social individual cannot be a complete rational, proprietary, and moral subject; capacities for agency persist, but rights, duties, impartial verdicts, and authority emerge only through social mediation.
Self-grounding normativity is inadmissible: no moral predicate, right, obligation, or authority can function simultaneously as its own originating motive and generated result.
Institutions cannot be merely external restraints on antecedently complete agents and objects; they must reorganize motivations and constitute the relations they govern.
Legal and moral determinacy cannot mirror an equally determinate natural terrain, because psychological, possessory, sympathetic, and functional grounds remain graded and conflicting.

General rules can be neither reducible to their immediate causes nor wholly independent of them: reduction would eliminate normative persistence, while independence would eliminate functional correction.
Impartiality cannot require an impartial motivational center; it must be produced through public rules and corrected judgment while agents retain unequal concerns.
Linear time and monotonic reinforcement must be false: iteration must be capable of producing inclination, sedimentation, inertia, exhaustion, prescription, and terminal reversal.
Correct judgment, emotional attachment, institutional validity, and practical motivation cannot be required to converge, because the system depends on their temporal and functional separation.
The absent center is an intrinsic or transcendent source of normativity capable of grounding affective value, property, morality, and authority before mediation.
No common measure determines the thresholds among engagement and languor, possession and property, misgovernment and tyranny, or partial sentiment and stable public judgment.
The unavailable social order is one simultaneously natural, perfectly stable, exactly distributive, universally affectionate, continuously equitable, and responsive to every singular case.

A self-identical subject standing prior to affective and institutional history is unavailable; the subject appears only as a provisional configuration of acquired inclinations, expectations, roles, and standpoints.

Final adjudication beneath convention is unavailable: causal endowment, association, utility, sympathy, and functional tendency constrain decisions but do not eliminate stipulation or qualitative judgment.

An authority permanently insulated from historical reversal is inadmissible, because generated authority remains dependent on the relational function whose stabilization originally made it intelligible.
Affective mobility makes convention possible: force generated in immediate passion can be transferred into reflected interest, reciprocal restraint, and attachment to a rule-system.

Conduct can precede the motive later attributed to it at every scale: repeated action generates inclination, observance precedes moral duty, and institutional benefit precedes sympathetic approbation.
Institutions are affective path-engineers: by stabilizing expectations and classifications, they alter the passions, interests, and judgments entering subsequent encounters.
Relation is an ontological generator across scales: it vivifies affect, attaches titles, distributes duties, and converts durable effects on others into moral identity.

Sympathy undergoes institutional amplification: direct transmission supplies the natural capacity, contemplation of public utility sanctions rules, and standpoint correction converts variable sympathy into stable evaluative language.

Stability contains its own reversal condition: the same repetition that creates tranquillity, convention, and normative inertia can produce exhaustion, rigid injustice, or evidence of recurrent anti-function.

Effective agency is second-order rather than sovereign: agents act by redirecting passions, coordinating expectations, inhabiting general rules, correcting standpoints, and mobilizing generalized judgments.
The shared method is priority reversal: object-value is subordinated to mediation, property to justice, obligation to interested observance, and political title to protective function.
Constructive plasticity remains bounded: affect requires initial valence, justice requires durable scarcity and partiality, and moral judgment requires sufficiently shared sympathetic capacities.

The absence of common threshold metrics makes closure increasingly practical: affective regulation, juridical decision, moral weighting, and political resistance all require non-algorithmic determination.
Practical objectivity is secured by stabilized relations and generalized functional judgment rather than intrinsic truth, natural title, or private intensity.
Generalization is doubly productive: it first converts variable conduct into stable norms and later converts accumulated failures into a counter-rule capable of revising those norms.

Affective value, property, moral character, and political authority form one escalating ontology of constituted relations: each becomes real through stabilized effects, expectations, and classifications.
Normativity becomes endogenous without becoming private: it originates in ordinary passions but acquires public stability through convention, general rules, and corrected judgment.

The subject is institutionally installed rather than merely restrained: habits, property relations, public expectations, moral language, and political roles become components of its practical identity.
Agency consists in recursive self-redirection: passions are not abolished but reorganized through reflection, rule-following, standpoint correction, and functional reassessment.
Social time is constitutive and phase-changing: iteration creates inclinations and rights, sedimentation produces authority, and accumulated counter-evidence transforms established status.
Institutions operate as affective conversion machines: they transform partial interest into restraint, restraint into rights, utility into approval, and recurrent injury into generalized resistance.
Law and morality divide closure functions: law produces determinate relations where natural grounds remain gradual, while morality generalizes relational effects without requiring uniform affection.
Resistance is internal to generated order: because authority derives from stabilized public function, recurrent destruction of that function activates the architecture’s own reversal mechanism.

Legitimacy is recursively maintained rather than foundationally possessed: it depends on continuing relations among observance, determinacy, public benefit, generalized approval, and historical performance.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Affective-institutional loop: mediated passion → repeated conduct → inclination → reciprocal expectation → convention → rule-governed identity → internalized sentiment → renewed conduct.
Partiality loop: immediate interest → conflict → reflective enlargement of interest → reciprocal restraint → systemic benefit → stronger interest in maintaining the system.
Sympathetic-generalization loop: perceived consequence → transmitted pleasure or pain → variable approval → common standpoint → stable verdict → revised perception of subsequent consequences.
Relational escalation: conjunction → affective transfer → possessory expectation → juridical attachment → role-defined obligation → moral classification.
Sedimentation loop: repetition → confidence → rule → second nature → normative inertia → expanded reproduction of the rule.
Rigidity-correction loop: general rule → suppressed local variation → stable order → accumulated anti-function → generalized counter-rule → authoritative revision or resistance.
Object-construction escalation: sensible or causal relation → affective salience → stabilized expectation → property or character attribution → public status → historically revisable identity.

The dominant attractor is supportable relational order: affective regulation, determinate property, moral evaluation, and political authority converge on sustaining predictable relations without erasing the possibility of correction.
Phase change is the recurrent dynamic: degree-sensitive accumulation transforms pleasure into languor, possession into right, observance into duty, and abuse into tyranny.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Initial conditions: sensitive endowment + partial affection + cognitive inequality + scarcity + social dependence + fallible power.
Relational encounter: objects, persons, actions, and institutions produce pleasure, pain, interest, resistance, benefit, insecurity, or harm through mediation.
First-order output: partial passions generate inclination, acquisition, conflict, sympathy, approval, resentment, or immediate allegiance.
Recursive redirection: reflection, repetition, and comparison enlarge temporal horizons and convert immediate outputs into motives for coordinated conduct.
Conventional stabilization: mutually legible restraint + repeated reciprocity → confidence + general expectations + non-promissory convention.
Constitutive transformation: stabilized expectations → justice, property, duty, coordinated scheme, and role-defined authority.
Determinate closure: utility demands settlement; relation and imagination propose form; general rules and positive decision produce integral boundaries.
Moralization: visible systemic effects + sympathetic uptake + corrected standpoint + education and reputation → stable approval and internalized obligation.
Functional-temporal test: accidental failure preserves standing; persistent relational benefit reinforces authority; recurrent anti-function produces reclassification.
Conditional closure: endogenous normativity + determinate but revisable institutions + plural moral sources + generalized exception.

Mediated affect → partial conflict and variable judgment → reflective redirection → reciprocal convention → constituted rights and roles → determinate rules → sympathetic moralization → normative inertia → recurrent-failure test → correction or resistance.
Natural limitation → artificial coordination → relational object-construction → public authority → relative normative autonomy → historical functional reassessment → conditional closure.

Affective relation → acquired concern → stable possession → property → coordinated justice → generalized moral judgment → protective authority → recurrent anti-function → vice, tyranny, or resistance.
Affect, law, morality, and politics become successive organizations of one relational field rather than autonomous domains governed by independent faculties.

The natural/artificial opposition is replaced by a distinction between first-order materials and second-order organization: artifice coordinates natural passions without becoming either innate or arbitrary.
Objects of valuation are reclassified as generated relations: affective value, property, character, and authority depend on histories of mediation, expectation, and function.
Impartiality is relocated from motive to procedure: invariant rules and corrected standpoints make public judgment possible without equal affection.
Time becomes constitutive rather than contextual: repetition creates affective dispositions, juridical titles, moral inertia, and evidence for terminal reclassification.
Law is reclassified as authoritative completion of a graded relational field, while morality is reclassified as generalized evaluation of durable effects and functions.
Obedience and resistance cease to be external opposites: both become phase-dependent expressions of the same functional criterion of public supportability.

Adequate reading must separate cause, mediator, constituted object, rule, verdict, motive, temporal phase, and reversal condition; collapsing these levels reproduces the circular explanations the system dismantles.

Stability and correction become complementary rather than contradictory: rigidity is required to create common objects, while generalized functional reassessment is required to prevent rigidity from becoming unconditional domination.
[Surface level] The explicit objects are affective variation, habit, curiosity, justice, possession, property, moral merit, political allegiance, tyranny, and resistance.

[Structural level] Mediation, transfer, repetition, reflected interest, reciprocal expectation, relation, imagination, general rules, sympathy, and functional testing form one recursive production system.

[Metastrategic level] Intervention requires diagnosing phase and scale: whether a force should be redirected, a relation stabilized, a boundary stipulated, a judgment corrected, or an institution reclassified under recurrent anti-function.

[Ontological / Temporal level] Reality consists of historically accumulated relational configurations whose status can persist beyond immediate causes yet change through repeated performance and public reassessment.

[Methodological / Performative level] The architecture performs its thesis through differential variation, genealogical inversion, staged constitution, objection-driven correction, and terminal stress-testing of stabilized categories.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The system’s processual construction depends on natural saliences, shared affective operations, scarcity, limited benevolence, and social dependence whose origins it does not reconstruct.

Affective causes are phase-sensitive and reversible, while justice requires inflexible rules; the transition from plastic motivation to rigid institutional form remains functionally necessary but causally compressed.
Utility bears multiple burdens—motivation, necessity, sanction, and functional test—without providing a common metric for titles, plural virtues, or competing political judgments.
Integral rights and stable verdicts arise from gradual relations and qualitative comparisons, leaving determinacy dependent on closure that exceeds its justificatory materials.

Norms must exceed their originating passions to govern conduct yet remain dependent on those passions and functions to permit correction; this relative autonomy cannot be resolved into identity or independence.
General standpoints and public rules manufacture impartiality, but the system does not uniquely derive their content or guarantee that stabilized consensus is correct.

Thresholds remain unspecified across the architecture: engagement versus exhaustion, reciprocal conduct versus convention, possession versus title, failure versus anti-function, and misgovernment versus tyranny.
Corrected verdict can diverge from attachment and motivation, while institutional change and resistance require practical force; the conversion of authorization into action remains underdetermined.
Artifice is non-arbitrary at the level of necessity but stipulative at particular boundaries, leaving functional legitimacy unable to justify every inherited distribution or decision.
Relation mutates from an affective mediator into a juridical constitutor and then into the ontology of moral and political identity.
Repetition mutates from habit-forming iteration into convention, normative inertia, and finally accumulated evidence for reversal.
Self-interest mutates from destabilizing acquisition into reflected coordination, interested observance, and allegiance to generalized public function.
Sympathy mutates from direct affective communication into institutional moralization and corrected public judgment.
Utility mutates from mediated motivational input into institutional necessity, systemic sanction, and criterion of political persistence or failure.
General rule mutates from stabilizing expectation into socially corrected judgment and then into the counter-rule that terminates established authority.
Artifice mutates from a suspected deviation from nature into the positive recursive capacity by which natural limitations produce necessary but revisable social form.

Reality appears as a recursive conversion network: affect circulates, repetition channels it, convention hardens it, institutions assign it objects, sympathy moralizes it, and history tests its products.
The subject is a permeable, divided switching-point—desiring agent, habitual participant, rights-holder, sympathetic spectator, corrected judge, and possible resister.

Time is sedimentary and catastrophic: ordinary repetition accumulates inclinations, expectations, and authority until thresholds produce stabilization, exhaustion, prescription, or terminal reclassification.
Law is a hard shell over graded affective and relational material, while morality is a mobile public sensor testing whether the shell continues to sustain its constitutive function.

Navigation consists neither in escaping artifice nor submitting unconditionally to it, but in regulating affect, maintaining determinate relations, correcting standpoint, and generalizing evidence of recurrent failure.

The meta-cluster is reconstructible from eight indispensable components: mediated affect, path-dependent transfer, reflected partiality, reciprocal convention, constituted juridical relations, determinate closure, sympathetic generalization, and functional reversal.
The architecture is coherent at this scale as a recursive and plural genealogy of endogenous normativity, but not as a reduction to one psychological, legal, utilitarian, or moral mechanism.
It remains underdetermined at the origins of natural salience, the thresholds of convention and reversal, the content of common standards, and the production of particular authoritative boundaries.

The architecture is strongest where it reverses explanatory priority and shows generated relations becoming causally efficacious: passion precedes motive, justice precedes property, and public function precedes authority.

Reconstruction depends on recursive sequencing: affect must precede coordination, coordination must precede right, right must precede moralization, and accumulated performance must precede terminal reclassification.

The indispensable remainder resistant to axiomatic reduction is practical boundary production: qualitative thresholds, juridical stipulations, common-standpoint content, and the mobilization of authorized resistance cannot be fully derived from a common measure.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if generated normativity is retained as both sedimented and revisable; flattening it into natural fact, arbitrary convention, or transcendent command would destroy the meta-cluster’s engine.

The governing problem is how perception-bound human nature can generate knowledge, factual reality, selfhood, affective order, property, morality, and political authority without access to substance, intrinsic power, natural right, or an external tribunal.

The global thesis is operational and anti-substantialist: contents are inherited from perception and affect, relations organize them, force activates them, repetition stabilizes them, and recursive institutions convert stabilized effects into objects, identities, and norms.

Apparent additions—formal structures, intrinsic powers, substantial selves, objective values, natural rights, and unconditional authority—are repeatedly decomposed into sourced materials, directed relations, intensive differences, temporal pathways, and rule-governed effects.

The architecture is recursively productive: ideas become causes of reflection and action, beliefs become causes of passions, passions alter judgment and relation, and generated conventions and institutions reorganize the agents and materials that produced them.

The directional movement is empirical restriction → perceptual decomposition → relational and intensive production → customary stabilization → social feedback → conventional constitution → moral generalization → functional correction or resistance.
The subject moves from a denied substantial origin to a cognitive relay, affective comparator, socially represented object, rights-bearing participant, corrected judge, and possible resister.
Time escalates from ordered succession into customary projection, recursive feedback, institutional sedimentation, normative inertia, and threshold-driven reversal.

Error, contradiction, counterfeit force, social anomaly, and institutional failure are productive stressors that expose unrestricted mechanisms and convert them into qualified rules, differential gates, or generalized counter-rules.

Closure is asymmetrical: metaphysical completion remains unavailable, cognition closes provisionally through correction, law imposes determinate boundaries, and political legitimacy remains conditionally reversible under recurrent anti-function.
[Attractor] Human nature is the medium within which evidence, reality, agency, value, and authority must be reconstructed and through which every reconstruction must itself operate.

[Persistent] Legitimate explanation begins from perceptions, affects, experienced relations, observable operations, and recurrent effects rather than from inaccessible substances, essences, powers, or intrinsic values.

[Persistent] The system produces no ex nihilo content, affective valence, or normative authority: higher-order novelty arises by reorganizing constrained perceptual, affective, natural, and social materials.

[Attractor] Relation is the trans-scalar operator that organizes perception, association, causation, self-reference, affective transmission, comparison, possession, duty, moral identity, and political function.
[Mutating] Force develops from a difference among perceptions into transferable vivacity, affective activation, social efficacy, institutional adherence, and practical authority.
[Mutating] Repetition and custom move from stabilizing mental transitions to producing expectations, selves, social values, conventions, rights, moral inertia, and evidence for terminal reversal.

[Attractor] Generated effects recursively become causes: ideas, beliefs, passions, reflected judgments, conventions, rules, and institutions return to reorganize subsequent perception, conduct, and relation.

[Mutating] Imagination is both the productive medium of synthesis and the endogenous source of fictive completion, projected unity, social simulation, and institutionally mediated object-construction.
[Emergent] Comparison is a branching operator: controlled variation can correct projection, retained contrast can produce rivalry, and generalized standpoint-comparison can stabilize public judgment.

[Mutating] The self has no warranted status as a substantial origin but remains operationally indispensable as relay, temporal comparator, represented object, institutional participant, and recursive locus of attribution.

[Emergent] Practical reality consists in stable relational efficacy: factual objects, social ranks, property, character, and authority become operative through regulated effects, expectations, classifications, and conduct.
[Persistent] Natural production, subjective force, social circulation, and institutional stability do not by themselves establish truth, warrant, merit, justice, or legitimacy.

[Attractor] Correction is immanent and recursive: source-audit, comparison, controlled variation, general rules, corrected standpoints, and functional reassessment regulate mechanisms from within the same system that generates error.

[Emergent] Time is constitutive and phase-changing: succession permits memory and projection, repetition creates disposition and authority, and accumulated performance can transform status rather than merely extend it.
[Emergent] Artifice is necessary without being arbitrary when natural constraints underdetermine the second-order forms required for stable coordination, judgment, and authority.

[Emergent] Agency is second-order navigation: intervention alters attention, association, comparison, circumstance, authority, expectation, rule, and institutional route rather than escaping the machinery of human nature.

[Terminal] The system closes as bounded recursive naturalism: explanatory operations are preserved, metaphysical foundations are withheld, determinate institutions remain revisable, and no stabilization is exempt from renewed audit.
[Stable identity] Experience remains the admissible field from perceptual genealogy through causal experiment, affective analysis, institutional genesis, and political reassessment.
[Escalation] Genealogy expands from tracing ideational content to tracing conviction, self-attribution, social value, property, obligation, and political legitimacy.

[Absorption] The idea begins as a derivative switching element and is progressively absorbed into the broader categories of representation, simulated condition, social classification, and constituted normative object.
[Domain expansion] Relation moves from perceptual arrangement and association into causal routing, affective transmission, social topology, juridical attachment, and moral-political identity.
[Escalation] Force progresses from perceptual classification to belief-production, affective activation, social circulation, institutional observance, and practical authority.
[Terminal transformation] Repetition changes from recurrence into custom, feedback, convention, second nature, normative inertia, and finally accumulated evidence capable of authorizing reversal.
[Mutation] Imagination changes from recombination and associative completion into factual projection, metaphysical fiction, constructive sympathy, and social object-production.
[Reversal] Comparison begins as source-sensitive differentiation, reverses into affective opposition and self-estimation, and is recoded as corrected public standpoint.
[Escalation] Causation moves from perceptual dependence and customary transition to gated conversion, social feedback, institutional path-production, and historical reassessment.
[Mutation] Reality moves from regulated factual presence to socially productive representation and finally to historically stabilized juridical, moral, and political status.
[Terminal transformation] The subject changes from non-originating relay to temporal comparator, socially permeable self-reference, institutionally installed participant, and possible resister.
[Reversal] General rules first regulate conviction and suppress local variation, then produce stable public judgment, and finally become counter-rules capable of revising authority.

[Terminal transformation] Ignorance and skepticism cease to be merely privative: they become permanent controls that prohibit metaphysical completion while preserving operational inquiry and conditional authority.

[Disappearance] Substance, autonomous faculties, intrinsic powers, pre-social rights, and sovereign reason disappear after their explanatory functions are redistributed across materials, relations, force, repetition, gates, and institutions.
[Local] The missing shade, exact mnemonic fidelity, perceptual minima, and the sensory specifications of extension remain local tests of the early content-genealogy.

[Local] The exact inventory of associative relations, the detailed status of empty space and time, and particular classifications of fiction remain subordinate implementations of the de-additive architecture.
[Local] Particular experimental rules, questions of spatial compatibility, soul-substance, and the exact gates of pride and humility remain domain-specific instruments or targets.
[Local] Named passions, title doctrines, legal modes of acquisition, and particular political cases remain local outputs of broader relational and institutional machinery.
[Domain-bound] Utility scales as motive, sanction, and functional test but does not become a universal metric of truth, title, virtue, or every institutional decision.
[Scales upward] The prohibition on essence-first explanation governs the treatment of mind, causation, self, value, property, morality, and authority.
[Scales upward] Relation-mediated force becomes the common architecture connecting factual belief, passion, social valuation, institutional adherence, and political efficacy.
[Bridge] Ideas, imagination, and represented conditions connect perceptual derivation to belief, sympathy, comparison, social object-construction, and moral classification.
[Bridge] Custom and repetition connect mental regularity to social expectation, reciprocal convention, institutional persistence, and normative inertia.

[Catalyst] Counterfeit belief, contradictory affect, reversed social valence, and recurrent institutional failure scale upward as anomaly-mechanisms forcing restriction, differentiation, and reversal.

[Superseded and recoded] Passive copying, sealed faculties, linear causation, pre-social subjects, intrinsic value, and unconditional authority are replaced by recursive production, distributed routing, constituted objects, and conditional legitimacy.
No known substance, essence, intrinsic power, or metaphysical interior is required where experienced relations and transformations perform the explanatory work.
No faculty, imagination, institution, or normative procedure can originate its materials, valences, or authority absolutely from itself.
Relation, order, space, time, selfhood, value, and authority are not independent additions separable from the terms, histories, and operations they organize.
No necessary connection or unrestricted causal principle governs every transition; circumstance, direction, threshold, competition, and feedback remain indispensable.
Felt vivacity, affective intensity, social circulation, repetition, or institutional endurance cannot independently authenticate truth, value, or legitimacy.
The subject is neither sovereign origin nor affect-free judge; it cannot stand outside custom, imagination, comparison, social relation, and institutional history.
No intrinsic object-quality determines factual actuality, social rank, property, moral merit, or political authority.
Pre-social property, natural right, promise, contract, or allegiance cannot explain institutions that first constitute the relevant rights, duties, and authoritative expectations.
Natural production cannot be equated with epistemic or ethical validity: custom can produce prejudice, imagination fiction, sympathy distortion, and institutions hierarchy or injustice.
No autonomous rational tribunal, universal benevolence, or originally impartial motive can supply final correction.
No law, verdict, social hierarchy, property distribution, or political authority is permanently exempt from historical and functional reclassification.
The architecture requires the falsity of any model in which cognition or normativity can ground itself from a standpoint outside perceptual, affective, social, and historical mediation.
It excludes a fixed source–object ontology: objects and subjects must remain transformable by relation, force, attribution, expectation, and institutional history.
It rejects both passive receptivity and sovereign production, requiring constrained materials to become productive through recursive organization without acquiring absolute spontaneity.
It excludes linear causality and neutral chronology because beliefs reinforce habits, passions recruit judgments, institutions reshape motives, and accumulated effects alter later causes.
It cannot identify genealogy with warrant: the same production mechanisms yield ordinary belief and delusion, sympathy and rivalry, convention and domination.
It cannot admit a self-identical subject prior to mediation, because continuity, self-value, rights, roles, and judgment are all operationally or institutionally produced.
It excludes self-grounding normativity: factuality, property, obligation, impartiality, and authority cannot be presupposed as explanations of their own production.
It cannot admit a universal metric or algorithm capable of determining adequate force, sufficient repetition, decisive relation, proper title, correct verdict, or legitimate reversal.
It cannot admit final stabilization: correction, convention, law, moral consensus, and political authority remain products of mechanisms capable of generating new error, rigidity, and anti-function.
The absent origin is an unmediated ground capable of supplying sensation, causal power, selfhood, value, and normativity prior to every relation and operation.
The unavailable outside is a standpoint that could certify perception, custom, sympathy, law, and authority without using the same human operations it judges.
The missing common measure is a single scale aligning intensity, conviction, truth, welfare, title, merit, public utility, and legitimacy.
